## Chapter 1 — פרק 1 (Milchamot ha-Shem 1:1–1:13)

### Reading text

<sup>1:1</sup> The Author's Introduction.

<sup>1:2</sup> Let the enlightened man reflect, and let him who fears and trembles at the word of the LORD lament over the state of the people of Israel, upon seeing that every people and each people, of all the divisions of the nations, cherish their tongue and magnify their language, in which they were educated. And in it their faith and their religion were engraved, each man in his own tongue. And we, the people of Israel, since the time that we were exiled from our land, have abandoned our holy tongue, in which the first Adam spoke and in which our holy Torah was given, when His glory, may He be blessed, was revealed on Mount Sinai, and He said to His people, “I am the LORD your God,” etc., and we have not done as we were commanded, and you shall teach them to your children, to speak of them. And as Rashi of blessed memory explained in Parashat Ekev, “from here they said: ‘When the child begins to speak, his father speaks with him in the holy tongue and teaches him Torah.’” Thus far his words, but all our conversation with our children is in the language of the people among whom we dwell, and most of the children’s teachers too, are not able to speak all their needs in the holy tongue, even though they know it, for they have not tried these, and there are no systems for teaching the children of the elementary school. It is known and famous, the compassion of the father for his sons, and how many toils and exertions the parents exert in raising their children. With abundant attention to all their children’s needs: his food and his drink, suited to him, his bedding, and his clothing! But when it comes to striving to bring him into school, he casts him off with a teacher of children, in narrow and dark houses, on remnants of mats on the ground, without cleanliness, for the teacher does not clean the children’s abode, only from one festival to the next. And all day they sit crowded, without order, and breathe foul and musty air. And they drink salty water, and because of this, when some months pass since he was brought to school, growths and a bad boil come up on his head. And their fathers do not look after them to bring them clear, sweet water to drink, nor clean bedding to sit on, and on most days they sit on the ground without a mat! And in the period of the new era, from the year 5650 of the full count of creation, many of the enlightened were stirred and sought an organisation of the schools and an organisation of their children for the study of Torah and the study of the languages Hebrew, Arabic and Turkish, which are in use! And they strove to seat enlightened teachers versed in the Torah of the LORD, to manage the children of the school in moral upbringing and cleanliness of the place of learning, in bright houses and spacious windows in order to breathe fresh and clean air! And all the labour of those enlightened men came to nothing, and their plan did not come to fruition, and the children of the elementary school remained as they were, with a teacher, in dark and musty rooms, sitting in a crowd: this one learns the alef-bet, and this one learns Scripture, and this one learns with the Targum of Onkelos and the translation of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic, without understanding. Also the very smallest, who are not at all fit to learn, like a child of two and three years, are brought there. And many times the child relieves himself there. And the teacher sends to his mother that she should come and wipe her son’s excrement! And at the call of the one who calls in the newspapers in those days, from Mr. Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, for the revival of the holy Hebrew language, our soul yearned only in words and mere conversations, and it did not come to realization until the year 5670, when our exalted government, the government of Turkey, then deigned to open schools for the children of Israel, and there was made there a fine organisation for the children of Israel, in spacious upper rooms with open windows, and bedding of wool, and curtains of goat-hair, and also tables for the older children to learn and to write on them! Then we said: behold, the time has come to bring out Ashtonot Ish Yerushalayim, may it be rebuilt and established, which, before she travailed, bore the great man in the revival of the Hebrew language, namely Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, and we acknowledge our debt to him for what he did and made, and with all his strength he toiled for the good of the people of Israel and the settlement of the land of Israel and the revival of the Hebrew language; this holy work he performed with wondrous alacrity and diligence; he did, and succeeded in raising it from the dust, and after its wearing out it had delight, and because of his love for the holy tongue its wrinkles were smoothed out, and the appearance of its face budded and blossomed, and it found grace and honour in the eyes of its seekers, its knowers, and its acquaintances, and they awoke from their sleep to gird up their senses, to widen it and to enrich it as in the days of its youth, before the exile of the people of Israel! And because of this mitzvah, may his soul be bound up in the bundle of life with the LORD our God, and from the fruit of his labour may his soul be satisfied in Eden, the garden of God!

<sup>1:3</sup> From the time the government opened the school, the children were studying Scripture and its translations, Onkelos and Rabbi Saadia Gaon, Mishnah and the Rambam, and grammar and the explanation of the words, all was done properly the study of the Torah, Prophets and Writings with clear explanation, a grammar book of the Holy Tongue! and the study of the Turkish language through the Turkish teacher, upright of heart, Chafetz Effendi. And after him Zia Bey with wonderful diligence! and we accustomed them to speak one with another in Hebrew and in Turkish, so that they would be well accustomed in their mouths, and at the turn of the year the examiners came from the government, may his majesty be exalted, and the children arranged their studies in Turkish and they showed them their writing, and the examiners saw their talents on display in their studies, and they praised them, that they are educated! Also the Hebrew examiners came on the day after and the children arranged their studies before them in Hebrew and in Arabic, and they found favour in their eyes for the ability of their studies, and praised them! And the following year the children did so, studying with diligence and alacrity, and at the end of the year the Turkish examiners came and examined them with uprightness of heart, and praised them, that they were making progress in their studies, and urged them with words and blessed them! But as for the Hebrew examiners who came after them, there had already begun to flare up among them the hatred of enlightenment and of the study of languages. And they began to provoke them and to ask them about what they had not yet studied, and whoever could not answer anything, in any place where they asked him as is due to a complete sage, was counted by them as nothing at all. In order to diminish their honour, to sadden them and to slacken their hands from the studies, and they sought faults and blemishes in each and every one, and out of malice they did not turn to the studies and the knowledge that the children had acquired. Only to trip them up over what they had not yet studied, and to question them on the order of Nezikin, while they were still at the order of Moed, and when they showed them the beauty of their writing, the splendid and orderly Ashuri script, they sought a fault in the joining, as fine as a hair's thread, in some of the letters, as if they were writing Torah scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot. And they did not look at the beauty of the script and its order. And in the interpretation of the verses they asked them to solve for them difficult verses, such as "Binding his foal to the vine", and the like, and they went out from before them in low spirits, good, grieved, sad and with limp hands.

<sup>1:4</sup> And at the turn of the third year the war broke out against the good studies and the pleasant arrangements, as we are commanded by our Rabbis of blessed memory. The opponents spread an evil slander, saying that through this the children have gone out, God forbid, into bad ways, and many of the fools believed their lies and took their children out of the school. Also the foolish boys who had gone out of the school are hostile toward their teachers, because in their humble opinion they are heretics and stand outside the community. But those of understanding among them know and recognise that a lie is in the right hand of those who spread this evil slander, and they were greatly distressed that their fathers had taken them out of school in their folly! And when they had led many astray, the hand of the benighted grew strong and by false informing they informed against the teachers before the government, that they wished to incite the inhabitants of the land to rebel. And they informed that they were writers of libel against the government, to the government of England, to shelter in its shadow, and also to H.N.Ts. And because of this informing the teachers were led to prison, and also expelled from the school. And they brought in their place another teacher, who knew neither Hebrew thoroughly nor Arabic as it should be. And he had no duty to teach them except the weekly portion, with the Targum of Onkelos and the Targum of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic. And he was to teach them the Haftarah with the Targum of Jonathan in Aramaic, with no understanding at all, like the other teachers! And after some days the school closed entirely! All this came upon us because we did not object, for the honour of our Creator, when we were hearing from those who study the Zohar and other Kabbalists, things that are forbidden to hear, and we were silent before them as our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "R. A. was seized for heresy, etc.; perhaps a word of heresy, etc." and there was fulfilled in us the saying of our Rabbis of blessed memory: "Whoever concedes to them falls into their hands; whoever relies on them, what is his is theirs." Thus far! Therefore we abandoned our way of studying the languages, Hebrew and Arabic, in their grammar, against our will, because of the wrath of the oppressor, through false informing, and we turned to the path of holiness, to the honour of our Father who is in heaven, in the nullification of the opinions of the philosopher, the false prophet, the author of the Zohar, who gathered into his hands the opinions of ancient philosophy, the worshippers of idols, images and hidden powers, which they had invented from their own heart. And the author of the Zohar seized their opinions, and thought to bring them into the faith of our holy Torah, and falsely called his name by the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, and said that the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called by him Atika Kadisha, was revealed to him and revealed to him hidden mysteries. And he hung his prophecy and his ideas on Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, peace be upon him. And he made his composition, the Zohar, and said that the higher ones agreed to his composition, because this philosopher saw that the Mishnah, the two Talmuds and the true midrashim of our Rabbis of blessed memory stood against him in the belief in His oneness, may He be blessed, therefore he thought to disqualify them, and he despised and mocked them and all who occupy themselves with them, and he called them by names of contempt and abasement, as the reader will see within! And he promised that Israel would not merit redemption until they turned from their way of occupying themselves with the Mishnah and the Talmud. Let them occupy themselves only with his new Torah, full of idols of images and faces of monstrous form, and various couplings. And by cunning and deceit they buried it in a chest in the ground, so that it would grow old and begin to rot; after some time they published it and brought it out through a king from among the kings of the idolaters (as Rabbi Chida wrote in his book Shem ha-Gedolim, in the section on books), as if it were an ancient composition of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna. And many of our later rabbis were drawn after the aforementioned philosopher with eyes shut, for he took them with the smoothness of his lips and his trimmings, and they did not give heed to his lies! Heaven forbid that any Jew should believe that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna or another of our Rabbis of blessed memory believed in such beliefs to exchange and replace the LORD our God, who made known His ways to Moses and His deeds to the children of Israel, for "He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in kindness," etc. for a strange god, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), and to conjoin and associate with Him five partzufim whose existence has not been established even by proof (Rabbi Ovadiah Sforno, Deuteronomy 13:3; and there 29:25; and see there 28:14) and to call them by the name of the LORD our God, and the LORD, the God of truth, whose existence has been established by many proofs, strong as a cast mirror, as Rabbi Saadia Gaon wrote in Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Rabbi, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and the Rambam in Moreh Nevukhim and in the Yad, let us abandon Him and leave Him, and say that He has no name and no appellation, and let us worship the partzufim and the forms which, according to his words, were created and descended from Him! And we have already expounded at length within, with clear proofs from our Rabbis of blessed memory, on the nullification of these strange opinions of the philosopher, the false prophet, the aforementioned! For it is the aim of our holy Torah to distance us from belief in idols, whether corporeal or spiritual. And its aim is to know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him. And He has neither father nor brother nor son (Rabbah, parashat Yitro), and did not receive His kingship from another and is not destined to hand it on to another, as our Rabbis of blessed memory explained (Rabbah, Bamidbar; Shir ha-Shirim, parashah 1; Yerushalmi, Sanhedrin, chapter Dinei Mamonot) on the verse "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God," and on what Nebuchadnezzar said: "and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods!" And I have seen Rabbi Menachem di Lonzano, in the book Derekh ha-Chayyim, who opened his mouth wide to speak error about the holy pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, concerning his saying, in the name of the philosopher, that one could not worship the Cause of causes, except the prophet of the generation by his nature, or the outstanding philosopher in what he acquired from wisdom; but others worship other than Him, because they do not understand: the result is only composite! And at these words of the pietist he was angered and thought that here was ground for complaint against him, and found a pretext to mislead the listeners and alarm them by saying: "Is it so that such-and-such and such-and-such of our later famous sages worship other than Him?" And he counted them, in his language, one by one by name. And he did not take to heart that many of the sages whom he counted went along with eyes shut and believed the words of the author of the Zohar who called himself by the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, in order to attach his false prophecies to the name of the Tanna, and spoke rebellion against the LORD our God, who was revealed to him in his study house as Atika Kadisha, and revealed to him hidden secrets and hidden powers (Zohar, Bereshit 22), for the Creator is the idol called Abba, who used to command his consort, the she-idol Imma, and she does all that he says to her, except for the creation of the first man: it was she, Imma, who said and made the first man, not with the will of Abba! And in Parashat Vayera, folio 112, and likewise in Parashat Balak, folio 191, he ascribes our worship and our prayers to a strange god, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), who did not make the heavens and the earth. And he calls these idols by the name of the LORD our God. And about Ze'ir Anpin, Jeremiah the prophet, peace be upon him, proclaimed "Thus shall you say to them: the gods that did not make the heavens and the earth shall perish from the earth and from under these heavens." For it is clear in many places in the Zohar that he is created, not creator (see Zohar, Bereshit 22; and Yosher Levav, folio 3b). And yet he says to worship him, and to bless him, and to accept him as God, and to fear his consort! And many of our later rabbis, whom he mentioned in the book Derekh ha-Chayyim, in his amazement at the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, went along with eyes shut and were drawn after him and believed his belief and accepted upon themselves the idol, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), as God! And all this came upon them because they did not contemplate the wisdom of the Creator of all, which is to investigate and examine the works of Creation as explained in the words of the Rabbi, the author of Moreh Nevukhim, and in the words of the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and our master Saadia Gaon and Rabbi Yehudah Halevi in the Kuzari, as the prophet, peace be upon him, said: "They do not regard the deed of the LORD." For they thought their words were Greek wisdom, and they kept far from it, as far as a bow-shot, and they also did not take to heart the true words of our forefathers of blessed memory in the midrashim that Abraham our father did not recognise his Creator except by contemplating the work of the LORD, and investigated and expounded them and brought proofs from them until he attained the truth; then the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed to him and said to him: "You love righteousness and hate wickedness," etc. A parable: to one walking on the road who saw a castle, etc. (Midrash ha-Gadol, at the beginning of Parashat Lekh Lekha). And perforce we acknowledge the truth that the words of the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, clearly say that one cannot worship the God of truth except, etc. but others worship other than Him, as the prophet said: "For many days Israel was without a true God," and as our eyes see and our ears hear, to the point that a man can say to his fellow! "Your people is my people, and your God is not my God!" And to the God of truth let us pour out our prayer, to guide us on paths of uprightness, and to deliver us from every strange belief. Amen, may it be His will.

<sup>1:5</sup> And I named the book The Wars of the LORD for His unity, because the philosopher, the author of the book the Zohar, spoiled for us the truth of the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, and several rabbis and great men of the Torah followed him with eyes shut. And of them Solomon said in his wisdom: "For she has cast down many slain, and mighty are all her slain." As our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded (Sanhedrin, the Rif): "For she has cast down many slain" this is a student who has not reached instruction and teaches, (as we see with our own eyes how many authors who bring an elephant through the eye of a needle, from the scantness of their expertise) "and mighty are all her slain" this is a student who has reached instruction and does not teach (who does not set his mind to teach others correctly; "mighty" is the word of "and he shuts his eyes", Rashi of blessed memory). And all the more so, if he entices others to occupy themselves with the external book, the book of the Zohar, and does not set his mind to understand the contradiction, but walks with the eye of reason shut, and makes others stumble in a false faith, of whom it is said, "and mighty are all her slain"; and transgresses against "and before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block"; and error in study counts as wilful sin, and he sins and causes the many to sin, and the sin of the many hangs on him.

<sup>1:6</sup> And concerning this external faith of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar, our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded (Yalkut, Parashat Kedoshim, and the Midrash ha-Gadol there, and the Rambam in Sefer ha-Mitzvot, negative commandment 10): "Do not turn to the idols, and the gods of; if you turn to others (to honor them, Sforno), your end is to make them divinities." Thus far. And so it befell the faith of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar, for the early students who learned from it, thinking that it was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna's, they thought to make sense of his words; and to call the partzufim vessels, and they esteemed them and honored them, and those who came after them made them divinities, according to the thought of the philosopher, the author, and accepted them upon themselves as divinities, as will be explained within. And likewise our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded in the verse: wine and strong drink you shall not drink, and these are his words: "Rabbi Chiya opened: 'The precepts of the LORD are right'; and it is written of wine: 'it goes down smoothly'; and it is written: 'rejoicing the heart'; and it is written: 'and wine gladdens the heart of man.' Just as this wine gladdens the heart, so the words of Torah gladden the heart; just as this wine, one who drinks of it more than his need in the end vomits everything; so the words of Torah, one who occupies himself with them and thinks about them too much, in the end he goes out into heresy." Thus far. (Midrash ha-Gadol, Parashat Shemini, verse 'wine and strong drink'). In this way did the philosopher, the false prophet, the author of the Zohar, act, to follow after his heart, to think about the words of Torah too much, in paths far from the truth, and very far from the rules that the Sages received, a man from the mouth of a man, by which the Torah is expounded, and these are the thirteen rules of Rabbi Ishmael and the thirty-three rules of Rabbi Yose the Galilean, for the Aggadah, as the discerning, attentive reader will see; and he enticed and seduced the sages, the upright of heart, who walk in their simplicity, to believe him in his lies: that there was revealed to him the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called by him the Elder of Elders, and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and Elijah, and they revealed to him secrets of heresy, which it is forbidden to think about them, even in the lavatory; and he promised one who occupies himself with his Torah without understanding, a reward greater than the essentials of the Torah, in order to blind the eyes of the sages and to stop up the way of study in his words so as not to understand his machinations, and to magnify the merit of those who occupy themselves with his new Torah, full of idols different in their essences and their activities, without being particular about the addition and multiplicity, in our God, the Unique, above all other ones; and do not take note how the Torah was strict about 'you shall not add', whether in tefillin, or in a mezuzah, or in the four species of the lulav, and likewise in the other commandments, even though he puts five sections in one hide and he joins them to be one, and likewise, if he adds one section to a mezuzah, even though parchment joins them to be one, we do not say 'as though it were not one'; and likewise in tzitzit, and in the bundle of four species, if he added a fifth species to the bundle, it is disqualified; and we do not say 'as though it were not one'.

<sup>1:7</sup> All the more so, a fortiori, regarding our God, blessed be He, and blessed be His name, that the Torah insisted that one should not attach to Him or associate with Him anything of all created things, whether corporeal or spiritual, as it is said: "He who sacrifices to the gods shall be destroyed, save to the LORD alone." And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever associates the name of Heaven with something else is uprooted from the world." And we should not say that He is one as the others are one, since the Torah has made clear plainly in many places that He is one, unique, apart from all the other ones. Thus, you who mention the LORD, do not stay silent about making known His oneness, may He be blessed, to your children and your disciples, as you are commanded.

<sup>1:8</sup> Because the beginning of this composition was made at first by the question of one student: whom shall we worship? Therefore I placed at its opening the question of the student, and its reply from one of the learners who persisted the first, second and third time.

<sup>1:9</sup> The humble Yichya, son of Sali' al-Kafich, may his Rock keep him and give him life.

<sup>1:10</sup> The Publisher's Introduction.

<sup>1:11</sup> The book The Wars of the LORD makes known the way of the truths of His unity, may He be blessed, according to the Torah and its interpreters, our Rabbis of blessed memory, in the Mishnah, in the Talmud, Bavli and Yerushalmi, and the Midrashim of our Rabbis of blessed memory, and in accordance with the view of the Geonim, Rabbi Saadia Gaon, and Rabbeinu Bachya in Chovot ha-Levavot, and Rabbi Yehuda Halevi in his poems, and in the Kuzari, the Rambam, the Semag (Sefer Mitzvot Gadol) and the author of the Ikkarim, of blessed memory, and as is accepted by every Jew. In it is a severe warning not to worship any created thing, in accordance with the tradition of all our prophets and all our sages, the Tannaim, the Amoraim, the Geonim and the early decisors, from the mouth of Moses, Aaron and the elders, not to deviate from them and not to add to them.

<sup>1:12</sup> Know, esteemed reader, that you will not grasp the intention of this book, unless you read and study all of it, for its author made nights as days, and labored and scrutinized many books, and drew from seas and rivers proofs strong as a cast mirror, and the matters did not come from his own opinion. Therefore I ask you, esteemed reader, that you not come with the fist of Esau, in mockery, but with the voice of Jacob, and to consider the matters, and whoever is lacking in strength, let him be silent from speech and be still, and may El Shaddai give you mercy, and the merit of the author will protect us, and upon all His people Israel.

<sup>1:13</sup> The publisher

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 1:2

> יתבונן המשכיל ויתאונן הירא והחרד אל דבר ה', על מצב עם בני ישראל בראותו אשר כל עם ועם מכל מפלגות הגוים מחבבים את לשונם ומגדילים את שפתם אשר חנכו עליה. ואשר הוחקה בה אמונתם ודתם איש ללשונו ואנחנו עם בני ישראל מעת אשר גלינו מארצנו עזבנו את לשונינו הקדושה אשר דבר בה אדם הראשון ובה ניתנה תורתינו הקדושה בהגלות כבודו ית' על הר סיני ואמר לעמו אנכי ה' אלהיך וכו' ולא עשינו כמצווה עלינו ולמדתם אותם את בניכם לדבר בם. וכמו שפי' רש״י ז״ל בפרשת עקב שמכאן אמרו כשהתינוק מתחיל לדבר אביו משיח עמו בלשון הקדש ומלמדו תורה עכ״ל, רק כל שיחתנו עם בנינו בלשון העם אשר אנו יושבים בקרבם ומלמדי תינוקות גם הם רובם לא יכינו לדבר כל צרכם בלשון הקדש אף שיודעים אותו כי לא נסו באלה ואין סדרים ללמוד תינוקות של בית רבן. וידוע הוא ומפורסם חמלת האב על בניו וכמה טרחות ויגיעות ייגעו ההורים בגידול בניהם. עם רוב השקפתם על כל צרכי ילדיהם במאכלו ומשקיו הניאותים לו ומצעו ומלבושו! אך כאשר הגיע חתור להכניסו לבית הספר ישליכהו אצל מלמד תינוקות בבתים צרים וחשוכים על שיירי מחצלאות על הארץ בלי נקיון כי לא ינקה המלמד את מעון התינוקות רק מרגל לרגל אחר. וכל היום יושבים צפופים בלי סדרים ושואפים אויר סרוח ומעופש. ושותים מים מלוחים ובגלל זה כאשר יעברו איזה חדשים מעת שהובא אל בית הספר יעלו בראשו צמחים ושחין רע. ואבותיהם לא ישגיחו עליהם להביא להם מים צלולים ומתוקים לשתות ולא מצע נקי לישב עליו וברוב הימים יושבים על האדמה מאין מחצלת! ובתקופת העת החדשה משנת התר״ן לפרט גדול ליצירה התעוררו רבים מהמשכילים ויבקשו הסתדרות בתי הספר והסתדרות ילדיו לתלמוד תורה ולימוד השפות העברית והערבית והתורקית המתהלכות! וחתרו להושיב מלמדים משכילים בתורת ה' לנהל את ילדי בית הספר בחנוך מוסרי ובנקיון מעון התלמוד בבתים מאירים ובחלונות מרווחים כדי לשאוף רוח צח ונקי! וכל יגיעם של המשכילים ההם היה לריק ולא יצאה מחשבתם לפועל ותינוקות של בית רבן נשארו כשהיו אצל מלמד בחדרים חשוכים ומעופשים יושבים ברבוביא זה לומד אלפא ביתא וזה לומד מקרא וזה לומד עם תרגום אונקלוס ותרגום רס״ג בערבי בלי הבין. גם קטני קטנים שאין ראוים ללמוד כלל כבן שתים ושלש שנים מביאים שם. ופעמים רבות התינוק נפנה שם. והמלמד שולח לאמו שתבוא ותקנח צואת בנה! ולקול הקורא במכתבי עתים בימים ההם מאת ה' אליעזר בן יהודה לתחית השפה העברית הקדושה נכספה נפשינו אך ורק בדברים ושיחות בעלמא ולא באה לידי התגשמות עד שנת תר״ע, אשר אז הואילה ממשלתינו הרוממה ממשלת תוגרמה לפתוח בתי ספר לילדי בני ישראל, ונעשה שם הסתדרות יפה לילדי בני ישראל בעליות מרווחים וחלונות פתוחים ומצעות של צמר, ויריעות עזים וגם שולחנות לילדים גדולים ללמוד ולכתוב עליהם! ואז אמרנו הנה בא העת להוציא לאור עשתונות איש ירושלים ת״ו, אשר בטרם תחיל ילדה האדם הגדול בתחית השפה העברית הוא ניהו אליעזר בן יהודה, ואפריין נמטיה על אשר פעל ועשה ובכל כחו עמל לטובת עם ישראל וישוב ארץ ישראל ותחית השפה העברית ועבודת הקדש הלזו עבד בזריזות וחריצות נפלאה ועשה והצליח להקימה מעפר, ואחרי בלותה היתה לה עדנה, ובגלל אהבתו לשפה הקדושה נתפשטו קמטיה, ותואר פניה הציץ ופרח, ותמצא חן וכבוד בעיני שוחריה יודעיה ומכיריה ויעורו משנתם להחלץ חושים להרחיבה ולהעשירה כבימי נעוריה לפני גלות עם ישראל! ובגלל מצוה זו תהי נפשו צרורה בצרור החיים את ה' אלהינו ומפרי עמלו תשבע נפשו בעדן גן אלהים!

**Let the enlightened man reflect, and let him who fears and trembles at the word of the LORD lament over the state of the people of Israel, upon seeing that every people and each people, of all the divisions of the nations, cherish their tongue and magnify their language, in which they were educated. And in it their faith and their religion were engraved, each man in his own tongue. And we, the people of Israel, since the time that we were exiled from our land, have abandoned our holy tongue, in which the first Adam spoke and in which our holy Torah was given, when His glory, may He be blessed, was revealed on Mount Sinai, and He said to His people, “I am the LORD your God,” etc., and we have not done as we were commanded, and you shall teach them to your children, to speak of them. And as Rashi of blessed memory explained in Parashat Ekev, “from here they said: ‘When the child begins to speak, his father speaks with him in the holy tongue and teaches him Torah.’” Thus far his words, but all our conversation with our children is in the language of the people among whom we dwell, and most of the children’s teachers too, are not able to speak all their needs in the holy tongue, even though they know it, for they have not tried these, and there are no systems for teaching the children of the elementary school. It is known and famous, the compassion of the father for his sons, and how many toils and exertions the parents exert in raising their children. With abundant attention to all their children’s needs: his food and his drink, suited to him, his bedding, and his clothing! But when it comes to striving to bring him into school, he casts him off with a teacher of children, in narrow and dark houses, on remnants of mats on the ground, without cleanliness, for the teacher does not clean the children’s abode, only from one festival to the next. And all day they sit crowded, without order, and breathe foul and musty air. And they drink salty water, and because of this, when some months pass since he was brought to school, growths and a bad boil come up on his head. And their fathers do not look after them to bring them clear, sweet water to drink, nor clean bedding to sit on, and on most days they sit on the ground without a mat! And in the period of the new era, from the year 5650 of the full count of creation, many of the enlightened were stirred and sought an organisation of the schools and an organisation of their children for the study of Torah and the study of the languages Hebrew, Arabic and Turkish, which are in use! And they strove to seat enlightened teachers versed in the Torah of the LORD, to manage the children of the school in moral upbringing and cleanliness of the place of learning, in bright houses and spacious windows in order to breathe fresh and clean air! And all the labour of those enlightened men came to nothing, and their plan did not come to fruition, and the children of the elementary school remained as they were, with a teacher, in dark and musty rooms, sitting in a crowd: this one learns the alef-bet, and this one learns Scripture, and this one learns with the Targum of Onkelos and the translation of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic, without understanding. Also the very smallest, who are not at all fit to learn, like a child of two and three years, are brought there. And many times the child relieves himself there. And the teacher sends to his mother that she should come and wipe her son’s excrement! And at the call of the one who calls in the newspapers in those days, from Mr. Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, for the revival of the holy Hebrew language, our soul yearned only in words and mere conversations, and it did not come to realization until the year 5670, when our exalted government, the government of Turkey, then deigned to open schools for the children of Israel, and there was made there a fine organisation for the children of Israel, in spacious upper rooms with open windows, and bedding of wool, and curtains of goat-hair, and also tables for the older children to learn and to write on them! Then we said: behold, the time has come to bring out Ashtonot Ish Yerushalayim, may it be rebuilt and established, which, before she travailed, bore the great man in the revival of the Hebrew language, namely Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, and we acknowledge our debt to him for what he did and made, and with all his strength he toiled for the good of the people of Israel and the settlement of the land of Israel and the revival of the Hebrew language; this holy work he performed with wondrous alacrity and diligence; he did, and succeeded in raising it from the dust, and after its wearing out it had delight, and because of his love for the holy tongue its wrinkles were smoothed out, and the appearance of its face budded and blossomed, and it found grace and honour in the eyes of its seekers, its knowers, and its acquaintances, and they awoke from their sleep to gird up their senses, to widen it and to enrich it as in the days of its youth, before the exile of the people of Israel! And because of this mitzvah, may his soul be bound up in the bundle of life with the LORD our God, and from the fruit of his labour may his soul be satisfied in Eden, the garden of God!**

Grammar:

- יתבונן and ויתאונן are jussives (hitpa'el): 'let him reflect' and 'and let him lament', a wish addressed to the enlightened and the fearful, not a plain report.
- בראותו is a construct infinitive with a pronominal suffix, 'upon his seeing'; the clause that follows, אשר כל עם ועם ..., states what he sees.
- Rashi's quotation runs from כשהתינוק to תורה, introduced by שמכאן אמרו ('from here they said') and closed by עכ״ל. The words before it are the author's own.
- ולמדתם אותם את בניכם לדבר בם is Deut 11:19 in the second person plural, embedded in the first person plural of ולא עשינו: the author speaks for the community, and the verse's 'you' is the people it addresses.
- חתור in הגיע חתור להכניסו is the infinitive of חתר, 'to strive'; the clause is 'when it comes to striving to bring him in'.
- מרגל לרגל: רגל here is a festival (the three pilgrim festivals), so 'from festival to festival', i.e. rarely.

Note: This paragraph is in the author's own voice (the publisher's voice begins at 1:10). The Hebrew full stops are kept as the English sentence breaks, and the long periods are divided into sentences without dropping a clause.

Other readings:

- ויתאונן הירא והחרד אל דבר ה: and let the fearful and trembling man lament over the word of the LORD (grammar). אל דבר ה' read with ויתאונן; the English takes it with הירא והחרד (cf. Isa 66:2).
- אך כאשר הגיע חתור להכניסו: But when he comes, eager to bring him (grammar). חתור read as an adjective of the subject (not the infinitive); the English reads the infinitive.

Ancient Near East:

- Eliezer Ben-Yehuda (1858-1922) led the revival of Hebrew as a spoken language, in Jerusalem.
- Beit rabban, 'house of the master', was the traditional elementary school; the author says children there learned the alphabet and Scripture with a translation, without understanding it.

Apparatus:

- Deut 11:19, 'ולמדתם אותם את בניכם לדבר בם', embedded without quotation marks (tokens 75-80).
- Exod 20:2, 'אנכי ה' אלהיך', the opening of the Decalogue, introduced by ואמר and cut off by the author's וכו' ('etc.'), so the English quotes it and keeps 'etc.'.
- Cf. Isa 66:2, 'וחרד על דברי', and Ezra 9:4: 'the one who fears and trembles at the word of the LORD' (tokens 4-8).
- Cf. Isa 40:3, 'קול קורא': 'ולקול הקורא' (tokens 363-364).
- Isa 66:7, 'בטרם תחיל ילדה': 'before she travailed she bore' (tokens 440-442).
- 1 Sam 2:8, 'מקים מעפר דל' (cf. 'להקימה מעפר'); Gen 18:12, 'אחרי בלתי היתה לי עדנה' (tokens 482-486); Isa 27:6, 'יציץ ופרח ישראל' (tokens 495-496); Exod 26:7, 'יריעות עזים' (tokens 418-419).
- 1 Sam 25:29, 'צרורה בצרור החיים את ה' אלהיך' ('the bundle of life'), with the author's אלהינו for אלהיך.
- Ezek 28:13, 'בעדן גן אלהים' ('in Eden, the garden of God'), the author's last words exactly.
- The Rashi reference is the author's: 'בפרשת עקב' (Parashat Ekev); no verse is given.
- Dates: 5650 is about 1889-1890 and 5670 is about 1909-1910 of the civil calendar; the text gives no civil year.
- Wikisource text: no collation with the 1931 scan has been made, so any Wikisource addition is translated as base text (Q2).

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 1:3

> ומעת אשר פתחה הממשלה את בית הספר היו הילדים לומדים מקרא ותרגומיו אונקלוס ורס״ג, משנה והרמב״ם, ודקדוק ופי' המלות, הכל נעשה על נכון לימוד התורה נביאים וכתובים בפי' ברור ספר דקדוק לשון הקדש! ולימוד השפה התורקית על ידי המלמד התורקי ישר הלבב חאפץ אפנדי. ואחריו זיא ביי בחריצות נפלאה! והרגלנום לדבר זה עם זה בשפה העברית והתורקית כדי שיהיו מורגלים בפיהם היטב, ולתקופת השנה באו הבוחנים מאת הממשלה יר״ה והסדירו הילדים את לימודם בשפה התורקית והראו להם כתיבתם ויראו הבוחנים את כשרונותם מתנוססת בלימודים, ויהללו אותם כי משכילים הם! גם הבוחנים העברים באו ביום של אחריו והסדירו הילדים לפניהם את לימודיהם בעברית ובערבית וימצאו חן בעיניהם בכשרון לימודיהם ויהללו אותם! ולשנה האחרת כן עשו הילדים ללמוד בחריצות וזריזות, ובצאת השנה באו הבוחנים התורקים ובחנו אותם ביושר לבב, ושיבחו אותם שהם עושים חיל בלימודים, וזירזו אותם בדברים ובירכו אותם! אך הבוחנים העברים הבאים אחריהם כבר התחילה להתנוצץ בקרבם שנאת ההשכלה ולימוד שפות. והתחילו לקנתרם ולשאול אותם במה שעדיין לא למדו, וכל שאינו יכול להשיב דבר בכל מקום ששואלין אותו כדין חכם גמור לא נחשב בעיניהם למאומה. כדי להפחית כבודם ולהעציבם ולהרפות ידיהם מן הלימודים ויבקשו חסרונות ומומים לכל אחד ואחד, ומרוע לב לא פנו אל הלמודים והידיעות שרכשו הילדים. רק לקפחם במה שעדיין לא למדו, ולשאול אותם בסדר נזיקים ועדיין עומדים בסדר מועד, ובהראות להם את יופי כתיבתם כתב אשורי מפואר ומסודר בקשו להם חסרון בדיבוק כחוט השערה בקצת אותיות כאלו הם כותבים סתו״מ. ולא הביטו ליופי הכתב וסדורו. ובפתרון הכתובים בקשו מהם לפתור להם מקראות חמורים כגון אסרי לגפן עירה, וכיוצא ויצאו מלפניהם בפחי נפש טובים דוים ועצבים ורפויי ידים.

**From the time the government opened the school, the children were studying Scripture and its translations, Onkelos and Rabbi Saadia Gaon, Mishnah and the Rambam, and grammar and the explanation of the words, all was done properly the study of the Torah, Prophets and Writings with clear explanation, a grammar book of the Holy Tongue! and the study of the Turkish language through the Turkish teacher, upright of heart, Chafetz Effendi. And after him Zia Bey with wonderful diligence! and we accustomed them to speak one with another in Hebrew and in Turkish, so that they would be well accustomed in their mouths, and at the turn of the year the examiners came from the government, may his majesty be exalted, and the children arranged their studies in Turkish and they showed them their writing, and the examiners saw their talents on display in their studies, and they praised them, that they are educated! Also the Hebrew examiners came on the day after and the children arranged their studies before them in Hebrew and in Arabic, and they found favour in their eyes for the ability of their studies, and praised them! And the following year the children did so, studying with diligence and alacrity, and at the end of the year the Turkish examiners came and examined them with uprightness of heart, and praised them, that they were making progress in their studies, and urged them with words and blessed them! But as for the Hebrew examiners who came after them, there had already begun to flare up among them the hatred of enlightenment and of the study of languages. And they began to provoke them and to ask them about what they had not yet studied, and whoever could not answer anything, in any place where they asked him as is due to a complete sage, was counted by them as nothing at all. In order to diminish their honour, to sadden them and to slacken their hands from the studies, and they sought faults and blemishes in each and every one, and out of malice they did not turn to the studies and the knowledge that the children had acquired. Only to trip them up over what they had not yet studied, and to question them on the order of Nezikin, while they were still at the order of Moed, and when they showed them the beauty of their writing, the splendid and orderly Ashuri script, they sought a fault in the joining, as fine as a hair's thread, in some of the letters, as if they were writing Torah scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot. And they did not look at the beauty of the script and its order. And in the interpretation of the verses they asked them to solve for them difficult verses, such as "Binding his foal to the vine", and the like, and they went out from before them in low spirits, good, grieved, sad and with limp hands.**

Grammar:

- The paragraph is a chain of clauses joined by ו and by the time phrases that open each school year: ולתקופת השנה (3:63), ולשנה האחרת (3:111), ובצאת השנה (3:119). The sentence that begins with ומעת has its main verb in היו הילדים לומדים (3:8).
- והרגלנום לדבר זה עם זה (3:50) is a hif'il perfect with an object suffix; the purpose clause כדי שיהיו מורגלים בפיהם היטב (3:58) follows it.
- The sentence ואחריו זיא ביי בחריצות נפלאה! (3:45-3:49) has no verb, and the English adds none beyond the words.
- The turn to hostility comes at אך (3:139): the Hebrew examiners who came after them are set against the Turkish examiners, and the verb התחילה (3:145) starts the change. The purpose clause כדי להפחית כבודם (3:176) states the aim.
- The phrase אסרי לגפן עירה (3:248-3:250) is quoted as an example of a hard verse, so the English keeps quotation marks; the source is Gen 49:11.

Note: Translated from the Wikisource witness as base text. The paragraph is ironic in the author's framing: the examiners first praise the children, then the Hebrew examiners set out to shame them. משכילים and ההשכלה are rendered in neutral terms; see the token notes.

Ancient Near East:

- The government (הממשלה), its examiners, its teacher and its language are called Turkish (התורקים, התורקית). The text names no place and no date for the school.

Apparatus:

- Witness spelling הלמודים (1:3.195) is read as the evident word הלימודים.
- Bible verse: Gen 49:11, 'Binding his foal to the vine' (אסרי לגפן עירה), quoted as an example of a hard verse (1:3.248-1:3.250).
- The abbreviation סתו״מ (1:3.233) is expanded as ספרי תורה תפילין ומזוזות, 'Torah scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot' (1:3.233).
- Base text: the Wikisource witness, not yet collated against the 1931 scan (open question 2).

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 1:4

> ולתקופת השנה השלישית פרצה המלחמה נגד הלמודים הטובים והסדרים הנעימים כמצווה עלינו מרז״ל. ויוציאו המתנגדים דבה רעה לאמר כי על ידי זה יצאו הילדים ח״ו לתרבות רעה, והרבה מהטפשים האמינו לשקריהם והוציאו את ילדיהם מבית הספר. וגם הבנים הסכלים אשר יצאו מבית הספר עוינים את מוריהם כי לעניות דעתם הם מינים ויוצאים מן הכלל אך המשכילים שבהם יודעים ומכירים כי שקר בימין מוציאי הדבה הרעה הלזו, ודאגו מאד על שהוציאום אבותם מבית הספר בסכלותם! וכאשר התעו רבים חזקה יד החשכים ובמלשינות שקר הלשינו על המלמדים אצל הממשלה שהם חפצים להמריד את יושבי הארץ. ושהם כותבי פלסתר על הממשלה אל ממשלת אנגליא לחסות בצל ממשלתה וגם אל הינ״ץ ועבור זה המלשינות הובלו המלמדים אל בית הכלא וגם גורשו מבית הספר. והביאו תחתיהם מלמד אחר אשר לא ידע לא עברית על בריה ולא ערבית כתקנה. ואין עליו ללמדם רק פרשת השבוע עם תרגום אונקלוס ותרגום רס״ג בערבי. והפטרה עם תרגום יונתן ב״ע באין הבין כלום כשאר המלמדים! ולימים מספר בטל בית הספר לגמרי! כל זאת באתנו על אשר לא מחינו בכבוד קונינו בעת שהיינו שומעים מהלומדים בזהר ושאר מקובלים דברים שאסור לשמען ומחרישים להם כמו שאמרו רז״ל דר״א נתפש למינות וכו' שמא דבר מינות וכו' ונתקיים בנו מאמר רז״ל דמודי להון נפיל בידיהון דמתרחץ עליהון דיליה דילהון ע״כ! לכן עזבנו דרכינו בלימוד השפות העברית והערבית בדקדוקן על כורחנו מפני חמת המציק על ידי מלשינות שקר ונפן אל דרך הקדש כבוד אבינו שבשמים בבטול דעות הפילסוף נביא השקר מחבר הזהר אשר אסף בחפניו דעות הפלסופיא הקדומה עובדי האלילים תמונות וכוחות נעלמים אשר בדו מלבם. ומחבר הזהר תפס דעותיהם וחשב להכניסם באמונת תורתינו הקדושה, וקרא את שמו בשם רשב״י התנא בשקר ואמר שנגלה לו הקב״ה הנקרא אצלו עתיקא קדישא וגילה לו רזין טמירין. ותלה נבואתו ורעיונותיו ברשב״י התנא ע״ה. ועשה את חבורו הזהר ואמר שהעליונים הסכימו לחבורו לפי שראה הפילסוף הזה כי המשנה ושני התלמודים ומדרשי רז״ל האמתיים עומדים נגדו באמונת אחדותו ית' לכן חשב לפסלן ובזה ולעג להם ולכל העוסקים בהם, וכינה אותם בשמות של זלזול ופחיתות, כאשר יראה המעיין בפנים! והבטיח שלא יזכו ישראל לגאולה עד אשר ישובו מדרכם מלעסוק במשנה ובתלמוד. רק יעסקו בתורתו החדשה המלאה אלילי תמונות ופרצופים בעלי מפלצות וזווגים שונים. ובתחבולה ומרמה קברו בארון בקרקע עולם להתיישן ויתחיל להרקיב, אחר ימים פרסמו והוציאו ע״י מלך ממלכי העכו״מ (כמ״ש הר' חיד״א בספרו שם הגדולים במערכת ספרים) כאלו הוא חבור קדום מרשב״י התנא. והרבה מרבותינו האחרונים נמשכו אחר הפילסוף הנז' בעצימות עין כי לקח אותם בחלק שפתיו וגיזומיו, ולא שתו לב לכזביו! חלילה לשום בר ישראל להאמין כי רשב״י התנא או זולתו מרז״ל האמינו באמונות כאלה להחליף ולהמיר את ה' אלוהינו אשר הודיע דרכיו למשה לבני ישראל עלילותיו, כי חנון ורחום הוא ארך אפים ורב חסד וכו' באל זר קצר אפים (ז״א) ולצרף ולשתף עמו חמשה פרצופים אשר לא נתברר אפי' מציאותם במופת (ר' עובדיה ספורנו דברים י״ג ג'. ושם כ״ט כ״ה וע״ש כ״ח י״ד) ולקרותם בשם ה' אלהינו, ואת ה' אלהים אמת שנתבררה מציאותו בכמה מופתים כראי מוצק חזקים כמו שכ' הרס״ג בס' האמונות והדעות והר' בעל חובת הלבבות והרמב״ם במורה נבוכים וביד, נטוש ונעזוב ונאמר שאין לו שם ולא כנוי ונעבוד את הפרצופים והצורות אשר לפי דבריו נבראו ונשתלשלו ממנו! וכבר הארכנו בפנים בראיות נכוחות מרז״ל בביטול הדעות הזרות האלו של הפילסוף נביא השקר הנז'! כי הוא מטרת תורתינו הקדושה להרחיקנו מאמונת האלילים בין גשמיים בין רוחניים. ולדעת כי ה' הוא האלהים אין עוד מלבדו. ואין לו לא אב ולא אח ולא בן (רבה פרשת יתרו) ולא קיבל מלכותו מאחר ואינו עתיד למסרה לאחר כמו שביארו רבותינו ז״ל (רבה במדבר שיר השירים פרשה א' ירושלמי סנהדרין פרק דיני ממונות) על פסוק אני ראשון ואני אחרון ומבלעדי אין אלהים ועל מה שאמר נבוכדנצר וריויה די רביעאה דמי לבר אלהין! וראיתי להר' מנחם די לונזבנו בס' דרך החיים שהרחיב פיו לדבר תועה על החסיד הקדוש בעל חובת הלבבות על אמרו בשם הפילסוף שאמר שלא יוכל לעבוד עלת העלות רק נביא הדור בטבעו, או הפילסוף המובהק במה שקנהו מן החכמה אבל זולתם עובדים זולתו מפני שאינם מבינים נמצא אלא מורכב! ועל דברי החסיד האלו התקצף וחשב כי כאן מקום תלונה עליו ותואנה מצא להתעות השומעים ולהבהילם באמרו וכי פלוני ופלוני מחכמינו האחרונים המפורסמים עובדים זולתו? והוא ספרם בלשונו אחד אחד בשמותם. ולא שם אל לבו כי הרבה מהחכמים שַמָנָה הלכו בעצימות עינים והאמינו לדברי מחבר הזהר אשר כינה את עצמו בשם רשב״י התנא כדי לתלות נבואותיו השקריות בשמו של התנא, ודבר סרה על ה' אלהינו שנגלה לו בבית מדרשו עתיקא קדישא וגילה לו סודות נעלמים וכוחות נעלמות (זהר בראשית כ״ב) כי הבורא הוא האליל הנקרא אבא שהיה מצוה לזוגתו האלילה אימא והיא עושה כל אשר יאמר אליה חוץ מבריאת אדם הראשון שהיא אימא שאמרה ועשתה את אדם הראשון שלא ברצון אבא! ובפרשת וירא דף קי״ב וכן בפרשת בלק דף קצ״א מיחס עבודתינו ותפילותינו לאל זר קצר אפים (זעיר אנפין) אשר לא עשה את השמים ואת הארץ. וקורא הוא לעצבים הללו בשם ה' אלהינו. ועל זעיר אנפין קרא ירמיה הנביא ע״ה כדנה תימרון להום אלהיא די שמיא וארקא לא עבדו ייבדו מן ארעא ומן תחות שמיא אלה. שהרי מבואר בזהר בכמה מקומות שהוא נברא ולא בורא (עיין זהר בראשית כ״ב וביושר לבב דף ג' ע״ב) ועכ״ז הוא אומר לעבדו ולברכו ולקבלו עליו באלוה ולירא מזוגתו! והרבה מרבותינו האחרונים שהזכיר בספר דרך החיים בתמיהתו על החסיד בעל חובת הלבבות הלכו בעצימת עין ונמשכו אחריו והאמינו באמונתו וקיבלו האליל קצר אפים (ז״א) עליהם באלוה! וכל זה גרם להם על שלא התבוננו בחכמת יוצר הכל שהוא לחקור ולבחון במעשה בראשית המבוארים בדברי הר' מורה נבוכים ובדברי החסיד בעל חובת הלבבות. ורבינו סעדיה גאון ור״י הלוי בכוזרי כמו שאמר הנביא ע״ה ואת פעל ה' לא יביטו. כי חשבו דבריהם לחכמה יונית ורחקו ממנה הרחק כמטחוי קשת, וגם לא שמו אל לבם דברי אבותינו ז״ל האמתיים במדרשים שלא הכיר אברהם אבינו את בוראו אלא בהתבוננו בפעל ה' וחקר ודרש בהם והביא מופתים מהם עד שהשיג האמת ואז נגלה לו הקב״ה ואמר לו אהבת צדק ותשנא רשע וכו' משל לאחד שהיה מהלך בדרך וראה בירה וכו' (מדרש הגדול ריש פרשת לך לך) ועל כרחנו נודה על האמת שדברי החסיד בעל חובת הלבבות ברור מללו שלא יוכל לעבוד את אלהים אמת אלא וכו' אבל זולתם עובדים זולתו כמאמר הנביא וימים רבים לישראל ללא אלהי אמת, וכמו שעינינו רואות ואזנינו שומעות עד שאפשר שיאמר אדם לחבירו! עַמְּךָ עַמִּי וְאלֹהֶיך לֹא אֱלהָי! ואל אלהי אמת נשפוך שיחנו לנחותינו במעגלי יושר ולהצילנו מכל אמונה זרה אכי״ר.

**And at the turn of the third year the war broke out against the good studies and the pleasant arrangements, as we are commanded by our Rabbis of blessed memory. The opponents spread an evil slander, saying that through this the children have gone out, God forbid, into bad ways, and many of the fools believed their lies and took their children out of the school. Also the foolish boys who had gone out of the school are hostile toward their teachers, because in their humble opinion they are heretics and stand outside the community. But those of understanding among them know and recognise that a lie is in the right hand of those who spread this evil slander, and they were greatly distressed that their fathers had taken them out of school in their folly! And when they had led many astray, the hand of the benighted grew strong and by false informing they informed against the teachers before the government, that they wished to incite the inhabitants of the land to rebel. And they informed that they were writers of libel against the government, to the government of England, to shelter in its shadow, and also to H.N.Ts. And because of this informing the teachers were led to prison, and also expelled from the school. And they brought in their place another teacher, who knew neither Hebrew thoroughly nor Arabic as it should be. And he had no duty to teach them except the weekly portion, with the Targum of Onkelos and the Targum of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic. And he was to teach them the Haftarah with the Targum of Jonathan in Aramaic, with no understanding at all, like the other teachers! And after some days the school closed entirely! All this came upon us because we did not object, for the honour of our Creator, when we were hearing from those who study the Zohar and other Kabbalists, things that are forbidden to hear, and we were silent before them as our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "R. A. was seized for heresy, etc.; perhaps a word of heresy, etc." and there was fulfilled in us the saying of our Rabbis of blessed memory: "Whoever concedes to them falls into their hands; whoever relies on them, what is his is theirs." Thus far! Therefore we abandoned our way of studying the languages, Hebrew and Arabic, in their grammar, against our will, because of the wrath of the oppressor, through false informing, and we turned to the path of holiness, to the honour of our Father who is in heaven, in the nullification of the opinions of the philosopher, the false prophet, the author of the Zohar, who gathered into his hands the opinions of ancient philosophy, the worshippers of idols, images and hidden powers, which they had invented from their own heart. And the author of the Zohar seized their opinions, and thought to bring them into the faith of our holy Torah, and falsely called his name by the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, and said that the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called by him Atika Kadisha, was revealed to him and revealed to him hidden mysteries. And he hung his prophecy and his ideas on Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, peace be upon him. And he made his composition, the Zohar, and said that the higher ones agreed to his composition, because this philosopher saw that the Mishnah, the two Talmuds and the true midrashim of our Rabbis of blessed memory stood against him in the belief in His oneness, may He be blessed, therefore he thought to disqualify them, and he despised and mocked them and all who occupy themselves with them, and he called them by names of contempt and abasement, as the reader will see within! And he promised that Israel would not merit redemption until they turned from their way of occupying themselves with the Mishnah and the Talmud. Let them occupy themselves only with his new Torah, full of idols of images and faces of monstrous form, and various couplings. And by cunning and deceit they buried it in a chest in the ground, so that it would grow old and begin to rot; after some time they published it and brought it out through a king from among the kings of the idolaters (as Rabbi Chida wrote in his book Shem ha-Gedolim, in the section on books), as if it were an ancient composition of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna. And many of our later rabbis were drawn after the aforementioned philosopher with eyes shut, for he took them with the smoothness of his lips and his trimmings, and they did not give heed to his lies! Heaven forbid that any Jew should believe that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna or another of our Rabbis of blessed memory believed in such beliefs to exchange and replace the LORD our God, who made known His ways to Moses and His deeds to the children of Israel, for "He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in kindness," etc. for a strange god, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), and to conjoin and associate with Him five partzufim whose existence has not been established even by proof (Rabbi Ovadiah Sforno, Deuteronomy 13:3; and there 29:25; and see there 28:14) and to call them by the name of the LORD our God, and the LORD, the God of truth, whose existence has been established by many proofs, strong as a cast mirror, as Rabbi Saadia Gaon wrote in Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Rabbi, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and the Rambam in Moreh Nevukhim and in the Yad, let us abandon Him and leave Him, and say that He has no name and no appellation, and let us worship the partzufim and the forms which, according to his words, were created and descended from Him! And we have already expounded at length within, with clear proofs from our Rabbis of blessed memory, on the nullification of these strange opinions of the philosopher, the false prophet, the aforementioned! For it is the aim of our holy Torah to distance us from belief in idols, whether corporeal or spiritual. And its aim is to know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him. And He has neither father nor brother nor son (Rabbah, parashat Yitro), and did not receive His kingship from another and is not destined to hand it on to another, as our Rabbis of blessed memory explained (Rabbah, Bamidbar; Shir ha-Shirim, parashah 1; Yerushalmi, Sanhedrin, chapter Dinei Mamonot) on the verse "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God," and on what Nebuchadnezzar said: "and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods!" And I have seen Rabbi Menachem di Lonzano, in the book Derekh ha-Chayyim, who opened his mouth wide to speak error about the holy pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, concerning his saying, in the name of the philosopher, that one could not worship the Cause of causes, except the prophet of the generation by his nature, or the outstanding philosopher in what he acquired from wisdom; but others worship other than Him, because they do not understand: the result is only composite! And at these words of the pietist he was angered and thought that here was ground for complaint against him, and found a pretext to mislead the listeners and alarm them by saying: "Is it so that such-and-such and such-and-such of our later famous sages worship other than Him?" And he counted them, in his language, one by one by name. And he did not take to heart that many of the sages whom he counted went along with eyes shut and believed the words of the author of the Zohar who called himself by the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, in order to attach his false prophecies to the name of the Tanna, and spoke rebellion against the LORD our God, who was revealed to him in his study house as Atika Kadisha, and revealed to him hidden secrets and hidden powers (Zohar, Bereshit 22), for the Creator is the idol called Abba, who used to command his consort, the she-idol Imma, and she does all that he says to her, except for the creation of the first man: it was she, Imma, who said and made the first man, not with the will of Abba! And in Parashat Vayera, folio 112, and likewise in Parashat Balak, folio 191, he ascribes our worship and our prayers to a strange god, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), who did not make the heavens and the earth. And he calls these idols by the name of the LORD our God. And about Ze'ir Anpin, Jeremiah the prophet, peace be upon him, proclaimed "Thus shall you say to them: the gods that did not make the heavens and the earth shall perish from the earth and from under these heavens." For it is clear in many places in the Zohar that he is created, not creator (see Zohar, Bereshit 22; and Yosher Levav, folio 3b). And yet he says to worship him, and to bless him, and to accept him as God, and to fear his consort! And many of our later rabbis, whom he mentioned in the book Derekh ha-Chayyim, in his amazement at the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, went along with eyes shut and were drawn after him and believed his belief and accepted upon themselves the idol, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), as God! And all this came upon them because they did not contemplate the wisdom of the Creator of all, which is to investigate and examine the works of Creation as explained in the words of the Rabbi, the author of Moreh Nevukhim, and in the words of the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and our master Saadia Gaon and Rabbi Yehudah Halevi in the Kuzari, as the prophet, peace be upon him, said: "They do not regard the deed of the LORD." For they thought their words were Greek wisdom, and they kept far from it, as far as a bow-shot, and they also did not take to heart the true words of our forefathers of blessed memory in the midrashim that Abraham our father did not recognise his Creator except by contemplating the work of the LORD, and investigated and expounded them and brought proofs from them until he attained the truth; then the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed to him and said to him: "You love righteousness and hate wickedness," etc. A parable: to one walking on the road who saw a castle, etc. (Midrash ha-Gadol, at the beginning of Parashat Lekh Lekha). And perforce we acknowledge the truth that the words of the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, clearly say that one cannot worship the God of truth except, etc. but others worship other than Him, as the prophet said: "For many days Israel was without a true God," and as our eyes see and our ears hear, to the point that a man can say to his fellow! "Your people is my people, and your God is not my God!" And to the God of truth let us pour out our prayer, to guide us on paths of uprightness, and to deliver us from every strange belief. Amen, may it be His will.**

Grammar:

- Voice: 1:4 is in the author's own voice; 'we' (עלינו, עזבנו, נודה) is the author and the circle of the Yemenite teachers. The long periods are divided into English sentences, and no clause is dropped.
- Aramaic quotations: 1:4.198-206 (דמודי להון) is Bavli Aramaic; 1:4.274-275 (עתיקא קדישא) and 1:4.278 (רזין טמירין) are Zohar Aramaic; 1:4.591-600 is Biblical Aramaic (Dan 3:25) and 1:4.800-815 is Biblical Aramaic (Jer 10:11).
- Allusions with no quotation formula are translated from the verse and take no marks: 'שקר בימין' (1:4.61-62, Isa 44:20), 'בחלק שפתיו' (1:4.396-397, Prov 7:21), and 'ולדעת כי ה' הוא האלהים אין עוד מלבדו' (1:4.540-547, Deut 4:35). The other verses behind the author's phrases are listed in the apparatus.
- 1:4.667 'וכי' opens a rhetorical question, kept as a question. 1:4.688 'שַמָנָה' as pointed would be 'grew fat' (Deut 32:15), but the context requires 'שֶׁמָּנָה', 'whom he counted': he counted the sages 'one by one by name' (1:4.676-680), and 1:4.844-847 says the same again ('whom he mentioned'). The English follows the context.
- 1:4.76 התעו is Hif'il, 'they led astray' (transitive, with רבים as object). 1:4.90 להמריד is Hif'il of מרד, 'to make rebel'. 1:4.198-206 is Aramaic: דמתרחץ is Itpa'al of רחץ 'to trust, to rely' (cf. Dan 3:28 רחצו עלוהי), not 'to bathe'.
- Sentences that open after a Hebrew full stop with no main clause of their own: 1:4.94 ושהם, 1:4.146 והפטרה, 1:4.540 ולדעת. The English keeps the full stop and supplies a main clause from the sentence before (token notes); 1:4.896 ורבינו is a continuation of a list and is joined to the sentence before it.

Note: The paragraph is the author's own voice, a continuous prose period. The pack has no morphology, lexicon or commentary, so the reasons for the choices are in the token notes and the apparatus.

Other readings:

- ב״ע: by heart (context). ב״ע read as בעל פה: the Targum recited by rote, which would suit 'with no understanding at all'.
- ב״ע: in Arabic (context). ב״ע read as בערבי, the abbreviation of the 'in Arabic' of 1:4.145.
- וגיזומיו: and his exaggerations (גוזמא). גיזומיו may come from the Aramaic גוזמא, 'exaggeration'; the English keeps 'trimmings' (cuttings) pending the owner's ruling.
- שַמָנָה: had grown fat (pointing of the text). The pointing שַמָנָה reads as 'grew fat' (Deut 32:15); the context requires 'whom he counted'.

Ancient Near East:

- Chida is Rabbi Chayyim Yosef David Azulai; his Shem ha-Gedolim is a bibliographical dictionary of Jewish authors and books, which the author cites here.
- Ze'ir Anpin, Abba, Imma and Atika Kadisha are the partzufim of the Zohar's divine structure. The author calls them idols in his own charge, and the English gives his words as he writes them.
- Saadia Gaon's Arabic translation of the Torah is taught in Yemenite communities beside the Aramaic Targum Onkelos; Targum Jonathan is the Aramaic Targum to the Prophets, from which the Haftarah is read.

Apparatus:

- Base text: Wikisource transcription. Q2 additions are translated as base text and are not yet collated with the 1931 scan.
- 1:4.62 'a lie in the right hand' alludes to Isa 44:20.
- 1:4.396 'the smoothness of his lips' alludes to Prov 7:21.
- 1:4.429-437 'He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in kindness' is Joel 2:13 (cf. Exod 34:6, Jonah 4:2), cut short by the author with 'etc.'; the author's 'quick to anger' (1:4.440-441, 1:4.775-776, 1:4.866-867) is set against it.
- 1:4.478-480 'strong as a cast mirror' is Job 37:18 (Hebrew 'strong like a cast mirror').
- 1:4.454-465 references as the author gives them: Sforno on Deut 13:3, 29:25, 28:14.
- 1:4.540-547 Deut 4:35.
- 1:4.584-590 Isa 44:6: 'I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God'.
- 1:4.591-600 Dan 3:25 (Biblical Aramaic).
- 1:4.800-815 Jer 10:11 (Biblical Aramaic); 'gods' renders Aramaic elahaya.
- 1:4.910 Isa 5:12, quoted by the author.
- 1:4.1001-1006 2 Chr 15:3, quoted by the author as 'the prophet'.
- 1:4.1017-1021 Ruth 1:16 with the negation the author gives ('your God is not my God'); the English follows his wording.
- 1:4.107 'הינ״ץ' is not expanded in the English; the expansion is not certain. A conjecture is in the token note (see the question).
- 1:4.150 'ב״ע' is read 'in Aramaic' (the Targum to the Haftarah, set against 'בערבי' for the Torah portion at 1:4.145, so that the pupils understand nothing); the other expansions, 'בעל פה' ('by heart') and 'בערבי' ('in Arabic'), are in readings. None is certain.
- 1:4.186 'ר״א' (in 'דר״א') is the author's abbreviation, left as 'R. A.' by the ruling, since the paragraph names no Rabbi; the token note says who is meant.
- 1:4.1034 'אכי״ר' expanded as 'may it be His will' (אמן כן יהי רצון).
- 1:4.14-17 and 1:4.63-65 'spread an evil slander' / 'those who spread this evil slander' echo Num 14:37 (מוציאי דבה רעה).
- 1:4.129-130 'על בריה' as printed ('on a creature'); the likelier word is 'על בוריה' ('thoroughly'), which the English follows.
- 1:4.162-164 'All this came upon us' is Ps 44:18.
- 1:4.202-203 'דמתרחץ עליהון' is read 'whoever relies on them' (Aramaic רחץ, 'to trust'; cf. Dan 3:28).
- 1:4.218-219 'the wrath of the oppressor' is Isa 51:13 (חמת המציק).
- 1:4.226-227 'the path of holiness' is Isa 35:8 (דרך הקדש).
- 1:4.239-240 'gathered into his hands' alludes to Prov 30:4 (אסף ... בחפניו).
- 1:4.250-251 'invented from their own heart' alludes to 1 Kgs 12:33 and Neh 6:8 (בדא / בודא מלבו).
- 1:4.357-358 'בקרקע עולם' is the idiom for the ground itself, not 'everlasting ground'.
- 1:4.423-428 'who made known His ways to Moses and His deeds to the children of Israel' is Ps 103:7.
- 1:4.471-473 'the LORD, the God of truth' is Jer 10:10 (ה' אלהים אמת).
- 1:4.611-612 'to speak error' is Isa 32:6 (ולדבר אל ה' תועה).
- 1:4.688 'שַמָנָה' as printed would be 'grew fat' (Deut 32:15); the likelier word is 'שֶׁמָּנָה' ('whom he counted'), which the English follows (see readings).
- 1:4.710-711 'ודבר סרה על ה'' ('spoke rebellion against the LORD') is Deut 13:6 (cf. Isa 59:13).
- 1:4.918-920 'as far as a bow-shot' is Gen 21:16 (כמטחוי קשת).
- 1:4.956-959 'You love righteousness and hate wickedness' is Ps 45:8.
- 1:4.985-986 'ברור מללו' ('clearly say') echoes Job 33:3.
- 1:4.1025-1026 'let us pour out our prayer' echoes Ps 142:3.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 1:5

> וקראתי שם הספר מלחמות ה' על יחודו כי הפילסוף מחבר הספר הזהר קלקל עלינו את אמיתת ייחוד השי״ת, ונמשכו אחריו כמה רבנים וגדולים בתורה בעצימת עינים ועליהם אמר שלמה בחכמתו, כי רבים חללים הפילה ועצומים כל הרוגיה כמו שדרשו רז״ל (סנהדרין רי״ף) כי רבים חללים הפילה זה תלמיד שלא הגיע להוראה ומורה (כמו שעינינו רואות כמה מחברים דמעיילי פילא בקופא דמחטא ממיעוט בקיאותם) ועצומים כל הרוגיה זה תלמיד שהגיע להוראה ואינו מורה, (שאינו נותן לב להורות לאחרים כהלכה, ועצומים לשון ועוצם עיניו רש״י ז״ל) וכל שכן אם משדל אחרים לעסוק בספ' החיצון ס' הזהר ואינו נותן לב להבין הסתירה רק הולך בעצימת עין השכל ומכשיל אחרים באמונה כוזבת שעליו נאמר ועצומים כל הרוגיה ועובר על ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול, ושגגת תלמוד עולה זדון, והוא חוטא ומחטיא את הרבים וחטא הרבים תלוי בו.

**And I named the book The Wars of the LORD for His unity, because the philosopher, the author of the book the Zohar, spoiled for us the truth of the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, and several rabbis and great men of the Torah followed him with eyes shut. And of them Solomon said in his wisdom: "For she has cast down many slain, and mighty are all her slain." As our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded (Sanhedrin, the Rif): "For she has cast down many slain" this is a student who has not reached instruction and teaches, (as we see with our own eyes how many authors who bring an elephant through the eye of a needle, from the scantness of their expertise) "and mighty are all her slain" this is a student who has reached instruction and does not teach (who does not set his mind to teach others correctly; "mighty" is the word of "and he shuts his eyes", Rashi of blessed memory). And all the more so, if he entices others to occupy themselves with the external book, the book of the Zohar, and does not set his mind to understand the contradiction, but walks with the eye of reason shut, and makes others stumble in a false faith, of whom it is said, "and mighty are all her slain"; and transgresses against "and before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block"; and error in study counts as wilful sin, and he sins and causes the many to sin, and the sin of the many hangs on him.**

Grammar:

- וקראתי is a perfect with waw ('and I called'); with שם הספר it means 'named the book'.
- The reason clause runs from כי (1:5.8) to בעצימת עינים (1:5.25-26): the philosopher spoiled the truth of the unity, and the followers went after him with eyes shut. From ועליהם a new sentence begins.
- כי רבים חללים הפילה is Prov 7:26, said of the 'strange woman' of Prov 7 and here applied to the author of the Zohar; הפילה is a perfect, third feminine singular.
- Each זה ('this is') in the Talmudic exposition introduces a rabbinic identification of one of the verse's words; the English keeps 'this is' at each point.
- דמעיילי פילא בקופא דמחטא is a Talmudic Aramaic idiom for doing the impossible; the English gives its sense, 'who bring an elephant through the eye of a needle'.
- ועובר על takes the cited prohibition, Lev 19:14, as its object; ושגגת תלמוד עולה זדון is a rabbinic maxim cited without a formula.

Note: The author's own Hebrew, with the Talmud's gloss on Prov 7:26 translated as his paraphrase. The English keeps his lists of 'this is' and 'who' clauses in order.

Apparatus:

- The text is the Wikisource base text; Wikisource additions and corrections are not flagged word by word until the 1931 scan is collated (decisions, Q2).
- The title: מלחמות ה׳ takes the form of Num 21:14, 'ספר מלחמת ה׳' (the book of the Wars of the LORD).
- Prov 7:26, quoted: 'For she has cast down many slain, and mighty are all her slain' (translated from the verse as he quotes it).
- Lev 19:14, 'ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול', cited after 'ועובר על': 'and before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block'.
- 'Sanhedrin' and 'the Rif' as written; the Talmudic gloss on the verse is his paraphrase and is not marked as a quotation.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 1:6

> ועל אמונה החיצונה הלזו של הפילסוף מחבר הזהר דרשו רז״ל (ילקוט פרשת קדושים ומדרש הגדול שם ורמב״ם בס' המצות לאוין י') אל תפנו אל האלילים ואלהי אם אתה פונה אחרים (לכבדם ספורנו) סופך לעשותם אלוהות ע״כ, וכך אירע באמונת הפילסוף מחבר הזהר כי הלומדים הראשונים אשר למדו בו בחשבם שהוא לרשב״י התנא, חשבו לישב דבריו ולקרות את הפרצופים כלים, והחשיבום וכיבדו אותם והבאים אחריהם עשו אותם אלוהות כמחשבת הפילסוף המחבר וקיבלום עליהם באלוהות כמו שיתבאר בפנים וכן דרשו רז״ל בפסוק יין ושכר אל תשת וז״ל ר' חייא פתח פקודי ה' ישרים וכתיב ביין יתהלך במישרים וכתיב משמחי לב וכתיב ויין ישמח לבב אנוש מה היין הזה משמח את הלב כך דברי תורה משמחין את הלב מה היין הזה השותה ממנו יותר מצרכו לסוף מקיא את הכל כך דברי תורה העוסק בהן ומחשב בהן יותר מדאי סוף שהוא יוצא למינות ע״כ (מדרש הגדול פרשת שמיני פסוק יין ושכר) כדבר הזה עשה הפילסוף נביא השקר מחבר הזהר לתור אחרי לבבו לחשב בדברי תורה יותר מדאי בדרכים הרחוקים מן האמת, ורחוקים מאד מן המדות שקבלו חכמים איש מפי איש שהתורה נדרשת בהן והן הי״ג מדות דר' ישמעאל ול״ג מדות דר' יוסי הגלילי דאגדתא כמו שיראה המעיין הנבון והסית והדיח לחכמים ישרי לב ההולכים לתומם, להאמינו לשקריו שנגלה לו הקב״ה הנקרא אצלו סבא דסבין ומשה רבינו ‏ע״ה ואליהו וגילו לו סתרים של מינות שאסור לחשב בהן אפי' בבית הכסא והבטיח לעוסק בתורתו בלי מבין לשכר רב יותר מגופי תורה כדי להעור עיני חכמים ולסתום דרך העיון בדבריו שלא להבין את נכליו ולהגדיל מעלת העוסקים בתורתו החדשה המלאה אלילים שונים בעצמותם ופעוליהם מבלי להקפיד על תוספת ורבוי באלהינו המיוחד מכל שאר האחדים ולא יתנו לב איך הקפידה תורה על בל תוסיף בין בתפילין בין במזוזה בין בארבעה מינין שבלולב וכן בשאר מצות אע״פ שנותן חמש הפרשיות בעור אחד והוא מחברן להיות אחד, וכן אם מוסיף במזוזה פרשה אחת אע״פ שקלף מחברן לחיות אחד לא אמרינן כלא חד וכן בציצית ובאגודת ארבעה מינין אם הוסיף מין חמישי באגודה פסל ולא אמרינן כלא חד.

**And concerning this external faith of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar, our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded (Yalkut, Parashat Kedoshim, and the Midrash ha-Gadol there, and the Rambam in Sefer ha-Mitzvot, negative commandment 10): "Do not turn to the idols, and the gods of; if you turn to others (to honor them, Sforno), your end is to make them divinities." Thus far. And so it befell the faith of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar, for the early students who learned from it, thinking that it was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna's, they thought to make sense of his words; and to call the partzufim vessels, and they esteemed them and honored them, and those who came after them made them divinities, according to the thought of the philosopher, the author, and accepted them upon themselves as divinities, as will be explained within. And likewise our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded in the verse: wine and strong drink you shall not drink, and these are his words: "Rabbi Chiya opened: 'The precepts of the LORD are right'; and it is written of wine: 'it goes down smoothly'; and it is written: 'rejoicing the heart'; and it is written: 'and wine gladdens the heart of man.' Just as this wine gladdens the heart, so the words of Torah gladden the heart; just as this wine, one who drinks of it more than his need in the end vomits everything; so the words of Torah, one who occupies himself with them and thinks about them too much, in the end he goes out into heresy." Thus far. (Midrash ha-Gadol, Parashat Shemini, verse 'wine and strong drink'). In this way did the philosopher, the false prophet, the author of the Zohar, act, to follow after his heart, to think about the words of Torah too much, in paths far from the truth, and very far from the rules that the Sages received, a man from the mouth of a man, by which the Torah is expounded, and these are the thirteen rules of Rabbi Ishmael and the thirty-three rules of Rabbi Yose the Galilean, for the Aggadah, as the discerning, attentive reader will see; and he enticed and seduced the sages, the upright of heart, who walk in their simplicity, to believe him in his lies: that there was revealed to him the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called by him the Elder of Elders, and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and Elijah, and they revealed to him secrets of heresy, which it is forbidden to think about them, even in the lavatory; and he promised one who occupies himself with his Torah without understanding, a reward greater than the essentials of the Torah, in order to blind the eyes of the sages and to stop up the way of study in his words so as not to understand his machinations, and to magnify the merit of those who occupy themselves with his new Torah, full of idols different in their essences and their activities, without being particular about the addition and multiplicity, in our God, the Unique, above all other ones; and do not take note how the Torah was strict about 'you shall not add', whether in tefillin, or in a mezuzah, or in the four species of the lulav, and likewise in the other commandments, even though he puts five sections in one hide and he joins them to be one, and likewise, if he adds one section to a mezuzah, even though parchment joins them to be one, we do not say 'as though it were not one'; and likewise in tzitzit, and in the bundle of four species, if he added a fifth species to the bundle, it is disqualified; and we do not say 'as though it were not one'.**

Grammar:

- The paragraph is one long period. The quotation from Lev 19:4 (in the Yalkut, Midrash ha-Gadol and Rambam) runs from 'Do not turn' to 'Thus far'; its parenthesis is Sforno's gloss, kept in parentheses.
- The Midrash ha-Gadol passage (Rabbinic Hebrew) chains verses with 'and it is written' (וכתיב): Ps 19:9, Prov 23:31 (in the Midrash's wording) and Ps 104:15. Its analogy 'just as ... so' (מה ... כך) carries the argument, and the second half turns on 'too much' (מדאי).
- The infinitives after עשה (לתור, לחשב, להעור, ולסתום, ולהגדיל) give the purpose of the philosopher's deed; לתור אחרי לבבו alludes to Num 15:39, and להעור עיני חכמים to Deut 16:19.
- בחשבם שהוא לרשב״י התנא: the ל of לרשב״י is possessive. The early students thought the book was Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna's.
- The verbs in the sentence about the early students (חשבו, והחשיבום, וכיבדו, עשו, וקיבלום) narrate what followed from the first error, in the perfect with waw.
- דאגדתא, מינין and לא אמרינן כלא חד are Talmudic Aramaic inside the author's Hebrew; the last two clauses are the halakhic conclusion of the paragraph and the English keeps them as parallel sentences.

Note: One period in the Hebrew, divided at the quotation boundaries and at the Midrash's clauses. Each quotation formula is translated and each closing ע״כ is 'Thus far'.

Apparatus:

- Lev 19:4, quoted words 'Do not turn to the idols' (אל תפנו אל האלילים). The rest of the quotation is the author's wording (ואלהי אם אתה פונה אחרים) and is rendered as he gives it; in the verse ואלהי continues 'מסכה'.
- Lev 10:9, 'Wine and strong drink you shall not drink' (in the verse: wine and strong drink).
- Ps 19:9: 'The precepts of the LORD are right' and 'rejoicing the heart' (משמחי לב).
- Prov 23:31: 'ביין יתהלך במישרים' ('of wine: it goes down smoothly'); the verse has 'כי יתן בכוס עינו יתהלך במישרים' and the Midrash's wording is rendered as he gives it.
- Ps 104:15: 'and wine gladdens the heart of man' (ויין ישמח לבב אנוש).
- Num 15:39, alluded to in 'לתור אחרי לבבו' (to follow after his heart).
- Deut 16:19, alluded to in 'להעור עיני חכמים' (a bribe 'blinds the eyes of the wise').
- 'בל תוסיף', the rabbinic name of the prohibition of Deut 4:2 and 13:1 (לא תספו / לא תסף עליו).
- ל״ג in 'ול״ג מדות דר׳ יוסי הגלילי' is written as thirty-three by letters; the English follows the wave 1 ruling (thirty-three). The usual count of Rabbi Yose the Galilean's rules is thirty-two.
- לחיות (1:6.307) is the witness's spelling of להיות; translated 'to be'.
- כלא חד (1:6.311, 1:6.326): rendered 'as though it were not one' under the owner's reservation on 1:7; a possible alternative reading is כולא חד, 'it is all one'.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 1:7

> כל שכן וקל וחומר באלהינו ברוך הוא וברוך שמו שתורה הקפידה שלא לטפול ולשתף עמו שום דבר מכל הנבראים בין גשמי בין רוחני כמו שנאמר זובח לאלהים יחרם בלתי לה' לבדו, ואמר רשב״י התנא ע״ה כל המשתף שם שמים ודבר אחר נעקר מן העולם, ולא אמרינן כלא חד כיון שהתורה ביארה בהדיא בכמה מקומות שהוא אחד מיוחד מכל שאר האחדים הנה כן המזכירים את ה' אל דמי לכם מלהודיע אחדותו ית' לבניכם ולתלמידיכם כמצווה עליכם.

**All the more so, a fortiori, regarding our God, blessed be He, and blessed be His name, that the Torah insisted that one should not attach to Him or associate with Him anything of all created things, whether corporeal or spiritual, as it is said: "He who sacrifices to the gods shall be destroyed, save to the LORD alone." And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever associates the name of Heaven with something else is uprooted from the world." And we should not say that He is one as the others are one, since the Torah has made clear plainly in many places that He is one, unique, apart from all the other ones. Thus, you who mention the LORD, do not stay silent about making known His oneness, may He be blessed, to your children and your disciples, as you are commanded.**
