| word | gloss | lemma | root | parse | sense |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| המו"ל | the publisher — Abbreviation of המוציא לאור (the one who brings out to the light), written with gershayim before the final letter. It is the heading of the publisher's voice, not the author's. |  |  |  |  |

Grammar:

- המו"ל is a one-word heading with no verb and no syntax; it names the speaker of the paragraph that follows.
- The abbreviation stands for המוציא לאור, and the English gives the ordinary title 'the publisher'.
- The publisher's voice (1:10 to 1:13) is not the author's, as the decisions for this work require.

Note: Heading only; the section it introduces is translated in its own unit.

## Chapter 2 — פרק 2 (Milchamot ha-Shem 2:1–2:34)

### Reading text

<sup>2:1</sup> The Wars of the LORD

<sup>2:2</sup> Question: one of the students asked, and these are his words: "Let our teacher inform us: the worship and the prayer that we pray, to whom it pertains. To the Cause of causes, blessed be He, or to the emanated being that was emanated from Him (Ze'ir Anpin), as explained to us in your hearing by our teacher Salem son of David, who travelled from here to the Holy Land, according to the true faith, as explained in the book Matzref ha-Emunah and in a book on the Torah, that whoever worships Ein Sof worships without a God of truth and without a God of judgment, so that we may know whom we shall worship. And your reply, speedily, my lord. Thus far."

<sup>2:3</sup> Reply. "Your reply is explained in the book Kisse Eliyahu, from folio 13 to folio 18: 'A wise man will hear and add to learning.' And what we have received is that worship is to God, one Lord, in order to draw the flow from Him to the ten sefirot, as Lechem Shlomo wrote. Thus far the words of the respondent."

<sup>2:4</sup> The questioner replied again. Your reply, my friend, came closed and sealed, and in it there is nothing but an indication of a place: "to study in Kisse Eliyahu, from folio 13 to folio 18, 'A wise man will hear and add to learning,' and what we have received is that worship is to God, one Lord, etc." I did not understand your opinion and your intention in this, whether this, what you have received, is in accordance with the words of Kisse Eliyahu or the opposite of his words. For when I studied in Kisse Eliyahu the place you marked for me, I did not find what I sought; on the contrary, there, on folio 3, he compares the oneness of the Creator to the other kinds of oneness, where he wrote: "Just as this house as a whole is called by the name one house. And if you enter it, you will find many rooms, large and small, and many other places. And each and every one of them ascribes to it a designation, one name. Also, a wooden building that has several attributes within it has them. Also, you will find further that this holy wall, which was built, was in parts; each and every stone was separate from the clods of earth, by itself, and the lime by itself, etc. And after the builder came and joined all these parts with his wisdom, this within that, and this beside that, and they became one wall, etc., thus, then, all is one piece and one part. And so is the matter with us, etc." And there, on folios 25 and 29, he compares it to the human body, joined of bones and sinews and flesh, head and eye and ear and nose and mouth and hands and feet, and the whole is called by the name man, Reuben or Simeon. And on folios 25, 26 and 27 he wrote: "The sum of the matter is that the First Cause, which is called Ein Sof by all the Kabbalists, is He who emanated, created, formed and made, and He is hidden within Ze'ir Anpin, and then Ze'ir Anpin is the one who rules over all creatures, leads them, feeds them and sustains them, by the power of Ein Sof within him. Therefore He is our God, and we are His people, for our souls are His portion, and Him we shall worship, and He is the God of our fathers, in whose hand is the conduct of the worlds, for reward and punishment. But Ein Sof, with the other partzufim above Ze'ir and his Nukva, if human beings order their prayers to them individually, without praying to Ze'ir Anpin, even if they direct their intention to the soul hidden in them, they will cry out and not be answered. And on the contrary, those who pray to them will be punished, for it is the will of the First Cause that He be the one who brings out and brings in His flow to the lower beings, and there is no other besides Him. See there carefully." And the words of the Rabbi, the author of Kisse Eliyahu, stand against the words of the Rambam, of blessed memory, in his commentary on the Mishnah, in his composition, and in Moreh Nevukhim, and against the words of the pious one, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, in the Gate of Unity, and Rabbi Saadia Gaon in the book Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Roke'ach, who wrote that His oneness, may He be blessed, is not like the one of a pair, nor like the one of a species, nor like the one man who is divided into many ones. And not one like a simple body, etc., which receives division without end. But the Name, may He be blessed, is one with a oneness that has no like. Also, Kisse Eliyahu wrote that Ein Sof is the soul of Atik, and Arikh Anpin, and Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva, and my teachers, of blessed memory, the aforesaid, wrote that He is not a body, nor a force in a body! And according to his words He is a force in a body. Also he wrote that Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma preceded Ze'ir Anpin who is our God (according to his words), and he is called a son of Abba and Imma, etc. And our Rabbis of blessed memory said that He is eternal before all that exists, and that every existent other than Him is not eternal, etc. Also he wrote concerning Ein Sof, blessed be He, that no worship pertains to Him, and no invocation at all. And no name applies to Him: not YHVH, nor Adonai, etc. but only to Ze'ir Anpin and his Nukva in the World of Emanation alone, and not to Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva that are in the emanated worlds above the World of Emanation, as explained there, 4, 49, the end of side a, and on folio 53....

<sup>2:5</sup> And how can we leave all the divinities that are above the World of Emanation, and worship specifically Ze'ir and his Nukva, who are in the World of Emanation, since there have already preceded him several Atikin and Arikhei Anpin, and Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva in the upper worlds; there is no number of those still closer to Ein Sof?

<sup>2:6</sup> And our early rabbis said that it is not fitting to worship, to give thanks, to magnify, and to glorify, except to the first God of all that exists apart from Him! And why should we leave the principal Ein Sof, that contracts above all of them, with all the partzufim close to it, and worship that which is very far from it, which is the last partzuf of the World of Emanation? All this, make us understand, our lord, let us go and pursue the LORD our Maker the Creator of the beginning. And do not pour upon us a word of Belial, God forbid. For who has gathered grace and good understanding in his palms, to have insight and to know the LORD through investigating divine matters in the principles of the faith, like you. Who will ascend to the mountain of the LORD, and who will stand in His holy place, like you, for I am more brutish than any man, and I have no understanding of a man. And the Rock knows the secrets of the heart, the examiner of hearts, for I did not give sleep to my eyes, and my sleep was taken from my eyes until I find solutions and whoever comes to purify himself, they help him, to provide for him a guide to the way of holiness by intellect and knowledge, like Khalkhal and Darda, and among the sages of truth a sage and an artisan, like Ethan and Heman, for perhaps the rabbis who lack this wisdom are to us false oracles and misleading ones, God forbid. And you, my lord, to you its secrets are revealed, and your treasure will fill the bellies of your disciples, they will be sated and delight in your goodness, and upon us to pay the wages of your work. And you, do not withhold good from its owners. And here I adjure you by the God of heaven: make Your face shine upon us, to answer the weary with a word spoken in its proper setting, and we shall be servants to my lord. And our lips will ask a great reward for your goodness, then we shall not be ashamed, neither in this world nor in the world to come, and we shall return and graze among the lilies from the company of sages and discerning ones.

<sup>2:7</sup> Second Reply. I saw all that is written in the letter of the eminent one, a tree whose branches are many, its height like the height of cedars, After the pardon for the delay, for the pressure of the times is outstretched, and every delay is for good. When I looked at the letter, behold, you opened your mouth, by mentioning divinities, thinking that it is against us. And what are we, that you murmur against us, and your scorn does not reach us, but only to the sages of Israel, whose least is thicker than your loins, and all Israel rests on them, and by their merit the world stands. Woe to you, for you have brought out against them words that are not according to the law, in innocence, and in its place guile. But your judgment has already been made clear, by the mouth of all the masters of wisdom. And as for what you wrote about Kisse Eliyahu, that on folio 3 he likens His oneness, may He be blessed, to the other unities. You are already walking in darkness. Surely the beginning of his words on folio 20 is that all these likenesses are about holy lights, which have no grasp, no form and no likeness, neither in intellect nor in knowledge at all and in principle, but so that the intellect can receive them, we were permitted to liken. And on folio 4b he wrote that all the epithets and attributes are in the manner of likeness, in the sefirot and the holy lights, the emanated beings. But in Him, may He be blessed, there is not in Him any likeness and form, and grasp in thought at all and in principle. And as for what you wrote, how can we leave the other partzufim and worship Ze'ir Anpin with the power in him, Ein Sof, blessed be He. The Master, Kisse Eliyahu, has already explained on folio 25b, that when we call upon Ze'ir Anpin, we call all the partzufim together, with a soul hidden in them. And as for what you wrote, why do we leave the partzufim closest to Ein Sof and call upon Ze'ir Anpin. Because it is known that among the inner attributes some are judgment and some are mercy, and this one includes them all, and therefore the Emanator wanted to perform His actions through this vessel. Before you object to the likenesses concerning the upper ones, which you have no right to ponder, all the more so to mock, object to your corporeal hand, which does all the labors, and the head above does not do anything. Also, the power of speech, which is your glory, above every living creature, why was it not given above your eyes. But thus His wisdom decreed, may He be blessed. And if you have proper counsel, go to your Creator and counsel Him. And as for what you wrote, that the words of Kisse Eliyahu are against the Rambam, etc., who wrote that it is not a force in a body, and according to the words of Kisse Eliyahu it is a force in a body. Surely all the Kabbalists with one mouth answer and say that whoever ascribes corporeality to the sefirot, like you, is a denier and has no share in the God of Israel. And as for their having called them subtle lights, it is only to soothe the ear! We have to ask about what the Rambam wrote: "Let him direct his heart toward the Shekhinah and pray." And in the Guide he wrote that the Shekhinah is a created light. And more than this, what he wrote about the glory of the LORD, that it is created. If so, how did Israel go out to the opening of their tents and bow down to the created thing. And more than this, what he wrote, that every form which the prophets saw and spoke with is a created light. If so, we have no prophecy through the Creator, but all of it from the side of the created ones. And if it is said that the created thing was attached to the Creator, then, in your opinion, it is a force in a body! Your answer will quickly spring up, the end of the verse: "They refuse to know Me, says the LORD."

<sup>2:8</sup> Reply from the questioner. My soul longed to hear words refined like cast mirrors, from the heights of heaven, burning. For I am poor in all knowledge, longing for the shade of the gourd. And instead of your humility making me great, you gave me to drink many waters, bitter as gall. You made me like a booth in a cucumber field, and my soul is incurable by praises of deceit (like the blessing of the wicked Balaam), dreadful ones. And with the words of a slanderer you concluded, and you resembled a man who casts off discipline, and a bereaved bear. And in truth this is not the way of the Torah. Our holy Torah, its ways are ways of pleasantness. And you shall love your neighbor as yourself. "What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow." Thus said Hillel, Prince of Israel! He stated the sum of the matter: as for my having opened my mouth to disparage the sages of Israel, and having brought out against them words that are not according to the law. Far be it from me to disparage any person, even a gentile, all the more so an Israelite. And I know no place in my words for what you claim, that there is disparagement in them. And if one raises difficulties against them from the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory, and reveals a place of contradiction, there is no prohibition in this at all. And also in the Talmud they raise difficulties even against those greater than they, and bring proof to refute their words, and say, "Refutation of Rabbi So-and-so." That of Rabbi So-and-so is a fabrication (the Arukh's reading: berota), and in Sanhedrin and in Berakhot we say: "The one who sees the rainbow must bow down, for it is written: 'Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud, etc., and I saw and fell on my face.'" "They curse it in the West, etc. Rabbi Abahu blasphemes against it, etc." And behold, in this your letter I found a complaint; a reply I did not find. Is it I who called these partzufim divinities? Did not the Kabbalists themselves say so. Go and learn from the intention of the blessings and the prayer: who is our God, and who is the God of our fathers. And in the Zohar he asks: "Who is this Elohim, such and such?" Moreover, for the Kabbalists explained that many worlds, thousands of thousands and myriads of myriads, were emanated, created, formed and made, only they did not put forth a hand to explain them because of their great concealment. For they are very subtle lights. And each world is comprised of ten sefirot. And each sefirah is comprised of ten details of details, as we said in the World of Emanation. And all of them are in the aspect of circles, this within this, and this inside that. And likewise in the aspect of the sefirot of straightness, which are in the form of a man of upright stature with 248 limbs, etc. All these worlds, each one of them comprises two aspects, of circles and of straightness, in general and in particular. And all the words of the Kabbalists and their explanations are only in the World of Emanation, which has already been coarsened and revealed more; and in it they explained all the matters of the comprehensive partzufim, which are five: Arikh Anpin, and Abba, and Imma, and Ze'ir, and his Nukva. Since it has already been made clear to you from their words that they say the partzufim were coarsened and revealed, and that they call the aforementioned partzufim divinities, when they say our God and the God of our fathers in prayer and in blessings, and that they intend a known attribute in every word. Your complaint does not stand against me, neither as a charge of corporeality nor as a charge of divinity, but against them, for they said it, and they said it. And the difficulty returns to its place: how shall we leave aside Ein Sof together with all the sefirot that are in the upper worlds, together with Arikh Anpin and Abba and Imma, and worship Ze'ir Anpin and say that He is our God, and we are His people and His servants; He made us, and to Him we are. In this letter of yours (where you said, "since it is known that the inner attributes are, some of them judgment and some of them mercy, etc.") you have already made a complete admission that this is your opinion: that no worship and no prayer applies to the Cause over all the causes, but only to Ze'ir Anpin, as the Rav Mikdash Melekh wrote, and Kisse Eliyahu, and Mahari Lopes in the Gate of the True Faith. Therefore we need you to resolve and answer for us how this opinion of the Kabbalists, that all our worship and our prayers are to Ze'ir Anpin and his soul, will agree with our holy Torah, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. And as for your anger that burned against me, and your saying that I ascribe corporeality to the sefirot, I also know no place for this in my words, for I said nothing that I did not find in their books. They said that the World of Emanation has in it a body, a soul and a garment. And it is not hidden from you that light, air and fire are subtle and light bodies. Moreover, they themselves explained their words, and said that the upper worlds and the partzufim above Arikh Anpin they did not speak of, only from Arikh Anpin and downward, since they had already been coarsened and revealed more. Behold, it is plain to you from their words that the sefirot they speak of were coarsened and revealed more than those above them, and they themselves admit that the sefirot they speak of were coarsened.

<sup>2:9</sup> Would that, my lord, you would inform me also, who governs all the hidden worlds, of which the Kabbalists did not speak, and who feeds and sustains them. Whether Ze'ir Anpin, this one in Emanation, is the one who feeds and sustains them, and to him they worship and bow down, or Ein Sof is their God, and to Him alone they worship; and we worship Ze'ir Anpin, for he feeds us, and he is our God, as the Kabbalists said. It follows from this that Ein Sof is the God of the upper ones and Ze'ir Anpin the God of the lower ones, and here we have two authorities, God forbid. And explicitly, some of them said: "all the great work of the LORD," by implication there is a small one. And our true Rabbis said, as cited in Menorat ha-Maor, chapter 143, that at the time of the giving of the Torah He tore open for them seven heavens and opened seven lands, and said to them, to Israel: "Understand the upper ones and understand the lower ones, and know that there is no God besides Me, neither among the upper ones nor among the lower ones: I am the LORD your God." And in Midrash Rabbah, Parashat Yitro, they said: "I am the LORD your God." Rabbi Abbahu said: "A parable of a king of flesh and blood who reigns; he has a father, or a brother, or a son. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am not so. I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God. I am the first, for I have no father. I am the last, for I have no son. And besides Me there is no God, for I have no brother." Thus far the wording of the Midrash, etc. The Rabbi Etz Yosef, of blessed memory, that is to say, "that a king of flesh and blood, his kingship is not complete, because he has a father, whom he must honor, and who shares the kingship with him, or he has a brother who has a share in the honor of kingship, or he has a son who exercises authority with him, and after him is heir to the throne. And the explanation: He has no father, for He is the First Cause. And He has no brother, for He is one, and has no second. And He has no son, in that the effects were not drawn from Him by nature, as a son is drawn from a father, as some thought (this is the view of the Kabbalists, who said that Ze'ir Anpin is a son of Abba and Imma, and he is a father to the effects that follow him, etc., and he has a sister or sisters, his nukvin) for according to that view he has no power to change any of the things, and his kingship is not complete. But the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'I am the LORD your God,' for this is His power to bring them out of the land of Egypt, since His kingship is complete and there is none who can stay His hand." Thus far his words.

<sup>2:10</sup> In the Yerushalmi, Shabbat, chapter Bemah Ishah, our Sages of blessed memory said: "'And the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.' Rabbi Reuven said: At that hour an angel came down and slapped that wicked one on his mouth, and said to him: 'Is your word right, and is there a son for him?' He returned and said: 'Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meishach and Abed-nego, who sent His angel and saved His servants.' 'His son' is not written here, but 'His angel.' Thus far." That is to say, Nebuchadnezzar the wicked thought that the angels are effects, descending in a chain of descent from him by nature, like a son from the father, according to the words of the Kabbalists concerning the sefirot of all the worlds, and likewise the souls; and for this the angel slapped him. And he returned and said: 'who sent His angel, etc.' Here you have it explicit, coming out of the words of Midrash Rabbah and the Yerushalmi, contrary to the words of the Kabbalists. And all that exists, the Holy One, blessed be He, brought into being in His kindness, something from nothing, from the first form down to a small gnat; and not that they are drawn from His essence, as the son comes into being by the power of the seed drawn from his father.

<sup>2:11</sup> The conclusion from all this is that no face or form is to be worshipped of all the created things that exist in the upper and the lower world, which the Name, may He be blessed, brought into being in His kindness. For to Him alone it is fitting to worship and to pray, and for this the commandment and the warning came at Sinai: "I am the LORD your God. You shall have no other gods," as the Rambam of blessed memory wrote in chapter two of the Laws of Idolatry. And in chapter three of the Laws of Repentance he wrote, and these are his words: "And these are those who have no share in the world to come, but are cut off and perish for the greatness of their wickedness and their sins, forever and ever: the heretics and the apikorsim, etc." And in the law that follows it he wrote: "Five are those that are called heretics. The one who says that there is no God, and no ruler of the world, and the one who says that there is a ruler, but they are two or more, and the one who says that there is one Lord, but He is a body and possessed of a form, and the one who says that He is not alone the first and the rock of all. Likewise one who worships one other than Him in order to be an intercessor between him and the Lord of the worlds. Each of these five is a heretic. Thus far." And the Rav Lechem Mishneh wrote on the fourth division that our Master wrote, "and the one who says that He is not alone the first, etc." The Ravad wrote: "like one who said, your God is a great painter, but He found for Himself great pigments, formlessness and void, and darkness and water and wind, and with them made what He made." Thus far, the words of the Ravad. And the Rav Lechem Mishneh explains that his intention is to add to the words of our Master that although he concedes that no cause preceded our God, for whose sake He came to be, but says that He created the world something from something, then this one is a heretic; see there. In our case, the belief of the new Kabbalah, as explained in their books, according to our understanding and the understanding of many great ones, wise of heart, among our Rabbis who separated from it, early and late, like the Ribash and Chavot Yair, cited in Pitchei Teshuvah and the other later authorities: in it have gathered and come three or four of these words that our Rabbis said, that whoever believes thus has no share in the world to come. First, a multiplicity of divinities: Ein Sof, and Adam Kadma'ah, and Adam Kadmon, and Atik, and Arikh Anpin, and Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva! Second, that they have a subtle body, namely light, and Ein Sof is a soul to these bodies. Third, that the worship is not to the First Cause, which they call Ein Sof, but to Ze'ir Anpin, which is the last cause among these causes. Fourth, that he is an intermediary drawing down the flow from those upper attributes, which are Atik, Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma, and they call him son of Abba and Imma, and he is also father to the Keter of Creation, according to the chain of descent of the worlds, in their opinion, the Merciful One save us.

<sup>2:12</sup> And this I have seen in your reply. And I will tell these words that split roofs, since you replied to my words that I said to you: how shall we set aside Ein Sof and the rest of the partzufim close to Ein Sof and worship Ze'ir Anpin? And your reply was, because the other attributes are some judgment and some mercy, and this one is composed of them all. And for this reason the Emanator wished to perform His actions through this vessel, etc. And you brought me an analogy from the bodily hand, which does all the tasks, while the head, which is above, does nothing. Also the power of speech, which is splendor, etc.; all these words of yours are nothing but astonishing words! I asked you about their saying that Ze'ir Anpin is our God, and we worship him, and you answer me from those who act upon us by the will of their Maker. Do we then worship all those who act upon us by the will of their Maker? And shall we say that they are our God? Surely the sun acts for us in many good actions: to shine for us, to warm the air and the earth, to make grass sprout, and to ripen the fruit. Shall we worship her? The moon and the stars too act upon the lower beings by the will of the Creator, may He be blessed, as it is said: "and from the precious things of the yield of the sun, and from the precious things of the growth of the moons." Shall we worship them? The earth, the water and the fire also act to sprout grass and trees and to raise them. And with fire we do all that we want: to bake and to cook all our food. And in most crafts one blows on a charcoal fire and brings out a tool for its work. Shall we worship one of them? And His will, may He be blessed, to perform His actions through intermediary agents is plain and clear in the verses. "Let the waters swarm, let the earth bring forth a living creature, let the earth sprout grass," and it is said: "He makes His messengers winds, His ministers a blazing fire," and more and more, in every case of one doing its errand. And yet, despite all this, the Name, may He be blessed, commanded us to worship Him alone, and warned us not to worship any one besides Him. And at the chosen assembly, when He revealed Himself on Mount Sinai, He gave His voice before His host: "I am the LORD your God … You shall have no other gods before Me." And it is said: "I am the LORD, that is My name; and My glory I will not give to another!" You and I stood before a craftsman who made us, and He did not wish us to worship another god, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), apart from Him, although he is His agent to perform some action. And why do we not heed His voice to worship Him, and go and worship Ze'ir Anpin, which He did not command us?

<sup>2:13</sup> As for your questions that you wrote, that one should ask about what the Rambam of blessed memory wrote: "Let him direct his heart toward the Shekhinah and pray," and in Moreh Nevukhim he wrote that the Shekhinah is a created light, etc. Behold, in your question you have revealed that you are wise in your own eyes and have not learned discipline. Is it, then, the way of one who is asked to question his questioner? In any case I will not withhold my quill from replying, even though you have not acted properly! And I say that it is plain and known to every learned man well versed in the books of Israel that the name Shekhinah is said of 3 things: either of the Name, may He be blessed, as our Master wrote in Laws of Repentance, chapter 7: "Great is repentance, which brings a person near to the Shekhinah, as it is said: 'Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God,' etc., and it is said: 'Yet you did not return to Me, says the LORD,' and it is said: 'If you return, O Israel, to Me you shall return.' That is to say, if you turn in repentance, you will cleave to Me, etc." Again there, on the excellence of repentance: "Yesterday this man was separated from the LORD, the God of Israel, etc., and today he is attached to the Shekhinah, as it is said: 'And you who cleave to the LORD your God,' he cries out and is answered at once, as it is said: 'And it shall be that before they call, I will answer.'" And so is the sense of his words in Laws of Prayer, that if he was in a place where he cannot determine the directions, etc. And so our forebears rendered it: "And if he is in a place and cannot tell the direction, let him direct his heart to his Creator and pray."

<sup>2:14</sup> And the second is in a place where the name "the revelation of the Shekhinah" is mentioned, for example, regarding Abraham our father when he went to bind Isaac, of whom it is said: "And he saw the place from afar." Our Rabbis of blessed memory said that he saw a light from afar on Mount Moriah, and as the liturgical poet said: "And he saw a likeness of glory, splendor and honor, and further asked his young men, 'A light: did you see it shining on the top of Mount ha-Mor?' etc." This is the created light that our Master wrote of. And so at the bush: "and he saw, and behold, the bush was burning with fire," and explicitly it is said there: "And the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the bush," and this is a created light. And so in every place where the name "the revelation of the Shekhinah" is mentioned, it is a created light.

<sup>2:15</sup> And the third: the providence of the Name, may He be blessed, over us is also called Shekhinah, as our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "They went into exile to Babylon; the Shekhinah was with them." That is to say, His providence, may He be blessed, clung to us, as He promised us in the Torah: "And yet even so, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them and I will not abhor them so as to destroy them, to break My covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God." And so it is with everything of the kind. Every place is to be understood according to its subject in one of these three mentioned aspects.

<sup>2:16</sup> And as for what you wrote: "And more than this, what he wrote about the glory of the LORD that it is created light, if so, how were Israel going out at the entrance of their tents and bowing down to the created thing?" Not to the visible glory do they bow down, but only to Him who made His glory dwell there. And the visible glory is there as a sign and a token for them, for the Name, may He be blessed, desired the tent of meeting as His dwelling, just as we bow down and pray to the Name, may He be blessed, toward the Temple and Jerusalem, for the LORD chose Zion; He desired it as His dwelling. And the Rambam had already explained in chapter 64 of the first, that the glory of the LORD sometimes denotes the created light, which the Holy One makes dwell in the place, as "and the glory of the LORD dwelt on Mount Sinai, and covered it, etc." and sometimes by it they mean His essence, may He be blessed, and His reality, as in "show me, please, Your glory," and the answer came: "for no man shall see Me and live," which shows that the glory spoken of here is His very essence, may He be blessed, and he said "Your glory," to magnify, etc. And similarly we find in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory that the name Elohim is equivocal, applying to judges and to angels, and to the Name, may He be blessed. Also, the name Shekhinah is equivocal, applying to what I mentioned above. And I saw fit to alert you here that there is no prohibition on bowing down to a man, so long as his intent is not to accept him as God, and he is not worshipped, but only submits to him and humbles himself before him, or by way of acknowledgment for a kindness that he did for him. For indeed Abraham our father bowed down to the sons of Heth for the kindness they did with him, to give him a burial place. And so Rabbi Saadia Gaon rendered: "and bowed down to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth, and prostrated to the people of the land that He created." And Joshua bowed down to the angel. And Nathan the prophet and Bathsheba bowed down to David. And we find much in the verses that they bowed down to the created being. And we read in Sanhedrin, chapter Four Deaths (Sanhedrin 61b): It was stated: "One who worships idolatry out of love and out of fear, Abaye says: he is liable, for he worshipped it. Rava says: he is exempt. If he accepted it upon himself as God, yes; if not, no. And Abaye said: How do I know this? for we learned: 'One who worships idolatry: one who worships, and one who sacrifices, and one who burns incense, and one who pours libations, and one who bows down, and one who accepts it upon himself as God, and one who says to him: You are my God.' What? Is it not that 'one who worships' means out of love or out of fear? And Rava says to you: No, but as Rabbi Yirmiyah resolves it: (Rashi explains: one who worships every worship that is customary for it, and one who sacrifices, etc., not in its customary way, and in every case the first clause and the last are for the sake of divinity). Abaye said: How do I know this? for it was taught: 'You shall not bow down to them; to them you do not bow down, but you bow down to a man like yourself.' One might think: even to worship like Haman? Scripture says: 'and you shall not worship them.' But Haman was worshipped out of fear! And Rava? Like Haman, and not like Haman. Like Haman, for he himself is idolatry; and not like Haman, for in the case of Haman it was out of fear, and here it is not out of fear. And Abaye said: How do I know this? for it was taught: 'An anointed priest in idolatry. Rabbi says: in an unwitting act, and the Sages say: in a concealed matter, and they agree that for a she-goat it is like an individual, and they agree that he does not bring a suspended guilt offering.' What is this unwitting act like? If he holds that it is a synagogue and bowed down to it, then his heart is with Heaven. But suppose he saw a statue and bowed down to it, (explanation: that he saw the figure of the king, which they were accustomed to make in the likeness of the king, and one who saw it bows down to it in honor of the king, and sometimes they worship it, and this one saw one who was worshipped and bowed down to it). If he accepted it upon himself as God, it is deliberate; and if he did not accept it upon himself as God, it is nothing. (Rashi explains: but he bowed down to him in honor of the king; it is nothing, for he did not intend idolatry). But is it not out of love and out of fear? And Rava says to you: In the case of one who says 'permitted.' Does 'says permitted' mean concealment of a matter? In the case of one who says permitted entirely; concealment of a matter is upholding part and nullifying part." Thus far the Gemara, with some of Rashi's explanation. And a matter is learned: that to every created being it is forbidden to bow down, except a man, provided that he not be worshipped like Haman, who made himself idolatry, (as we said in Megillah 19), for otherwise Mordecai would not have refrained from bowing down to him, as it is taught in the baraita: "You shall not bow down to them; to them you do not bow down, but you bow down to a man like yourself," provided that he not be worshipped like Haman, who made himself God, but one only bows down to him as a sign of honor, and not for divinity, and therefore Joshua bowed down to the angel, since he appeared to him in the form of a man, as it is written: "And behold, a man was standing opposite him," and therefore he bowed down to him as a sign of honor and not to worship him. And see in Sefer ha-Ikkarim, Treatise 2, chapter 28, where he elaborated on the verses that call the glory that appears to the prophets by the name YHVH, and also the ark, as it says: "And it was when the ark set out, etc. Arise, LORD, and when it rested he said: Return, LORD." And Joshua called the ark "Lord of all the earth"; see there. And in his view, that Joshua bowed down to the angel, because that bowing was in honor of the Name, may He be blessed, and since this one was His messenger, etc.; see there. And our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "Bow down to the fox in its time," that is to say: a man lowly and despised like a fox, and the moment stands for him in some office that is in his hand: bow down to him. And so it is customary with us and with the Arabs to bow down and kiss a man of high rank, and there is no prohibition in this, for he does not accept him as God; it is only as a sign of honor that he bows down to him and kisses his feet.

<sup>2:17</sup> And greater than this is what they also do: they sacrifice sheep and cattle before a king or a minister. It is one of the inner worships. Whoever does it for one of the kinds of idolatry, even though its worship is not in that way, is liable, as we learned in Sanhedrin, in the chapter “Four Death Penalties”: “The worshipper of idolatry: one who worships, and one who sacrifices, and one who burns incense, and one who pours libation, and one who bows down, etc.” And we say in the Gemara: On this: “What is ‘one who worships’?” Rabbi Yirmiyah said: “This is what it means: one who worships in the usual way, and one who sacrifices, and one who burns incense, and one who pours libation, and one who bows down, even not in the usual way.” And so all the decisors ruled that for the four worships one is liable even if not in the usual way. And this practice is still observed to this day among our brethren, the people of the villages and the towns: that if one of them had an enemy who seeks his harm, he brings a lamb and slaughters it before his minister, to save him from his enemy. And Scripture also says: “Offer it now to your governor, etc.” Our forebears also had this rule: when the king came to the province, they would sacrifice an ox before him, and they would take the price of the ox from the communal chest. And they heard of no one who doubted this on account of idolatry, since one does not intend to worship him by this or to accept him upon oneself as a god; it is only a sign of honor that one makes to him. Our father Jacob, peace be upon him, said to his sons: “Take of the choicest of the land's produce in your vessels, and bring down to the man a gift,” and it is said: “And they brought him the gift that was in their hands to the house, and bowed down to him, faces, etc.” And concerning Saul, the LORD's chosen one, it is said: “And sons of Belial said, ‘How can this one save us?’ and did not bring him a gift.” And in Nedarim we learned: “One who vowed by an offering and said, ‘I vowed only by the offerings of kings.’” So it is clear that bowing down, sacrifice, presenting a gift, and all four inner worships are permitted to do for a man who is not worshipped like Haman; but if he is worshipped like Haman it is forbidden, for Mordechai refrained from bowing down to Haman, because he made himself an object of idolatry.

<sup>2:18</sup> And in the book Teshu'at Yisrael by Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel he wrote, and these are his words: “I have been required to make known the customs of honor and submission with which the Jews honor the Torah scroll, for our enemies, who do not know what this is, provoke us, saying that we are worshippers of idols, and that we bow down to a wooden ark and to the sheets of skin within it. Therefore I shall set out my reply in proper order, as the good hand of the LORD is upon me, namely, every man of Israel will see himself obliged to rise and stand at the removal of a Torah scroll from the holy ark until it is placed on the reading platform, to show it to all the people and to read from it. And we find that they did so in the days of Nehemiah, as it is written: ‘And when he opened, all the people stood.’ And this they do out of the fear and honor with which they honor the words of the living God written in it, and for that same reason they bow their heads when carrying it from the ark to the reading platform, and not because of any other of the reasons that we shall mention.”

<sup>2:19</sup> The first: there is a great difference between one who worships and prays to something, and one who only honours something. To pray to something and to worship something with worship is forbidden to us, whether it be a man or an angel, corporeal or spiritual; but to bestow honour, as a youth honours an elder, a servant his master, and the lowly the honoured, is permitted. So too we find of our father Abraham, who believed in the LORD, that he shattered the monuments of idols and disowned them, and bowed down to the ground before three angels standing over him, even though they appeared to him as men. So too Joshua did at Jericho: when he saw a man standing before him and took him for an angel, he fell to the ground before him. And if men of understanding like them, in whose ways we walk and from the commandments of whose lips we do not shrink, did this, and it was not counted to them as a sin of idolatry; it is clear that to honour a Torah scroll is not the worship of idols.

<sup>2:20</sup> Second: the Jews are very careful in matters of other worship, and even to appear as one who honours it is forbidden to them. As they said in the Talmud and in the Rambam: "If a man turned aside from the road he was taking near a house of idolatry, and a thorn lodged in his foot, he may not bend, nor even kneel and bow down to remove it there, so that he should not appear in the eyes of passers-by as one who bows down and honours idolatry." And if the prostration before the Ark were like other worship, the Jews would not have kept this custom; and since they kept it from the days of their fathers, it is a sign of truth that it is not corrupted.

<sup>2:21</sup> Third: one of the customs of honour by which they once honoured idolatry was kissing. So too we find in Scripture: "And I will leave in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him." And it is said: "Those who sacrifice men kiss calves." And if it is so, will all who kiss the Torah scroll be worshippers of idols? But the matter is not so, for this is only honour, that they honour their Torah, and not worship; and therefore the prostration before the Ark is also only honour and not worship.

<sup>2:22</sup> Fourth: experience has taught us that in all the languages of the nations customs of honour are found, by which a man honours his fellow when they meet, and so they bow their heads, one opposite the other, and this too has been for us a sign that it is not the worship of idols, but customs of honour.

<sup>2:23</sup> "Fifth: the people who dwell in Asia, if a written command from the king comes to them, they take it in their hands, kiss it with their mouths and place it on their heads. How much more so shall we honor the words of the living God, King over all the earth.

<sup>2:24</sup> "Sixth: when the seventy-two elders brought the Torah to Ptolemy, king of Egypt, he rose from his throne and bowed down seven times to meet it, and if a worshipper of idols, who has not put his neck under the yoke of our Torah, honored it so much, how much more so we who enter into its covenant and to whom it was given as an inheritance.

<sup>2:25</sup> "Seventh: the foundations and principles of our religion are the existence of one, unique, eternal Creator, who is not a body, nor a force in a body, who gives the Torah to His people Israel through the faithful lawgiver Moses, servant of the LORD, master of all the prophets. He, may He be blessed, looks on and exercises providence over the worlds that He created. And His eyes roam over all, and He searches and examines the hearts of the sons of man and judges justly concerning the deeds of a man's steps. From Him alone we seek help in our distress, and He will bring forth a shoot from the stock of Jesse, who will gather the outcasts of Israel from the four corners of the earth, and from all the cut-off corners to which they scattered them there, the dry bones of their dead will live, and their corpses will rise. Indeed, all these are the principles and roots of our religion. And what trace of idolatry is found in them? Even in the opinion of those whose opinions and beliefs differ from our opinions and from our faith." Thus far his words.

<sup>2:26</sup> And according to our way, the way of our Rabbis of blessed memory in the aforementioned baraita, there is no need for all this, since our intention is not that we bow down before the Torah scroll, but to Him who chose the Torah. Explicitly, we say: "Come, let us bow down and bend the knee, let us kneel before the LORD our Maker." And as for the bowing down of Abraham our father to the angels, and so Joshua's, if you wish, say: since they appeared to them as men, we apply to them what the Rabbis said in the baraita: "'You shall not bow down to them.' To them you may not bow down, but you bow down to a man like yourself," since they were revealed to them in the form of men. And if you wish, say that the intention of Abraham and Joshua was to bow down to Him who sent them, and as the author of the Ikkarim wrote.

<sup>2:27</sup> And your question concerning prophecy, although it does not belong to our subject, and you asked only to mislead us and to divert us to another matter, behold, this is set out in the degrees of prophecy in the Rambam, Laws of the Foundations of the Torah, and in part two of the book Moreh Nevukhim, and in the book Emunot ve-De'ot of Rabbi Saadia Gaon. Since I have found you wise in your own eyes, I return to ask you to answer me a decisive answer from the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory in the Talmud, for you alone (in your opinion) all mysteries have been revealed to you, and extraordinary understanding and a new spirit have been given within you. Instruct us, I and my companions, how the matters can agree fully and well. For our soul has longed to hear your teachings, and to delight in your perfect Torah, and it will be to you a merit, and also great honor you will inherit from us.

<sup>2:28</sup> Reply. To man the arrangements of the heart, and from the LORD the answer of the tongue. And it was when I saw your letter, I sat astonished and dismayed. How your heart emboldened you to inquire and investigate after the band of the Geonim, who are faithful in the Torah, distinguished in lineage, like the seed of the mighty, and after several decisors and also expounders, the early and the later, the sages of the Maghreb, Ashkenaz, Sefarad and the Yemenites. And the rest of the congregations, the holy seed, the faithful children, this is their treasure, more than fine gold and many pearls. Can a stumbling come from the hand of righteous and faithful ones, who know knowledge, the wise and discerning, who fear God and turn aside from evil with their might. By their wisdom they felled many foes and multitudes who stood against them in every age. Can it be that their Kabbalah is compounded in vanity and errors, they who, because of their great wisdom, were approved by the mouths of princes and nobles and stood before kings and rulers, and can fathers and sons walk on a path that is not good? How many hundreds of years is this? And how many of them are distinguished in every wisdom, and scholars, Kabbalists with philosophy and logic, medicine, mathematics and astronomy, meditating day and night, quiet and at ease, eating the good fruit of their deeds, fat and lush. Heaven forbid! This is not to be believed and does not come to mind except to the simple, who believe every word, who lean on their understanding. And properly, it is not incumbent on me to answer you. For what am I, to enter the innermost, into what I was not permitted to ponder, all the more so to answer questioners. But because it is a time to act for the LORD, I answer you from what I found written in the words of our Sages of blessed memory. May their merit stand for me, that no stumbling befall through me. Now, as for what you wrote, that you do not despise the sages of Israel, there are already several witnesses against you; you cannot deny it. And as for what brought you to this, that you attribute to them error and heresy: it is only because they are despised in your eyes. But a person should take heed for himself, lest he be burned by their coals, for the righteous are greater in their death than in their life, as they said in the Talmud. And as for what you wrote, that if one reveals the place of contradiction, and the Talmud also brings proof to refute the words of those greater than them, the case is not comparable to the proof, for where do we find that they bring proof to refute a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai? And the sages of Kabbalah say that thus they received from the mouth of Moses, and who is this one, and where is he, who gave you permission to inquire and investigate after their words? And as for what you wrote, that they call the partzufim divinities, God forbid, that they say thus. And as for what you wrote, go and learn from the intention of the blessings and the prayers. They already explained that the Cause of all causes is designated in a certain sefirah by such a name, and in a certain sefirah by that name. And as for what you wrote, that the Kabbalists explained that there are several worlds, thousands of thousands, etc., even if they were millions of millions, since they say that their Creator is one, and He gives life to all of them: what loss is there from this? And as for what you wrote, that they are in the image of a man possessing stature, already they said, "Great is the power of the prophets, who liken the likeness of the Power above to the form of a man." And as for what you wrote about 248 limbs, they already explained what the limbs are. For they are 216 letters of the Name of 72 and 32 paths, which allude to divine powers. And as for what you wrote, that I already conceded that my opinion is that there is no prayer applicable to the Cause of all causes, you speak falsehood. But surely, from the beginning of your question to me about the words of the Mesharef, I answered you, see in Kisse Eliyahu. But our Kabbalah holds that prayer is to Ein Sof and to bestow the flow upon the ten sefirot, as Lechem Shelomo wrote. And as for what I told you, to consult Kisse Eliyahu, so that you would know that the words of the Mesharef are words of heresy, in truth, and fitting to root it out. And God forbid that there be found in any book words like his, but the words of Kisse Eliyahu are not like his, God forbid. For the words of Kisse Eliyahu hold that Ze'ir Anpin is nothing but a vessel for the action of the Creator. And as for what he wrote on folio 25, that when we call upon Ze'ir Anpin, we call upon all the partzufim, with a soul hidden in them, which is Ein Sof, blessed be He. This does not mean that prayer is not directed to Ein Sof, Heaven forbid, but it means that the ascent of prayer to Ein Sof, blessed be He, is by way of this attribute. And the proof for this is what he wrote on folio 17b, and these are his words: "As for what is written about the intentions of prayer and the blessings, to direct in each blessing a particular intention, to a particular sefirah, not, God forbid, to the essence of the sefirah. For it is a cutting off, God forbid, and Heaven forbid to direct it to any particular power or particular sefirah. But all is to the essence of the one Ein Sof, blessed be He, the totality of all the powers, all of them." And furthermore he wrote on folio 25a: "And all our prayers are to Ein Sof, may He be blessed. Except that we cannot call Him by any appellation and name. Therefore we pray through the sefirot. For there is the applicability of all, all the appellations and names. For all the appellations and names are names of His essence, extending through the sefirot." Also he wrote on folio 26: "And if they do not do so, and do not dedicate their prayer solely to Ze'ir Anpin, they will not be answered." And all the Kabbalists lay down this principle, and these are their words: "As for whatever you find in some book of theirs, that prayer is addressed to any sefirah, Heaven forbid that it be so. But the intention is that one intend to raise them to Ein Sof by way of that sefirah."

<sup>2:29</sup> I have gone on at length about all this, to reconcile for you the words of Kisse Eliyahu, but my tradition I have already mentioned above. And there is proof from this that what you ask me is not from the motive of your request for the truth, as you said, but rather to seek some pretext. And who am I that you should hold me to be a Kabbalist, for I am brutish and do not know. And all my prayers are not even like the chirping of birds, for the birds are fed without distress, and on them there lies neither the yoke of kingship nor the yoke of worldly occupation, and chirping can be done with intent, but I, under so much burden of the times and the cares of livelihood, have my mind and my thoughts confused. And furthermore, I have not received from a wise Kabbalist mouth to mouth. Would that the LORD relieve me of the troubles of time and of livelihood, and provide me a Kabbalist master who would set me on the paths of uprightness, and that I might merit to be among the sons of ascent. As for what I answered you the second time, it is the words of Kisse Eliyahu that you turned a blind eye to. And as for what you wrote, that you do not ascribe corporeality to the sefirot, but did you not write: "If so, there would be a force in a body"? And this time you say that light is a subtle body. And I already wrote to you that what they called them by the name light is only in order to accommodate the ear; one time you ascribe corporeality and another time you make excuses. And why do all these doubts come into your mind, except because you ascribe corporeality? As for what you wrote: "Who is it that governs all these hidden worlds?" The one who brings them into being is the one who keeps them alive. And as for what you wrote, that Ze'ir Anpin is found to be the god of the lower ones. Have I not written to you that he is nothing but a tool for the acts of the Creator? And as for what you wrote, that some of them said "all the great work of the LORD," from which it follows that there is a small one? Those who say so have themselves already explained that they meant Metatron, whose name is like his master's, as they said in the Talmud: "And to Moses He said, 'Come up to the LORD'; it should have said 'to Me'. But this is Metatron, whose name is like his master's"; and so it is in the Yalkut. And as for what you wrote, that our true rabbis said, it is cited in Menorat ha-Ma'or that at the time of the giving of the Torah the Holy One, blessed be He, tore 7 heavens, etc. And in Midrash Rabbah they said: "I am the LORD your God; I am the first and I am the last. I am the first, for I have no father, and I am the last, for I have no son; and besides Me there is no God, for I have no brother." Who is it that says he has a father, or a son, or a brother? Rather, you spread slander against the sages who say so, and they have already explained their words, of blessed memory, that all the epithets and the attributes are in the sefirot, to accommodate the ear. Go now and see what Mahari Gikatilia wrote in the introduction to Sha'arei Orah, and the divine Rabbi Menachem Rikanti, and Rabbi Y. Chayyim, and these are his words: "In sum, wherever you see things that are not fitting to say of the Creator, may He be blessed, such as measure of stature and the like, it is all said of the sefirot; and when you see them speak in the manner of praise and thanksgiving, it is all said of the Creator, may He be blessed, who is within them and outside them, for nothing limits Him; therefore one may not say of the Creator, may He be blessed, not right and not left, not face and not back, etc." See there. And as for what you wrote, that the opinion of the Kabbalists is that the sefirot descend in a chain, by nature like a son from the father, far be it that they said so. On the contrary, they said: "Far be it to believe or to bring to mind that the sefirot are part of Ein Sof that came out of it and descended from cause to effect, for it is a criminal sin. For Ein Sof is not divided into parts, God forbid, and it receives no addition and no diminution, but its existence is constant always, without any change whatever, and He originated them, an absolute origination."

<sup>2:30</sup> As for what you wrote, that Ze'ir Anpin is the son of Abba and Imma, and that he is the father of the effects that come after him, and he has a sister, his Nukva; all of it is a parable and an allusion concerning the sefirot. As for what you wrote, that no partzuf is to be worshipped, this is known on the lips of all the Kabbalists, and they have no need of your warning. As for what you wrote in the name of the Rambam: "Five are those called heretics, etc." Who is the one who says there is no God, or that there are two, or that He has a body, or that He is not the One alone, or that he worships another besides Him in order to be an intercessor, or the one who says he found ingredients, or the one who says the world was created something from something, God forbid. But a grudge has already risen in your heart, and you study the holy books, take the words in their plain sense, and rely on your understanding. And you forgot what the wisest of the wise said: "and do not lean on your understanding." Since you have already informed me that you understand, resolve my doubts, which I sent you and which I am about to send. As for what you wrote, that you understood that many and great men of wise heart, early and late, withdraw from it: God forbid that there be any sage who withdraws from it. And if there is one who withdraws from it, he himself admits openly that it is from his lack of knowledge of it. As for what you wrote, as the Ribash and the Chavot Yair wrote, you speak falsehood about them. And they are two valid witnesses to testify against you that you speak lies. And these are the words of the Ribash, in brief: "that Rabbi Peretz ha-Kohen did not speak of those sefirot and did not attach importance to them. Also he heard from his mouth that Rabbi Shimshon of Kinon used to say: 'I pray according to the understanding of this child,' that is, to remove from the hearts of the Kabbalists the idea that they pray at one time to one sefirah and at another time to another sefirah. Also in the Eighteen Benedictions they have, in each and every one, an intention toward a known sefirah. And all this is a very strange thing in the eyes of anyone who is not a Kabbalist like them, and they think it is the belief in duality. And he heard one of the would-be philosophers speaking in disparagement of the Kabbalists, and he would say: 'The Christians are believers in the Trinity, and the Kabbalists are believers in the tens.' And he asked the elderly sage Don Yosef ibn Shushan, who was a sage in the Talmud, who had looked into philosophy and was a Kabbalist, pious, great, and scrupulous in the commandments. And he said to him: 'How is it that you Kabbalists direct one blessing to one known sefirah and another blessing to another sefirah. Furthermore, is it so that there are divinities for the sefirot? That a man should pray to them?' And they answered him: 'God forbid that the prayer be anything but to the Name, may He be blessed, the Cause of causes; but one directs the thought to draw the flow to that sefirah which relates to the thing he asks for, just as you would say that in the blessing for the righteous one should direct to the sefirah called Chesed, which is the attribute of mercy, etc.' And he brought him a parable on this. He answered and said: 'And behold, very good.' And he said: 'I do not thrust myself into that wisdom, since I did not receive it from the mouth of a Kabbalist sage. And if I have seen commentaries on the secrets of the Ramban, they reveal a handbreadth and cover handbreadths.' And he said that a certain sage explained the Kabbalah not as the Ramban holds, and therefore he said that the words of that sage shall be his alone." And he ended his words. Therefore I say that one must not rely on such words, except from the mouth of a Kabbalist sage.

<sup>2:31</sup> Have you seen, to know that the Ribash's not getting involved in it is due to his not having received it from mouth to mouth, not due to any qualm as you say? And here you have the wording of the second witness, the Gaon, the author of Chavot Yair, of blessed memory, in very great brevity who was asked by a certain sage who spent his days in the Gemara and the decisors, and behold, a spirit rose within him and stirred him to study the Kabbalah for the exceeding excellence of its virtues, which is the soul of the Torah, and he saw several sayings of the Zohar that it is impossible to enter before the Holy King except by it, and the sages of the Talmud did not command about it, only warned not to expound it, "Do not inquire into what is too wondrous for you, etc." and he asked the Rabbi to free him from confusion, and he answered and said to him, "Woe is me if I advise you about withdrawal and cause slackening of hands and hindrance from this wisdom, which is without doubt the soul of the Torah and the root of faith, like wisdom and knowledge and understanding, and without doubt, whoever merits it is of the sons of ascent; happy is he, how good is his portion, and how pleasant is his greatness, beloved on high, etc." He cited the words of Yish'ar of Candia who went at very great length and gathered like sheaves to the threshing floor most of the opinions that preceded him to bring near and not to distance, against the book Bechinat ha-Dat, which sought to lead many astray! And he said that he found a peg fixed in a pillar of iron in a firm place to hang on to agree to receive a reward for withdrawal more than for inquiry in the book Shemen la-Ma'or, of the father of the Rav and these are his words, briefly: "And this matter that he wrote in the name of Rabbi Meir Gabbai, that everyone who has not received the secrets of the Torah from his master and thinks to weigh them in his mind transgresses the prohibition 'you shall not make for yourself a graven image', I said in my heart to call attention to the ways of people in our generation, I have seen infants who have not seen light, who say 'I am warm, I have seen light', hidden within them like leaven, chicks whose eyes had not opened, etc. And even the great ones on earth, whoever is sharp and diligent, expert in the chambers of the Torah, there is no strength in his intellect to grasp the chambers of light, except from the mouth of an elder and teacher. And these are the words of the Ramban in his introduction to the commentary on the Torah: 'And I hereby bring in a faithful covenant and it gives proper counsel to everyone who looks into this book, that he not suppose a supposition and not think thoughts about any matter of all the hints that I write in the secrets of the Torah, for I inform faithfully that my words will not be grasped by any reason or understanding except from the mouth of a wise Kabbalist into the ear of an understanding recipient. And the supposition about them is a folly of many harms, preventing benefit, etc.' And if you say that the commentary of the Ramban is different, since all his words are brief, by allusion, unlike other books of Kabbalah that explained their words, do you not see in Sha'arei Orah that he wrote on every page the phrase 'I hereby allude'? So too, in the book of Bachya, he was very brief and was accustomed to say in his own words 'and the wise will understand,' all the more so the book of the Zohar, which is closed and locked, and these are the words of Etz Chayyim in his introduction: 'Although certainly in the later generations they are sustained from this composition. There is no doubt that the waters of wisdom will not be revealed to any man by the power of contemplation according to their human intellect but only through a divine flow that flows upon him. And if the last of the Kabbalists went so far as to say that his words will not be grasped, how can it arise in the mind that human reason, especially of the people of our generation, this one, to understand and comprehend the words of the living God, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the voice of whose utterances is flames of fire and they are sealed with a thousand seals, etc. Therefore, men of understanding, hear me and do not break through to look at later books built according to their human intellect.' See there. And in my opinion, when a man sins in the musing of thought about the World of Emanation, his iniquity is too great to bear. Although many, and likewise perfect ones, of the later Kabbalists aroused the hearts of people greatly to the study of the Kabbalah and wrote that the one who withholds himself from studying Kabbalah is thrust out from his precinct and loses his world. It seems to me that they do not disagree, and surely whoever can learn from the mouth of a divine Kabbalist who will explain the matters to him as the Ari did for his disciples happy is his portion. And although the later ones permitted study from the books and understanding from one's own mind, 'better is the fingernail of the early ones, etc.' and 'sit and do not do' is better, for the danger to the body is graver, and all the more so to the soul, etc. And we may not inquire into hidden things but only to hear in the study of the plain meaning of Scripture and the reproof of moral instruction, to walk in the ways of the upright, for our knowledge is limited." Thus far the words of Shemen la-Ma'or, the proof from which is to agree to withdrawal, etc. And with all this I have revealed to you my opinion and do not rely on me, neither you nor another, for I am not fit to decide. And behold, I liken the study of this holy of holies to a journey to the Holy Land, for its virtue is known, as they said in the Talmud, that without it he is like one who has no God and like a worshipper of idols, and one who walks four cubits in the Land of Israel is a son of the world to come, and many praises. And even so, the Tosafot wrote in the name of Rabbi Chayyim that now it is not a commandment to dwell in the land, for there are many commandments dependent on the land which we are unable to fulfil, and further because of the danger of the roads, and because of the poverty there, which will lead him to transgress against his own will and the will of his Maker there. And if there is no expert before him and an excellent protection from all harm, it is good to refrain from this! Surely, too, who would deny the excellence of this wisdom, raised on high beyond compare, on condition that one who merits it learns it from the mouth of a Kabbalist who also received it from his master? And indeed it is true that I am astonished at books composed by later authors that brought sayings of the Zohar. And they raise difficulties about them and explain them according to their own judgment. Who gave permission to human reason to invent from the weighing of its own judgment the existence of three first ones and three tzachtzachot? For it is explained in the Zohar that there is a place that is not open to question, etc. and there is no proof from the saying of the Zohar and Sefer Yetzirah and R. M., who received from the mouth of the Elder of Elders and Elijah and the supernal holy ones, and all those children in the Zohar, the spirit of the LORD spoke through them and His word was on their tongue, and also the Ari and his disciples, who received from him mouth to mouth—from the mouth of the supernal ones the words came forth— and we, in our study of them, nothing comes to our mind except the reading of the words, which is not so with these later ones and with those who explain from their own judgment.

<sup>2:32</sup> And behold, my beloved, like my brother of blessed memory, the parable of the land of Israel, the referent, for the long journey toward the place of the Name in the grasp of the secret is the shortness of the one who grasps and the depth of what is grasped, and the multitude of propositions, which are preventing causes in every grasp of wisdom, and especially in the wisdom of Kabbalah, in several respects, and over all of them is the sin, which obstructs and separates between the intellect and the intelligible, etc., and indeed, even though the author of Pardes Rimonim, because of the greatness of his holiness and his piety, is very careful in many places, and warns greatly against a strange thought that is of division, and limit, and the composing of parables, etc., we too shall say: would that a spirit from on high be poured out upon us, that we might grasp and understand the matters without inclining from the truth and from the roots of the religion, etc. And by these, take this rule in your hand: all things that are forbidden in the books of the Kabbalists, which they mentioned without dispute on the matter and without inquiry, and their plain sense will be understood, and the joining of the things: bind them on a white tablet, and let them be frontlets between your eyes. And even when things are read before you that appear astonishing in themselves, or from the side that it seems, God forbid, that there is division, number, corporeality and change, you shall accept them in the faith of an artisan, and say in your heart that your mind is short, and your knowledge in the depth of understanding, without your doubting, God forbid, one of the roots of the religion that are stated in Yigdal and in several places, for even those fundamental ones, it is not possible to descend to their roots by human reason, etc. And now go and learn that it is forbidden to innovate and to understand a matter from what is written in the book, lest he not aim at the truth, however, to explain verses according to what the Kabbalists said, that the premise is agreed; only that on this he explains the verse, or says that there is an allusion in it, by means of gematria, or the initial and final letters of words. It is good and fine that he only say it as a possibility, without deciding the matter, etc., only let him not waste his time on them, and whatever the LORD has put in his heart, and it is well reasoned, sound, without strain, he should not cast it behind his back, but rather let him write it down for memory, and let it be in his eyes as one who finds great spoil, for it is a sign for his soul, a portion of God from on high, which has nourishment and access in a high place, and he will be called holy, and now, behold, I have revealed to you the secrets of my heart. And you, the king, in your reflection and your knowledge, holy and broad, tell me, please, your ways, and I will set aside my opinion before your opinion. Yair Chayyim Bakhrakh.

<sup>2:33</sup> Have you seen, to know the words of the Gaon Chavot Yair, how afraid and trembling he is to teach about separation, and relies on the words of the Gaon, the author of Shemen la-Ma'or, whose words were cited above, yet he is still afraid to say it outright, lest it slacken the hands from engaging in this holy wisdom, and how much he praises this wisdom, for one who merits it, to learn it from the mouth of a Kabbalist, and admits that anyone who holds himself back from studying it, after receiving it, is pushed away from his precinct; and also he permits engaging in the words of Kabbalah, and if he sees puzzling things before him, he should accept them in the faith of an artisan, and attribute it to the shortness of his understanding. If so, your two witnesses, the Ribash and Chavot Yair, will testify and bear witness against you that you invent things from your own heart; and where is his separation, that he separated, as you said? Did he not himself say, "Would that a spirit from on high were poured upon us," etc.? And I bring you proof that he merited the wisdom of Kabbalah, for in section 172 he wrote, and these are his words: "that it is possible there are further matters of secret and concealment in two verses, 'two thousand bath it held' and 'three thousand baths,' for at the sin of the first man three alefs were corrupted, of truth, of Adonai and of man, and there remained mat-din-dam against idolatry, illicit unions and bloodshed. And King David repaired truth; therefore he did not taste sleep at night, and did not manage to repair judgment, and also blood, as the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'You shall not build the house, for you have shed much blood; only your son Solomon, for peace, etc.' And Solomon repaired two alefs, and with the alef of his father, three alefs were repaired, and the matter of bat is known to the initiates, for the main flaw is there, and he further expanded on the secret of the matter there. And section 176, on the matter of one who feeds a man blind in one of his eyes, and with all this I protested, for it seems to me that in both cases there is room to distinguish. However, where there is another fitting and suitable one like him, for it is known that the 248 limbs are a throne and a likeness of the 248 supernal lights, and the 248 limbs of the soul. And so, in every such case the throne is flawed, for according to the hidden there are heaps upon heaps of secret mysteries in the parts of the body, and there is a lack of flow in the cup of blessing." The above-mentioned, too, in the colophon of the book, wrote that he made 635 responsa and gathered from them 232, the number of "Let there be light," and it has the gematria of the four fillings of YHVH, 72, 63, 45, 52: the son who is in Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva. And further, "Let there be light" is Yah ya'ir ("Yah will give light"). These are the sources of Tif'eret (Beauty) and Malkhut (Kingship) in Binah (Understanding), which is the light emanated on the first day. And he further expanded on many matters of secret and concealment. Also his father, the author of Shemen la-Ma'or, was a divine Kabbalist, for his verses were printed at the end of the book. And these are according to the Name of forty-two, and the twelve combinations of YHVH, and the twenty-four combinations of Adonai, and the Name of twenty-two. Also the true sage, the author of Menorat ha-Ma'or, was a divine Kabbalist, for in chapter 93 he wrote on "Baruch She'amar": "its way in it, the number of the ten, the ten, etc." And in chapter 95 he wrote: "Kaddish is not said with fewer than ten, and the reason is that with ten the holiness is completed, which is above the ten sefirot." And in chapter 133 he wrote: "When Jacob was going down to Egypt, he saw that the exile had begun in him and in his seed, and he feared it and sacrificed sacrifices to the Fear of his father Isaac, so that the attribute of judgment would not be stretched out against him; and did this at Beersheba, which is a house of prayer for his fathers, and offered peace-offerings to complete to him all the attributes, as they expounded: 'shelamim, which cast peace', to complete to him the attribute of Gevurah (Might)." And in chapter 147 he wrote: "It is found that the completeness of holiness is in the ten, which allude to the ten havayot, and they are the ten sayings by which the world was created." And in chapter 153 he wrote: "And in the way of truth, that in six days the LORD made, etc. and on the seventh day it is Sabbath, and it has no male mate, and the Assembly of Israel is its female mate, as it is said: 'and the earth,' and behold, it is the Eighth Day of Assembly, for there everything is held back. And this is their saying: 'The eighth is a festival in itself,' and it is the completion of the first, for it is the emanation of the first ones, and it is not in their unity, and whoever understands the havayot will be wise and find the truth." And in the colophon of the book he wrote: "And the fifth, I left out the grave matters, which are hidden and lofty, and there is no one who can attain them but a single individual in a generation." Thus he wished to write secret matters in his work, but because they are not fit for every person. Have you seen, to know that no one disputes the Kabbalah: neither the early ones nor the later ones, neither the many nor the individuals, neither the great nor the small. On the contrary, all agree that whoever merits Kabbalah from mouth to ear, there is no finer virtue for you than it, and that it is forbidden to expound and investigate it; but if he wishes, he should accept it in complete faith and not explain it by his human intellect. For he should attribute what troubles him to the shortness of his understanding, and not break through to think anything of the soul. And with this, all the words of the lowest of the low are complete. Seder. And you shall return and listen to the voice of the LORD.

<sup>2:34</sup> Reply. I ask of my God that He lead me in paths of straightness and rescue us from a lying lip, from a deceitful tongue. Teach me, LORD, Your ways; I will walk in Your truth. Unite my heart to fear Your name. And send Your light and Your truth; they will lead me to answer a word spoken in its settings. Roll reproach and scorn away from me, for I have kept Your testimonies. Even though princes sit and speak against me, Your servant meditates on Your statutes. Then I shall not be ashamed, when I do not turn aside from the way that our Rabbis of blessed memory taught us, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud and the true midrashim and the decisors who follow in their footsteps, on whom all the house of Israel lean. For they are the masters of the true tradition, who received from Moses our teacher the generalities and particulars of the Torah, upon which he stood at Sinai forty days and forty nights, and handed them to Joshua, and Joshua to the elders, etc., as is stated in tractate Avot. 1) And it is a holy duty incumbent on us to follow in their footsteps in everything that yields a practical difference in law: in all matters of forbidden and permitted, impure and pure, unfit and fit. All the more so in matters of the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, which is the great principle, and after it the tradition of all the commandments and how they are to be done, as the Tanna, peace be upon him, said: "Why did the section of Shema precede 'And it shall be, if you hearken, etc.!'" And any author of a book who comes to add to or subtract from their words, and all the more so to turn us from the faith of the holy Torah according to the tradition of our rabbis, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud, we will not hearken to him. And even if he performs signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, we will not turn aside from following the LORD our God, according to the tradition of our Rabbis of blessed memory, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud and the decisors who come after them and follow in their footsteps. And even if from heaven a bat kol calls, hearken to him, to depart from their tradition, we shall not heed it, as Rabbi Yehoshua said: "One does not heed a bat kol, for it is not in heaven."
