- Verse: Lev 26:44 ('And yet even so, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them ... for I am the LORD their God'); the author's text spells 'their enemies' and 'to destroy them' with an added vav.
- Rabbinic saying: 'They went into exile to Babylon; the Shekhinah was with them'; no source is given.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:16

> ומה שכתבת: ויותר מזה מה שכ' על כבוד ה' שהוא אור נברא אם כן כיצד היו ישראל יוצאים פתח אהליהם ומשתחוים לנברא? לא לכבוד הנראה משתחוים, רק למי שהשרה כבודו שם. והכבוד הנראה שם לאות וסימן להם, כי השי"ת איווה לאוהל מועד למושב לו, כמו שאנחנו משתחוים ומתפללים לשי"ת נכח המקדש וירושלם, כי בחר ה' בציון אוה למושב לו. וכבר ביאר הרמב"ם בפ' ס"ד מראשון, כי כבוד ה', פעמים רוצים בו האור הנברא אשר ישכינהו הק' במקום, כמו: וישכון כבוד ה' על הר סיני ויכסהו וכו', ופעמים רוצים בו עצמותו ית' ואמתתו, כמו "הראיני נא את כבודך", ובא המענה: "כי לא יראני האדם וחי", מורה כי הכבוד הנאמר פה עצמו ית', ואמר "כבודך" להגדיל וכו'. וכיוצא בזה מצינו בדברי רז"ל ששם אלהים משותף לדיינים ולמלאכים ולשי"ת, גם שם שכינה משותף למה שהזכרתי למעלה. וראיתי להעירך פה שאין איסור להשתחוות לאדם כל שאין דעתו לקבלו באלוה וגם אינו נעבד, רק נכנע לו ומשפיל עצמו לפניו, או דרך ההודאה על טובה שעשה לו. שהרי אברהם אבינו השתחוה לבני חת על החסד שעשו עמו ליתן לו אחזת קבר. וכן תרגם רבי סעדיה גאון: וישתחו לעם הארץ לבני חת, וסגד לאהל אלבלד שברא. ויהושוע השתחווה למלאך. ונתן הנביא ובת שבע השתחוו לדוד. והרבה מצינו בכתובים שהשתחוו לנברא. וגרסינן בסנהדרין פ' ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין ס"א ע"ב), אתמר: העובד ע"ז מאהבה ומיראה, אביי אמר חייב, דהא פלחה. רבא אמר פטור, אי קבליה עליה באלוה אין, אי לא לא. ואמר אביי מנא אמינא לה, דתנן העובד ע"ז אחד העובד ואחד המזבח ואחד המקטיר ואחד המנסך ואחד המשתחוה ואחד המקבלו עליו באלוה והאומר לו אלי אתה. מאי לאו אחד העובד מאהבה או מיראה? ורבא אמר לך, לא, אלא כדמתרץ ר' ירמיה (פירש רש"י: אחד העובד כל עבודה שהיא דרכה בכך, ואחד המזבח וכו' שלא כדרכה, ולעולם רישא וסיפא לשם אלהות). אמר אביי: מנא אמינא לה? דתניא: לא תשתחוה להם, להם אי אתה משתחוה, אבל אתה משתחוה לאדם כמותך. יכול אפי' לעבד כהמן? ת"ל ולא תעבדם. והא המן מיראה הוא נעבד! ורבא? כהמן ולא כהמן. כהמן, דאיהו גופיה ע"ז; ולא כהמן, דאלו המן מיראה, והכא לאו מיראה. ואמר אביי: מנא אמינא לה? דתניא: כהן משיח בע"ז. ר' אומר בשגגת מעשה, וחכמים אומרים בהעלם דבר, ושווין דבשעירה כיחיד, ושווין שאין מביא אשם תלוי. האי שגגת מעשה היכי דמי? אי קסבר ביהכנ"ס והשתחוה לו, הרי לבו לשמים. אלא דחזא אנדרטא והשתחוה לו (פירוש, שראה דמות המלך שהיו רגילים לעשות כדמות המלך והרואה אותו משתחוה לו לכבוד המלך, ופעמים שעובדין אותו, וזה ראה אחד שנעבד והשתחוה לו), אי קבליה עליה באלוה מזיד הוא, ואי לא קבליה עליה באלוה לאו כלום הוא (פירש רש"י: אלא לכבוד המלך השתחוה לו, לאו כלום הוא דהא לא איכוון לע"ז). אלא לאו מאהבה ומיראה? ורבא אמר לך: באומר מותר. אומר מותר היינו העלם דבר? באומר מותר לגמרי, העלם דבר קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת, עכ"ל הגמ' עם קצת פי' רש"י. ודבר נלמד, דלכל נברא אסור להשתחוות, זולת האדם, והוא שלא נעבד כהמן שעשה עצמו ע"ז, כדאמירן במגלה (יט), דאי לאו הכי לא היה מרדכי נמנע מלהשתחות לו, כדקתני בבריתא: לא תשתחוה להם, להם אי אתה משתחוה, אבל אתה משתחוה לאדם כמותך, והוא שלא יהא נעבד כהמן שעשה עצמו אלוה, רק משתחוה לו לאות הכבוד ולא לאלהות, ולכך השתחוה יהושע למלאך הואיל ונגלה לו בדמות אדם, כמ"ש: והנה איש עומד לנגדו, ולכן השתחוה לו לאות הכבוד ולא לעבדו. ועיין בס' העיקרים מאמר ב' פ' כ"ח שהאריך בביאור הכתובים שקורין לכבוד הנראה לנביאים בשם הוי"ה, וגם לארון, כמו שגאמר: "ויהי בנסע הארון וכו' קומה ה', ובנחה יאמר שובה ה'", ויהושע קרא לארון "אדון כל הארץ" ע"ש. ולדעתו שמה שהשתחוה יהושע למלאך, לפי שההשתחויה ההיא היתה לכבוד השי"ת, ולהיות זה שלוחו וכו' ע"ש. ורז"ל אמרו תעלא בעידניה סגיד ליה, ר"ל: אדם פחות ובזוי כשועל, והשעה עומדת לו באיזה משרה שבידו, סגיד ליה. וכן הוא נהוג אצלנו ואצל הערביים להשתחוות ולנשק אדם גדול המעלה, ואין בזה שום איסור, שאינו מקבלו עליו באלוה, רק לאות כבוד הוא משתחוה לו ומנשק את רגליו.

**And as for what you wrote: "And more than this, what he wrote about the glory of the LORD that it is created light, if so, how were Israel going out at the entrance of their tents and bowing down to the created thing?" Not to the visible glory do they bow down, but only to Him who made His glory dwell there. And the visible glory is there as a sign and a token for them, for the Name, may He be blessed, desired the tent of meeting as His dwelling, just as we bow down and pray to the Name, may He be blessed, toward the Temple and Jerusalem, for the LORD chose Zion; He desired it as His dwelling. And the Rambam had already explained in chapter 64 of the first, that the glory of the LORD sometimes denotes the created light, which the Holy One makes dwell in the place, as "and the glory of the LORD dwelt on Mount Sinai, and covered it, etc." and sometimes by it they mean His essence, may He be blessed, and His reality, as in "show me, please, Your glory," and the answer came: "for no man shall see Me and live," which shows that the glory spoken of here is His very essence, may He be blessed, and he said "Your glory," to magnify, etc. And similarly we find in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory that the name Elohim is equivocal, applying to judges and to angels, and to the Name, may He be blessed. Also, the name Shekhinah is equivocal, applying to what I mentioned above. And I saw fit to alert you here that there is no prohibition on bowing down to a man, so long as his intent is not to accept him as God, and he is not worshipped, but only submits to him and humbles himself before him, or by way of acknowledgment for a kindness that he did for him. For indeed Abraham our father bowed down to the sons of Heth for the kindness they did with him, to give him a burial place. And so Rabbi Saadia Gaon rendered: "and bowed down to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth, and prostrated to the people of the land that He created." And Joshua bowed down to the angel. And Nathan the prophet and Bathsheba bowed down to David. And we find much in the verses that they bowed down to the created being. And we read in Sanhedrin, chapter Four Deaths (Sanhedrin 61b): It was stated: "One who worships idolatry out of love and out of fear, Abaye says: he is liable, for he worshipped it. Rava says: he is exempt. If he accepted it upon himself as God, yes; if not, no. And Abaye said: How do I know this? for we learned: 'One who worships idolatry: one who worships, and one who sacrifices, and one who burns incense, and one who pours libations, and one who bows down, and one who accepts it upon himself as God, and one who says to him: You are my God.' What? Is it not that 'one who worships' means out of love or out of fear? And Rava says to you: No, but as Rabbi Yirmiyah resolves it: (Rashi explains: one who worships every worship that is customary for it, and one who sacrifices, etc., not in its customary way, and in every case the first clause and the last are for the sake of divinity). Abaye said: How do I know this? for it was taught: 'You shall not bow down to them; to them you do not bow down, but you bow down to a man like yourself.' One might think: even to worship like Haman? Scripture says: 'and you shall not worship them.' But Haman was worshipped out of fear! And Rava? Like Haman, and not like Haman. Like Haman, for he himself is idolatry; and not like Haman, for in the case of Haman it was out of fear, and here it is not out of fear. And Abaye said: How do I know this? for it was taught: 'An anointed priest in idolatry. Rabbi says: in an unwitting act, and the Sages say: in a concealed matter, and they agree that for a she-goat it is like an individual, and they agree that he does not bring a suspended guilt offering.' What is this unwitting act like? If he holds that it is a synagogue and bowed down to it, then his heart is with Heaven. But suppose he saw a statue and bowed down to it, (explanation: that he saw the figure of the king, which they were accustomed to make in the likeness of the king, and one who saw it bows down to it in honor of the king, and sometimes they worship it, and this one saw one who was worshipped and bowed down to it). If he accepted it upon himself as God, it is deliberate; and if he did not accept it upon himself as God, it is nothing. (Rashi explains: but he bowed down to him in honor of the king; it is nothing, for he did not intend idolatry). But is it not out of love and out of fear? And Rava says to you: In the case of one who says 'permitted.' Does 'says permitted' mean concealment of a matter? In the case of one who says permitted entirely; concealment of a matter is upholding part and nullifying part." Thus far the Gemara, with some of Rashi's explanation. And a matter is learned: that to every created being it is forbidden to bow down, except a man, provided that he not be worshipped like Haman, who made himself idolatry, (as we said in Megillah 19), for otherwise Mordecai would not have refrained from bowing down to him, as it is taught in the baraita: "You shall not bow down to them; to them you do not bow down, but you bow down to a man like yourself," provided that he not be worshipped like Haman, who made himself God, but one only bows down to him as a sign of honor, and not for divinity, and therefore Joshua bowed down to the angel, since he appeared to him in the form of a man, as it is written: "And behold, a man was standing opposite him," and therefore he bowed down to him as a sign of honor and not to worship him. And see in Sefer ha-Ikkarim, Treatise 2, chapter 28, where he elaborated on the verses that call the glory that appears to the prophets by the name YHVH, and also the ark, as it says: "And it was when the ark set out, etc. Arise, LORD, and when it rested he said: Return, LORD." And Joshua called the ark "Lord of all the earth"; see there. And in his view, that Joshua bowed down to the angel, because that bowing was in honor of the Name, may He be blessed, and since this one was His messenger, etc.; see there. And our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "Bow down to the fox in its time," that is to say: a man lowly and despised like a fox, and the moment stands for him in some office that is in his hand: bow down to him. And so it is customary with us and with the Arabs to bow down and kiss a man of high rank, and there is no prohibition in this, for he does not accept him as God; it is only as a sign of honor that he bows down to him and kisses his feet.**

Grammar:

- The paragraph is the respondent's reply in the correspondence of chapter 2. 'What you wrote' answers the questioner, and the question from 'And as for what you wrote' to 'created thing?' is his.
- The main sense turns on the Bavli passage (Sanhedrin 61b), Bavli Aramaic, quoted from 'It was stated' to 'Thus far the Gemara'. Its Aramaic forms are glossed in the tokens (פלחה, קבליה, דהא, אי ... אין). The author's two Rashi glosses and his explanation of the statue are in parentheses inside it.
- The Hebrew for 'not to the visible glory do they bow down' puts the negated object first. The English keeps that order, and 'but only' (רק) then answers it.
- שהשרה is causative (made dwell): 'to him who made His glory dwell there'. The verse cited, Exod 24:16, is cut short by the author's 'וכו'', and the English keeps the 'etc.'.
- Two verbs carry the argument: נעבד (passive, 'is worshipped') and נכנע ('submits'). The author separates bowing as worship from bowing as submission or thanks, so the English keeps the two apart.
- Saadia's rendering of Gen 23:7 is Judeo-Arabic in Hebrew letters: וסגד לאהל אלבלד is Arabic 'and he prostrated to the people of the land' (אהל is ahl, 'people of'); the word שברא after it is unexplained.
- משותף is the Maimonidean term for an equivocal word; the author says the names אלהים and שכינה each name several things, which is why a created thing may be called 'glory' and the bowing in Exod 33 is to the One who caused it to dwell.

Note: The reply quotes the questioner and the Gemara, and its Saadia and Joshua examples are kept as the author gives them.

Other readings:

- לעבד כהמן: a slave like Haman (plain reading of לעבד as a noun). The unpointed לעבד may be 'to a slave'; the answer, 'and you shall not worship them', favours 'to worship' or 'to one worshipped'.

Ancient Near East:

- The anderta (אנדרטא) in the Gemara quotation is an image or statue; the author's Rashi gloss reads it as 'a figure of the king'.
- The anointed priest (כהן משיח) of the Gemara quotation is the priest anointed for office (Lev 4:3).
- Gen 23 tells of Abraham's purchase of a burial place from the sons of Heth (Gen 23:3-20).

Apparatus:

- Base text: Wikisource. Its additions are translated as base text and flagged here until the 1931 scan is collated (decisions, Q2).
- Exod 33:8 and 33:10 (the people rising and bowing down, each at the door of his tent), echoed by the questioner's 'יוצאים פתח אהליהם ומשתחוים'.
- Ps 132:13 (embedded, no marks): 'כי בחר ה' בציון אוה למושב לו'.
- Exod 24:16 ('וישכון כבוד ה' על הר סיני ויכסהו'), cited with 'וכו''.
- Exod 33:18 ('הראיני נא את כבודך') and Exod 33:20 ('כי לא יראני האדם וחי').
- Num 10:35-36 ('ויהי בנסע הארון ... קומה ה' ... ובנחה יאמר שובה ה''), cited with 'וכו''.
- Josh 3:11 ('אדון כל הארץ'), the author's name for the ark, cited with 'ע"ש'.

- Gen 23:7: 'וישתחו לעם הארץ לבני חת' (and the kindness of Gen 23:4, 'אחזת קבר'); Saadia's rendering (Judeo-Arabic in Hebrew letters) is translated from the words as they stand: אהל is Arabic ahl, 'people of'. The word 'שברא' is not clear; 'that He created' is the translator's reading and the alternative is not known.
- 1 Kgs 1:16 and 1:23 (Bathsheba and Nathan bowing to David).
- Exod 20:5: 'לא תשתחוה להם ולא תעבדם' (the Baraita in the Gemara, and the author's quotation of it).
- Witness spelling 'שגאמר' (2:16.559) for 'שנאמר', translated as the evident word; and 'לעבד' (2:16.313) may be read 'to worship' or 'to a slave' (see readings).

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:17

> וגדולה מזו שעושים גם כן לזבוח לפני מלך או שר צאן ובקר והיא מעבודות שבפנים שהעושה לאחד ממיני ע"ז אף שאין עבודתה בכך חייב כדתנן בסנהדרין פ' ד' מיתות העובד ע"ז אחד העובד, ואחד המזבח, ואחד המקטר ואחד המנסך, ואחד המשתחוה וכו' ואמרינן בגמ' עלה מאי אחד העובד? אמר ר' ירמיה הכי קאמר אחד העובד כדרכה, ואחד המזבח ואחד המקטר ואחד המנסך ואחד המשתחוה, ואפי' שלא כדרכה. וכן פסקו כל הפוסקים דארבע עבודות חייב עליהן אפי' שלא כדרכה. ודבר זה נהוג עד היום אצל אחינו בני הכפרים והעירות שאם היה לאחד מהם אויב שהוא מבקש רעתו הוא מביא כבש ושוחטו לפני השר שלו להושיעו מאויבו. וקרא נמי כתיב: הקריבהו נא לפחתך וכו'. קדמונינו היה עליהם ג"כ החק הזה בבוא המלך אל המדינה לזבוח לפניו שור ונוטלים את דמי השור מקופה של צבור. ולא שמעו שום מפקפק בזה משום ע"ז, לפי שאין מכוין לעבדו בזה ולקבלו עליו באלוה, רק אות כבוד הוא עושה לו. ויעקב אבינו ע"ה אמר לבניו: קחו מזמרת הארץ בכליכם והורידו לאיש מנחה, ונאמ': ויביאו לו את המנחה אשר בידם הביתה וישתחו לו אפים וכו'. ובשאול בחיר ה' נאמר: ובני בליעל אמרו מה יושיענו זה ולא הביאו לו מנחה. ובנדרים שנינו: נדר בקרבן ואמר לא נדרתי אלא בקרבנות מלכים. אלמא שהשתחויה וזיבוח והגשת מנחה וכל ארבע עבודות פנים מותר לעשותן לאדם שאינו נעבד כהמן, שאם הוא נעבד כהמן אסור, שכן נמנע מרדכי להשתחות להמן מפני שעשה עצמו ע"ז.

**And greater than this is what they also do: they sacrifice sheep and cattle before a king or a minister. It is one of the inner worships. Whoever does it for one of the kinds of idolatry, even though its worship is not in that way, is liable, as we learned in Sanhedrin, in the chapter “Four Death Penalties”: “The worshipper of idolatry: one who worships, and one who sacrifices, and one who burns incense, and one who pours libation, and one who bows down, etc.” And we say in the Gemara: On this: “What is ‘one who worships’?” Rabbi Yirmiyah said: “This is what it means: one who worships in the usual way, and one who sacrifices, and one who burns incense, and one who pours libation, and one who bows down, even not in the usual way.” And so all the decisors ruled that for the four worships one is liable even if not in the usual way. And this practice is still observed to this day among our brethren, the people of the villages and the towns: that if one of them had an enemy who seeks his harm, he brings a lamb and slaughters it before his minister, to save him from his enemy. And Scripture also says: “Offer it now to your governor, etc.” Our forebears also had this rule: when the king came to the province, they would sacrifice an ox before him, and they would take the price of the ox from the communal chest. And they heard of no one who doubted this on account of idolatry, since one does not intend to worship him by this or to accept him upon oneself as a god; it is only a sign of honor that one makes to him. Our father Jacob, peace be upon him, said to his sons: “Take of the choicest of the land's produce in your vessels, and bring down to the man a gift,” and it is said: “And they brought him the gift that was in their hands to the house, and bowed down to him, faces, etc.” And concerning Saul, the LORD's chosen one, it is said: “And sons of Belial said, ‘How can this one save us?’ and did not bring him a gift.” And in Nedarim we learned: “One who vowed by an offering and said, ‘I vowed only by the offerings of kings.’” So it is clear that bowing down, sacrifice, presenting a gift, and all four inner worships are permitted to do for a man who is not worshipped like Haman; but if he is worshipped like Haman it is forbidden, for Mordechai refrained from bowing down to Haman, because he made himself an object of idolatry.**

Grammar:

- שעושים לזבוח: the relative clause שעושים ('that they do') governs the infinitive לזבוח ('to sacrifice'); the object is 'sheep and cattle' and the place is 'before a king or a minister'. והיא refers back to that act, and עבודות פנים is the Mishnah's term for the inner worships.
- Bavli Aramaic: ואמרינן ('and we say'), עלה ('on it', the Mishnah), מאי ('what is'), הכי קאמר ('this is what he means'); the Gemara asks what the Mishnah's first 'one who worships' means, and Rabbi Yirmiyah answers.
- Mishnaic Hebrew: the Mishnah's list has four participles with ה: העובד, המזבח ('one who sacrifices'), המקטר ('one who burns incense'), המנסך ('one who pours libation'), and המשתחוה. The Mishnah quotation is cut off by וכו'; the words ואפי' שלא כדרכה ('even not in the usual way') belong to Rabbi Yirmiyah's explanation, and the author repeats them in his own ruling.
- בסנהדרין פ' ד' מיתות: ד' stands for ארבע, so the words are the title of the chapter, 'Four Death Penalties'; the English does not turn it into 'chapter four'.
- נעבד (passive, 'is worshipped'), נמנע ('refrained') and the adjective אסור ('forbidden') carry the last sentences; the English keeps the passive, and the participle ונוטלים ('and they take') is habitual.
- שאם היה לאחד מהם אויב ... הוא מביא: a past verb in the conditional clause and a present verb in the main clause, with a habitual sense: 'if one of them had an enemy, he brings'.

Note: The Mishnah's list and Rabbi Yirmiyah's gloss are given as the author quotes them; המזבח is 'one who sacrifices'. 'Idolatry' and 'inner worships' follow the fixed terms. פ' ד' מיתות is read as the chapter's title, 'Four Death Penalties' (ד' = ארבע), not as 'chapter four'.

Other readings:

- פ ד מיתות: chapter four, death penalties (plain numeral). The letters could be read as the numeral 4 followed by מיתות; the English reads ד' as ארבע, the chapter's title.
- לעבדו: to serve him (plain sense of עבד). עבד also means serve a master; here, with ולקבלו עליו באלוה, it is the worship due to a god.
- באלוה: as God (ruling on אלוה). The ruling on singular אלוה would give 'God'; kept as 'a god' because the king is the object.

Apparatus:

- Mal 1:8: 'הקריבהו נא לפחתך' (Offer it now to your governor), quoted by the author with וכו'.
- Gen 43:11: 'קחו מזמרת הארץ בכליכם והורידו לאיש מנחה' (Take of the choicest of the land's produce in your vessels and bring down to the man a gift).
- Gen 43:26: 'ויביאו לו את המנחה אשר בידם הביתה'; the verse continues 'וישתחוו לו ארצה'. The author's 'וישתחו לו אפים וכו'' has the wording of Gen 42:6 ('וישתחוו לו אפים ארצה'); the English follows his wording.
- 1 Sam 10:27: 'ובני בליעל אמרו מה יושיענו זה ולא הביאו לו מנחה'; the verse has an extra clause, 'ויבזהו', before 'ולא הביאו' that the author omits, and the English omits it too.
- 'בחיר ה'' for Saul echoes 2 Sam 21:6 ('Saul, the chosen of the LORD').
- Esth 3:2: Mordechai's refusal to bow to Haman, given by the author in his own words.
- The Mishnah of Sanhedrin is cited as 'פ' ד' מיתות', read as the chapter's title 'Four Death Penalties'; the reference is kept as written and none is added.
- The quotation from Nedarim gives no reference, and none is added.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:18

> ובס' תשועת ישראל לר' מנשה בן ישראל כ' וז"ל: נדרשתי להודיע מנהגי הכבוד והכניעות אשר יכבדו בם היהודים את ספר התורה, כי צרינו אשר אינם יודעים מה זאת מכעיסים אותנו לאמר כי עובדי אלילים אנחנו, וכי נשתחוה לארון עץ וליריעות עור אשר בתוכה, לכן אערוך תשובתי בסדר הניאות כיד ה' הטובה עלי והוא כל איש ישראל יראה את עצמו מחוייב לקום ולעמוד בהוצאת ספר תורה מארון הקודש עדי תונח על התיבה להראותה לכל העם ולקרות בה. ומצינו כי כן עשו בימי נחמיה ככתוב וכפתחו עמדו כל העם. וזאת יעשו מפני היראה והכבוד אשר יכבדו דברי אלהים חיים הכתובים בה, ומאותו טעם יכופו ראשם בנשאם אותה מהארון עד התיבה, ולא משום דבר אחר מן הטעמים אשר נזכיר.

**And in the book Teshu'at Yisrael by Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel he wrote, and these are his words: “I have been required to make known the customs of honor and submission with which the Jews honor the Torah scroll, for our enemies, who do not know what this is, provoke us, saying that we are worshippers of idols, and that we bow down to a wooden ark and to the sheets of skin within it. Therefore I shall set out my reply in proper order, as the good hand of the LORD is upon me, namely, every man of Israel will see himself obliged to rise and stand at the removal of a Torah scroll from the holy ark until it is placed on the reading platform, to show it to all the people and to read from it. And we find that they did so in the days of Nehemiah, as it is written: ‘And when he opened, all the people stood.’ And this they do out of the fear and honor with which they honor the words of the living God written in it, and for that same reason they bow their heads when carrying it from the ark to the reading platform, and not because of any other of the reasons that we shall mention.”**

Grammar:

- נדרשתי להודיע: a niphal perfect, 'I have been required', with the infinitive להודיע, 'to make known'; the first person is the letter-writer's, quoted by the author.
- ככתוב וכפתחו עמדו כל העם: וכפתחו is a temporal clause ('when he opened'); עמדו is third plural, 'they stood'; the quotation is inside the quoted letter, so it takes single marks.
- והוא כל איש ישראל יראה: והוא introduces the content ('namely'); יראה is a yiqtol with a future sense, 'will see himself obliged'.
- ולא משום דבר אחר מן הטעמים אשר נזכיר: the last clause denies every other reason, so the reasons given are the only ones; the witness has no closing formula, and the quotation runs to the end of the paragraph.

Note: The letter is the one Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel is quoted as writing; 'the reading platform' renders tevah. The witness has no closing formula, so the quotation runs to the end of the paragraph.

Apparatus:

- Allusion to Neh 2:8 ('כיד אלהי הטובה עלי'; cf. Ezra 7:9, 8:18, 7:28); the English follows the author's wording.
- Allusion to Jer 23:36 ('דברי אלהים חיים'; cf. Jer 10:10, Deut 5:23 for 'אלהים חיים').
- Neh 8:5: the author writes 'וכפתחו עמדו כל העם'; his wording is followed.
- The title of the book is transliterated per the project scheme; its meaning is at token 2.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:19

> האחד הפרש גדול בין העובד ומתפלל לאיזה דבר, ובין המכבד איזה דבר לבד. להתפלל ולעבוד עבודה לאיזה דבר אסור לנו, יהיה אדם או מלאך, גשם או רוחני אבל לחלוק כבוד כמו שיכבד הנער את הזקן, העבד את אדוניו, והנקלה לנכבד מותר. וכן מצאנו באברהם אבינו אשר האמין בה' רצץ ושבר מצבות אלילים וכיחש בם, השתחווה ארצה לפני שלשה מלאכים הנצבים עליו אף כי נדמו לו לאנשים. וכן עשה יהושע ביריחו בראותו איש עומד לנגדו ויחשבהו למלאך נפל לפניו ארצה ואם אנשי לבב כמוהם אשר בדרכיהם נלך וממצות שפתותיהם לא נבוש עשו זאת ולא נחשב להם לעון ע"ז ברור הוא כי לכבד ספר תורה אינה עבודת גילולים.

**The first: there is a great difference between one who worships and prays to something, and one who only honours something. To pray to something and to worship something with worship is forbidden to us, whether it be a man or an angel, corporeal or spiritual; but to bestow honour, as a youth honours an elder, a servant his master, and the lowly the honoured, is permitted. So too we find of our father Abraham, who believed in the LORD, that he shattered the monuments of idols and disowned them, and bowed down to the ground before three angels standing over him, even though they appeared to him as men. So too Joshua did at Jericho: when he saw a man standing before him and took him for an angel, he fell to the ground before him. And if men of understanding like them, in whose ways we walk and from the commandments of whose lips we do not shrink, did this, and it was not counted to them as a sin of idolatry; it is clear that to honour a Torah scroll is not the worship of idols.**

Literal: the-first the-difference great between the-worshipper and-the-prayer to-some-thing, and-between the-honourer some-thing only. to-pray and-to-worship worship to-some-thing forbidden to-us, be-it man or angel, corporeal or spiritual; but to-bestow honour, as the-youth honours the-elder, the-servant [object] his-master, and-the-lowly to-the-honoured is-permitted. and-so we-found in-Abraham our-father who believed in-the-LORD, shattered and-broke monuments-of idols and-disowned them, bowed-down to-the-ground before three angels the-standing over-him, even-though they-appeared to-him as-men. and-so Joshua did at-Jericho when-he-saw a-man standing before-him and-took-him for-an-angel, fell before-him to-the-ground. and-if men-of heart like-them in-whose-ways we-walk and-by-commandments-of their-lips not we-shrink-from did this, and-not was-counted to-them as-sin idolatry; clear it-is that to-honour a-scroll-of the-Torah is-not the-worship-of idols.

Grammar:

- בין ... ובין frames the contrast: the second half is elliptical, so 'one who only honours' is set against 'one who worships and prays'.
- ולעבוד עבודה: the verb and its noun share a root; the English keeps 'worship' for both, as the Hebrew does.
- כמו שיכבד הנער את הזקן: the comparison gives the model of honour the author permits; the paragraph's argument turns on the difference between the two.
- ואם אנשי לבב ... עשו זאת ... ברור הוא כי: the 'if' clause gives the case of the patriarchs and Joshua; the main clause is 'it is clear that'.

Apparatus:

- Text translated from Wikisource as the base text; not yet collated with the 1931 scan.
- Gen 15:6: 'אשר האמין בה'' echoes 'והאמן בה''.
- Gen 18:2: the verse behind 'השתחווה ארצה לפני שלשה מלאכים' (Abraham bows to the ground before the three men); the author calls them angels.
- Josh 5:13-14: the verse behind Joshua's falling to the ground before the man who stands before him.
- Job 34:10: אנשי לבב, 'men of understanding'.
- Job 23:12: cf. 'מצות שפתיו ולא אמיש'; the printed נבוש may be a variant of נמוש (see the note on 2:19.90).

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:20

> שנית היהודים נזהרים מאד בענייני עבודה אחרת, ואף להראות כמכבדה אסור להם. כמו שאמרו בתלמוד וברמב"ם אם לפת איש ארחות דרכו אצל בית ע"ז וישב לו קוץ ברגלו לא ישח אף לא יכרע וישתחוה להוציאו שם למען לא יתראה בעיני העוברים כמשתחוה ומכבד לע"ז, ואם היתה ההשתחויה לפני הארון כעבודה אחרת לא היו היהודים מחזיקים במנהג זה, וכיון שהחזיקו בו מימי אבותיהם אות אמת הוא כי אינה משובשת.

**Second: the Jews are very careful in matters of other worship, and even to appear as one who honours it is forbidden to them. As they said in the Talmud and in the Rambam: "If a man turned aside from the road he was taking near a house of idolatry, and a thorn lodged in his foot, he may not bend, nor even kneel and bow down to remove it there, so that he should not appear in the eyes of passers-by as one who bows down and honours idolatry." And if the prostration before the Ark were like other worship, the Jews would not have kept this custom; and since they kept it from the days of their fathers, it is a sign of truth that it is not corrupted.**

Literal: second the-Jews are-careful very in-matters-of worship other, and-even to-appear as-honouring-it forbidden to-them. as they-said in-the-Talmud and-in-the-Rambam: if turned-aside a-man the-paths-of his-way near a-house-of idolatry, and-lodged in-him a-thorn in-his-foot, not bend, even not kneel and-bow-down to-remove-it there, so-that not appear in-the-eyes-of the-passers-by as-bowing-down and-honouring idolatry; and-if was the-prostration before the-Ark like-worship other; not would-be the-Jews keeping in-the-custom of-this, and-since they-kept in-it from-the-days-of their-fathers, a-sign of-truth it that it-is-not corrupted.

Grammar:

- כמו שאמרו בתלמוד וברמב"ם: the formula אמרו introduces the passage that follows, which is therefore in quotation marks; no reference is given.
- לא ישח אף לא יכרע וישתחוה להוציאו: the negative governs all three verbs: he may not stoop, nor even kneel and bow down; the clause 'so that he should not appear' gives the reason.
- ואם היתה ... לא היו היהודים מחזיקים: a counterfactual, both clauses in the past; the author argues from what the Jews would not have done.
- וכיון שהחזיקו בו מימי אבותיהם אות אמת הוא כי אינה משובשת: the argument from custom; 'since they kept it' is causal, and 'that it is not corrupted' gives the sign's content.

Ancient Near East:

- The Ark (הארון): the cabinet in the synagogue in which the Torah scrolls are kept; the custom the author describes is bowing before it.

Apparatus:

- Job 6:18: cf. 'ילפתו ארחות דרכם' (they turn aside the paths of their way), the source of the wording לפת ארחות דרכו.
- The author names no tractate or chapter for the Talmud and Rambam passage.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:21

> שלישית אחד ממנהגי הכבוד אשר כבדו לפנים את הע"ז היה הנשיקה וכן מצינו במקרא והשארתי בישראל שבעת אלפים כל הברכים אשר לא כרעו לבעל וכל הפה אשר לא נשק לו, ונאמר זובחי אדם עגלים ישקון. ואם כן הוא יהיו כל המנשקים את ספר התורה עובדי ע"ז? אבל לא כן הדבר, כי אין זה רק כבוד שיכבדו את תורתם ולא עבודה, ולכן ההשתחויה מול הארון הוא ג"כ רק כבוד ולא עבודה.

**Third: one of the customs of honour by which they once honoured idolatry was kissing. So too we find in Scripture: "And I will leave in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him." And it is said: "Those who sacrifice men kiss calves." And if it is so, will all who kiss the Torah scroll be worshippers of idols? But the matter is not so, for this is only honour, that they honour their Torah, and not worship; and therefore the prostration before the Ark is also only honour and not worship.**

Literal: third one of-the-customs-of the-honour which they-honoured formerly [object] the-idolatry was the-kissing. and-so we-found in-Scripture: and-I-will-leave in-Israel seven-thousand, all the-knees which not bowed to-Baal, and-every the-mouth which not kissed to-him; and-it-is-said: sacrificers-of men calves they-kiss. and-if so it-is will-be all the-kissers [object] scroll-of the-Torah worshippers-of idols? but the-matter not so, for not is this only honour that they-honour [object] their-Torah, and-not worship; and-therefore the-prostration before the-Ark it also only honour and-not worship.

- ואם כן הוא יהיו כל המנשקים ... עובדי ע"ז?: a question about the future, answered by 'but this is not so'.
- כי אין זה רק כבוד שיכבדו את תורתם ולא עבודה: 'for this is only honour, that they honour their Torah and not worship' explains 'this'.

Ancient Near East:

- Baal: the god of the Canaanites, whose worship Elijah opposed (1 Kgs 18); the verse the author quotes is set in that story.

Apparatus:

- 1 Kgs 19:18: quoted in the verse's own words.
- Hos 13:2: the author writes זובחי, the verse זבחי; ישקון may also be read as a wish, 'let them kiss calves'.

Grammar:

- The paragraph is the fifth point of a numbered series, and its number opens the English as it opens the Hebrew.
- The conditional אם takes yiqtol verbs (they take, kiss, place): these describe a habitual practice, so the English uses the present.
- The argument is from the lesser to the greater (qal wa-chomer): if the people honor a king's written command, 'how much more so' the words of God. נכבד, with the pronoun אנו before it, is the plain imperfect, 'we shall honor'.
- The three acts (seizing in the hands, kissing with the mouth, placing on the head) are parallel clauses, and the English keeps their order.

Note: Quotation: Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, Teshu'at Yisrael, begins at 2:18 ('and these are his words') and continues through 2:25, where 'Thus far his words' closes it. Proposed ruling: each paragraph of a quotation that runs across paragraphs opens with a double quotation mark, and only the last closes (so 2:19-2:22 and 2:24 open with one; 2:18 does not close). In this unit 2:23, 2:24 and 2:25 follow it.

Apparatus:

- Base text from Wikisource; the 1931 scan is not yet collated, so the paragraph is translated as the base text (decisions, Q2).
- Quotation: this paragraph is part of a quotation from the book Teshu'at Yisrael of Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, introduced at 2:18 with 'and these are his words'. It runs through 2:25, where עכ"ל closes it. The opening mark here is the paragraph-opening mark of a quotation that continues across paragraphs; the quotation does not begin at 2:23.
- Allusions, the author's wording and not a quotation: 'the words of the living God' (Jer 23:36, דברי אלהים חיים; cf. Jer 10:10) and 'King over all the earth' (cf. Zech 14:9; Ps 47:3).

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:24

> ששית כשהביאו שבעים ושנים זקנים את התורה לתלמי מלך מצרים, קם מכסאו והשתחוה ז' פעמים לקראתה, ואם עובד אלילים אשר לא הביא צוארו בעול תורתינו כבדה כל כך, אף כי אנחנו הבאים בבריתה ואשר ניתנה לנו למורשה.

**"Sixth: when the seventy-two elders brought the Torah to Ptolemy, king of Egypt, he rose from his throne and bowed down seven times to meet it, and if a worshipper of idols, who has not put his neck under the yoke of our Torah, honored it so much, how much more so we who enter into its covenant and to whom it was given as an inheritance.**

Grammar:

- The temporal clause כשהביאו puts the verb first and the subject after it: 'when the seventy-two elders brought the Torah'.
- קם ... והשתחוה are two past acts in sequence (qatal with vav); the English keeps the sequence, 'rose ... and bowed down'.
- The ואם clause is complete: 'and if a worshipper of idols, who has not put his neck under the yoke of our Torah, honored it so much' (כבדה, piel perfect with the suffix 'it'); the apodosis is 'how much more so we ...'.
- הביא צוארו בעול is an idiom for accepting a burden: 'brought his neck under the yoke'. In ואשר ניתנה לנו למורשה the verb ניתנה is feminine, so the Torah is what was given, 'as an inheritance' (Deut 33:4); the English reads 'to whom it was given'.

Ancient Near East:

- The Greek translation of the Torah, made in Alexandria in the third century BCE, is attributed in the rabbinic tradition to seventy-two elders in the time of Ptolemy, king of Egypt. The author follows that tradition.

Apparatus:

- Allusion, not quoted: Deut 33:4 for 'למורשה' ('an inheritance').
- The number seventy-two and the translation story are the author's (see context).

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:25

> שביעית יסודי ועיקרי דתינו הם מציאות בורא אחד יחיד קדמון אשר איננו גשם ולא כח בגשם, נותן התורה לעמו ישראל על ידי המחוקק הנאמן משה עבד ה' אדון כל הנביאים. הוא יתברך המציץ ומשגיח בעולמות שברא. ועיניו משוטטות בכל, וחוקר ובוחן לבות בני אדם ושופט בצדק על עלילות מצעדי גבר. ממנו לבד נבקש עזרה בצר לנו, והוא יפרה נצר מגזע ישי אשר יקבץ נדחי ישראל מארבע כנפות הארץ, ומכל קצוצי פאה אשר זרו אותם שמה, עצמות מתיהם היבשות תחינה ונבלתם יקומון. הן כל אלה עקרי ושרשי דתינו. ומה שמץ ע"ז נמצא בם? אף לדעת אותם אשר דעותיהם ואמונותיהם נבדלו מדעותינו ומאמונתנו עכ"ל.

**"Seventh: the foundations and principles of our religion are the existence of one, unique, eternal Creator, who is not a body, nor a force in a body, who gives the Torah to His people Israel through the faithful lawgiver Moses, servant of the LORD, master of all the prophets. He, may He be blessed, looks on and exercises providence over the worlds that He created. And His eyes roam over all, and He searches and examines the hearts of the sons of man and judges justly concerning the deeds of a man's steps. From Him alone we seek help in our distress, and He will bring forth a shoot from the stock of Jesse, who will gather the outcasts of Israel from the four corners of the earth, and from all the cut-off corners to which they scattered them there, the dry bones of their dead will live, and their corpses will rise. Indeed, all these are the principles and roots of our religion. And what trace of idolatry is found in them? Even in the opinion of those whose opinions and beliefs differ from our opinions and from our faith." Thus far his words.**

Grammar:

- The paragraph is one sentence: 'the foundations and principles ... are the existence of ...' (הם is plural). Its relative clauses (אשר, נותן) continue from the Creator, and the English keeps the sentence long.
- The verbs of providence (המציץ, ומשגיח, חוקר, ובוחן, ושופט) are participles with no finite verb; the English makes them finite with 'He'.
- והוא יפרה נצר: Isa 11:1 has this verb intransitively ('shall bear fruit'); here it takes נצר as its object, and the English follows the author ('bring forth a shoot').
- The last sentence is a fragment that continues the question: אף לדעת אותם אשר דעותיהם ואמונותיהם נבדלו ..., 'even in the opinion of those whose opinions and beliefs differ ...'. לדעת is 'in the opinion of', not an infinitive. In ועל עלילות מצעדי גבר, עלילות is in the construct: 'concerning the deeds of a man's steps'.

Ancient Near East:

- קצוצי פאה (Jer 9:25): in that verse the phrase names the desert peoples who clip the corners of their hair, a practice that Lev 19:27 forbids to Israel. Here the author uses it of the places (שמה, 'there') to which Israel was scattered; the English keeps the words literally, 'cut-off corners'.

Apparatus:

- Quotation: the double quotation marks close here with the formula עכ"ל. The quotation (Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, Teshu'at Yisrael) opens at 2:18 (see 2:23 apparatus); the opening mark here is the paragraph-opening mark.
- Allusions, the author's wording and not quotations: Jer 17:10 (חוקר לב בוחן) for 'searches and examines the hearts'; 2 Chr 16:9 and Zech 4:10 for 'His eyes roam over all'; Prov 20:24 and Ps 37:23 (מצעדי גבר) for 'a man's steps'; Deut 34:5 (משה עבד ה') for 'servant of the LORD'; Isa 11:1 for 'a shoot from the stock of Jesse'; Isa 11:12 (מארבע כנפות הארץ) for 'from the four corners of the earth'; Isa 56:8 and Ps 147:2 (נדחי ישראל) for 'the outcasts of Israel'; Ezek 37 (the dry bones) and Isa 26:19 (נבלתי יקומון) for the resurrection clause; Jer 9:25 for 'cut-off corners'.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:26

> ולפי דרכינו דרך רז"ל בבריתא הנז"ל אין צורך לכל זה שאין כוונתנו שאנו משתחוים מול הס"ת אלא למי שבחר בתורה, ובהדיא אנו אומרים בואו נשתחוה ונכרעה נברכה לפני ה' עושנו. והשתחוית אברהם אבינו למלאכים וכן יהושע, איבעית אימא כיוון שנדמו להם כאנשים קרינא בהו מאי דאמור רבנן בבריתא לא תשתחוה להם, להם אי אתה משתחוה אבל אתה משתחוה לאדם שכמותך כיון שנגלו להם בדמות אנשים ואיבעית אימא שכוונת אברהם ויהושע להשתחות למי ששלחם וכמו שכ' בעל העיקרים.

**And according to our way, the way of our Rabbis of blessed memory in the aforementioned baraita, there is no need for all this, since our intention is not that we bow down before the Torah scroll, but to Him who chose the Torah. Explicitly, we say: "Come, let us bow down and bend the knee, let us kneel before the LORD our Maker." And as for the bowing down of Abraham our father to the angels, and so Joshua's, if you wish, say: since they appeared to them as men, we apply to them what the Rabbis said in the baraita: "'You shall not bow down to them.' To them you may not bow down, but you bow down to a man like yourself," since they were revealed to them in the form of men. And if you wish, say that the intention of Abraham and Joshua was to bow down to Him who sent them, and as the author of the Ikkarim wrote.**

Grammar:

- בואו נשתחוה ונכרעה נברכה is Ps 95:6, given as the people's words: the cohortatives ('let us') stay in the English, and the verse is set in quotation marks. נכרעה is 'let us bend the knee' and נברכה 'let us kneel' (ברך, not 'bless').
- והשתחוית is a noun ('the bowing down'), so 'And as for the bowing down' is a topic phrase; the Hebrew joins it by a comma to איבעית אימא, and the English keeps one sentence: 'And as for ... Joshua's, if you wish, say: ...'.
- איבעית אימא ('if you wish, say') introduces a second explanation. The author gives two, the first (the angels appeared as men) and the second (the intention was toward the One who sent them); the English keeps both in order.
- The baraita is quoted inside the sentence ('what the Rabbis said in the baraita: ...'), and the English returns to the author's syntax with 'since they were revealed to them'.
- אי אתה משתחוה is the Talmudic negative of permission, 'you may not bow down'; the English keeps the modal.

Apparatus:

- Ps 95:6 for 'בואו נשתחוה ונכרעה נברכה לפני ה׳ עושנו'.
- Exod 20:5 for 'לא תשתחוה להם' ('you shall not bow down to them'), the words of the baraita.
- Cf. Gen 18:2 and Josh 5:14 for the bowing of Abraham and Joshua; the author alludes to them and does not quote them.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:27

> ושאלתך מענין הנבואה אעפ"י שאינו שייך לעניינינו ולא שאלת רק להטעותנו ולהשיאנו לדבר אחר, הנה זה מבואר מדרגות הנבואה ברמב"ם הל' יסודי התורה, ובחלק שני מספר המורה, ובספר האמונות והדעות להרס"ג. ולפי שמצאתיך חכם בעיניך אחזור לבקש ממך להשיב לי תשובה ניצחת מדברי רז"ל בתלמוד, כי רק אתה לבדך (לפי דעתך) לך נגלו כל תעלומות, ובינה יתירה ורוח חדש ניתן בקרבך. הורינו אני וחבירי איך הדברים יעלו בקנה אחד מלאות וטובות. כי נפשינו חשקה לשמוע לימודיך, ולהשתעשע בתורתך התמימה, ולך תהיה צדקה, וגם כבוד גדול תנחל מאיתנו.

**And your question concerning prophecy, although it does not belong to our subject, and you asked only to mislead us and to divert us to another matter, behold, this is set out in the degrees of prophecy in the Rambam, Laws of the Foundations of the Torah, and in part two of the book Moreh Nevukhim, and in the book Emunot ve-De'ot of Rabbi Saadia Gaon. Since I have found you wise in your own eyes, I return to ask you to answer me a decisive answer from the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory in the Talmud, for you alone (in your opinion) all mysteries have been revealed to you, and extraordinary understanding and a new spirit have been given within you. Instruct us, I and my companions, how the matters can agree fully and well. For our soul has longed to hear your teachings, and to delight in your perfect Torah, and it will be to you a merit, and also great honor you will inherit from us.**

Literal: and-your-question concerning prophecy although is-not relevant to-our-subject and-not you-asked only to-mislead-us and-to-divert-us to-a-matter other. behold this is-set-out the-degrees-of prophecy in-the-Rambam Laws-of the-Foundations-of the-Torah, and-in part two of-the-book the-Moreh, and-in-the-book the-Emunot and-the-De'ot of-Rabbi-Saadia-Gaon. and-since I-found-you wise in-your-eyes, I-return to-ask of-you to-answer to-me an-answer decisive from-the-words-of our-Rabbis in-the-Talmud, for you alone (in-your-opinion) to-you were-revealed all mysteries, and-understanding extraordinary and-spirit new has-been-given within-you. instruct-us I and-my-companions how the-matters will-agree in-one-reed in-full and-good. for our-soul longed to-hear your-teachings, and-to-delight in-your-Torah the-perfect, and-to-you will-be righteousness, and-also honor great you-will-inherit from-us

Grammar:

- The paragraph is a letter, and the list of works (the Rambam, the Moreh, Emunot ve-De'ot) is a series of 'in' phrases; the English keeps the series in the Hebrew's order. The opening ושאלתך ... אעפ"י ... ולא שאלת ... runs on, by commas, to the main clause הנה זה מבואר, and the English keeps it as one sentence.
- ולא שאלת רק להטעותנו: 'you asked only (nothing but) to mislead us'; לא ... רק is 'not ... except'.
- חכם בעיניך echoes Prov 3:7 (אל תהי חכם בעיניך), 'wise in your own eyes'; the English follows the verse's sense.
- הורינו אני וחבירי איך הדברים יעלו: the imperative is followed by a 'how' clause, so the English reads 'Instruct us ..., how the matters can agree'.

Apparatus:

- Cf. Ezek 36:26 for 'ורוח חדש ניתן בקרבך' ('a new spirit ... within you'); the author does not quote it.
- Prov 3:7 (אל תהי חכם בעיניך) for 'חכם בעיניך' ('wise in your own eyes'); the author alludes to it.
- Dan 5:12 and 5:14 (רוח יתירה) for 'בינה יתירה' ('extraordinary understanding').
- Ps 19:8 (תורת ה' תמימה) for 'תורתך התמימה' ('your perfect Torah'); cf. Ps 119:77, 92 (תורתך שעשעי) for 'to delight in your Torah'.
- Deut 24:13 (ולך תהיה צדקה) for 'ולך תהיה צדקה' ('it will be to you a merit').
- Prov 3:35 (כבוד חכמים ינחלו) for 'כבוד גדול תנחל' ('great honor you will inherit').

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:28

> תשובה לאדם מערכי לב ומה' מענה לשון. ויהי בראותי את מכתבך ישבתי משתומם ומתבהל. איך מלאך לבך לדרוש ולחקור אחר חבל גאונים, אשר הם בתורה נאמנים גדולי היחס כזרע האיתנים, ואחר כמה פסקנים וגם דרשנים ראשונים עם אחרונים חכמי מערב ואשכנז וספרד ותימנים. ושאר קהלות זרע קדש בני אמונים, זאת היא חמדתם מפז ורב פנינים. וכי תבוא תקלה מיד צדיקים נאמנים יודעי מדע חכמים ונבונים יראי אלהים וסרים מרע באונים. בחכמתם הפילו כמה צרים ומונים העומדים עליהם בכל זמנים. וכי קבלתם מרוקחת בהבל ושגיונים אשר לרוב חכמתם אושרו בפי שרים ורוזנים התיצבו לפני מלכים ושלטונים וכי ילכו בדרך לא טוב אבות ובנים? זה כמה מאות שנים? וכמה הם מופלגים בכל חכמה וספרנים מקובלים עם פילוסופיא והגיונים, רפואה ותשבורת ותוכנים. הוגים יומם ולילה שקטים ושאננים, אוכלים פרי מעשיהם הטוב דשנים ורעננים. חלילה! זה לא יאמן ולא יעלה על לב כי אם לפתיים, לכל דבר מאמינים, אשר על שכלם נשענים. ומן הראוי אין עלי להשיבך. כי מה אני להכנס לפני ולפנים מה שלא הורשתי להרהר כל שכן להשיב שואלים. אבל משום עת לעשות לה' אני משיבך ממה שמצאתי כתוב בדברי חז"ל. וזכותם יעמד לי שלא יארע שום תקלה על ידי. הנה מה שכתבת שאינך מבזה חכמי ישראל כבר יש עליך כמה עדים, לא תוכל להכחיש. ומה שהביא אותך לידי כך שאתה מיחס להם טעות ומינות. אלא מפני שהם בזויים בעיניך. אבל האדם יחוש לעצמו פן יכוה בגחלתן כי גדולים צדיקים במיתתן יותר מבחייהן כמו שאמרו בתלמוד. ומה שכתבת שאם לגלות מקום הסתירה וגם התלמוד מביאים ראיה לסתור דברי גדולים מהם, אין הנדון דומה לראיה, דהיכן מצינו שמביאים ראיה לסתור הלכה למשה מסיני? וחכמי הקבלה אומרים כך קיבלו מפי משה, ומי הוא זה ואיפה הוא שנתן לך רשות לחקור ולדרוש אחר דבריהם? ומה שכתבת שהם קורים לפרצופים אלוהות ח"ו שהם אומרים כך. ומה שכתבת צא ולמד מכוונת הברכות והתפלות. כבר ביארו שעילת כל העלות נתכנה בספירה פלונית בשם כן. ובספירה פלונית בשם כך. ומה שכתבת שביארו המקובלים שכמה עולמות יש אלפי אלפים וכו' אפילו יהיו מליוני מליונים כיון שהם אומ' שבוראם אחד והוא מחיה את כולם מה יש הפסד מזה? ומה שכתבת שהם בציור אדם בעל קומה, כבר אמרו גדול כחן של נביאים שמדמין דמות גבורה של מעלה לצורת אדם. ומה שכתבת ברמ"ח איברים כבר ביארו מה הן האיברים. כי הם רי"ו אותיות של שם בן ע"ב ול"ב נתיבות שהם רומזים לכוחות אלהיים. ומה שכתבת שכבר הודיתי שדעתי שאין שום תפלה שייכא בעילת כל העילות שקר אתה דובר. והלא מתחלת שאלתך אותי על דברי המשרף הישבתיך עיין בכס"א. אבל קבלתינו שהתפלה לא"ס ולהשפיע אל עשר ספירות כמו שכ' לחם שלמה. ומה שאמרתי לך לעיין בכסא אליהו כדי שתדע שדברי המשרף דברי כפירה באמת וראוי לבערו. וח"ו שנמצא בשום ספר כדבריו, אבל דברי כס"א אינם כדבריו ח"ו. כי דברי כסא אליהו אין הזעיר אנפין כי אם כלי לפעולת הבורא. ומה שכ' בדף כ"ה שבקראינו לז"א אנחנו קורין אל כל הפרצופים עם נשמה המסתתרת בהם שהוא אין סוף ב"ה. אין רוצה לומר שאין התפילה לא"ס חלילה, אלא רוצה לומר שעליית התפלה אל הא"ס ב"ה דרך זאת המדה. והראיה על זה מה שכ' בדף י"ז ע"ב וז"ל ומה שכתוב בכוונות התפלה והברכות לכוון בכל ברכה כוונה מיוחדת לספי' מיוחדת לא ח"ו לעצמות הספירה. כי הוא קיצוץ ח"ו, וחלילה לכוון לשום כח פרטי וספירה מיוחדת. אלא הכל לעצמות יחיד א"ס ב"ה כלל כל הכחות כולם. ועוד כ' בדף כ"ה ע"א וכל תפלותינו הם לאין סוף ית'. אך שאין אנחנו יכולים לכנותו בשום כנוי ושם. לזה אנחנו מתפללים על ידי הספירות. כי שם שייכות כל כל הכינוים והשמות. כי כל הכנויים והשמות הם שמות עצמותו המתפשט בספירות. וג"כ כ' בדף כ"ו ואם לא יעשו כן ולא ייחדו תפלתם אלא לז"א לא יהיו נענים. וכל המקובלים כיילי כללא דא וז"ל ומה שתמצא באיזה ספר מהם התפלה לשום ספירה חלילה שיהיה כן. אלא הכוונה שיכוין להעלותם אל הא"ס דרך אותה ספירה.

**Reply. To man the arrangements of the heart, and from the LORD the answer of the tongue. And it was when I saw your letter, I sat astonished and dismayed. How your heart emboldened you to inquire and investigate after the band of the Geonim, who are faithful in the Torah, distinguished in lineage, like the seed of the mighty, and after several decisors and also expounders, the early and the later, the sages of the Maghreb, Ashkenaz, Sefarad and the Yemenites. And the rest of the congregations, the holy seed, the faithful children, this is their treasure, more than fine gold and many pearls. Can a stumbling come from the hand of righteous and faithful ones, who know knowledge, the wise and discerning, who fear God and turn aside from evil with their might. By their wisdom they felled many foes and multitudes who stood against them in every age. Can it be that their Kabbalah is compounded in vanity and errors, they who, because of their great wisdom, were approved by the mouths of princes and nobles and stood before kings and rulers, and can fathers and sons walk on a path that is not good? How many hundreds of years is this? And how many of them are distinguished in every wisdom, and scholars, Kabbalists with philosophy and logic, medicine, mathematics and astronomy, meditating day and night, quiet and at ease, eating the good fruit of their deeds, fat and lush. Heaven forbid! This is not to be believed and does not come to mind except to the simple, who believe every word, who lean on their understanding. And properly, it is not incumbent on me to answer you. For what am I, to enter the innermost, into what I was not permitted to ponder, all the more so to answer questioners. But because it is a time to act for the LORD, I answer you from what I found written in the words of our Sages of blessed memory. May their merit stand for me, that no stumbling befall through me. Now, as for what you wrote, that you do not despise the sages of Israel, there are already several witnesses against you; you cannot deny it. And as for what brought you to this, that you attribute to them error and heresy: it is only because they are despised in your eyes. But a person should take heed for himself, lest he be burned by their coals, for the righteous are greater in their death than in their life, as they said in the Talmud. And as for what you wrote, that if one reveals the place of contradiction, and the Talmud also brings proof to refute the words of those greater than them, the case is not comparable to the proof, for where do we find that they bring proof to refute a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai? And the sages of Kabbalah say that thus they received from the mouth of Moses, and who is this one, and where is he, who gave you permission to inquire and investigate after their words? And as for what you wrote, that they call the partzufim divinities, God forbid, that they say thus. And as for what you wrote, go and learn from the intention of the blessings and the prayers. They already explained that the Cause of all causes is designated in a certain sefirah by such a name, and in a certain sefirah by that name. And as for what you wrote, that the Kabbalists explained that there are several worlds, thousands of thousands, etc., even if they were millions of millions, since they say that their Creator is one, and He gives life to all of them: what loss is there from this? And as for what you wrote, that they are in the image of a man possessing stature, already they said, "Great is the power of the prophets, who liken the likeness of the Power above to the form of a man." And as for what you wrote about 248 limbs, they already explained what the limbs are. For they are 216 letters of the Name of 72 and 32 paths, which allude to divine powers. And as for what you wrote, that I already conceded that my opinion is that there is no prayer applicable to the Cause of all causes, you speak falsehood. But surely, from the beginning of your question to me about the words of the Mesharef, I answered you, see in Kisse Eliyahu. But our Kabbalah holds that prayer is to Ein Sof and to bestow the flow upon the ten sefirot, as Lechem Shelomo wrote. And as for what I told you, to consult Kisse Eliyahu, so that you would know that the words of the Mesharef are words of heresy, in truth, and fitting to root it out. And God forbid that there be found in any book words like his, but the words of Kisse Eliyahu are not like his, God forbid. For the words of Kisse Eliyahu hold that Ze'ir Anpin is nothing but a vessel for the action of the Creator. And as for what he wrote on folio 25, that when we call upon Ze'ir Anpin, we call upon all the partzufim, with a soul hidden in them, which is Ein Sof, blessed be He. This does not mean that prayer is not directed to Ein Sof, Heaven forbid, but it means that the ascent of prayer to Ein Sof, blessed be He, is by way of this attribute. And the proof for this is what he wrote on folio 17b, and these are his words: "As for what is written about the intentions of prayer and the blessings, to direct in each blessing a particular intention, to a particular sefirah, not, God forbid, to the essence of the sefirah. For it is a cutting off, God forbid, and Heaven forbid to direct it to any particular power or particular sefirah. But all is to the essence of the one Ein Sof, blessed be He, the totality of all the powers, all of them." And furthermore he wrote on folio 25a: "And all our prayers are to Ein Sof, may He be blessed. Except that we cannot call Him by any appellation and name. Therefore we pray through the sefirot. For there is the applicability of all, all the appellations and names. For all the appellations and names are names of His essence, extending through the sefirot." Also he wrote on folio 26: "And if they do not do so, and do not dedicate their prayer solely to Ze'ir Anpin, they will not be answered." And all the Kabbalists lay down this principle, and these are their words: "As for whatever you find in some book of theirs, that prayer is addressed to any sefirah, Heaven forbid that it be so. But the intention is that one intend to raise them to Ein Sof by way of that sefirah."**

Grammar:

- The paragraph is the respondent's reply in chapter 2. "You" is the questioner; the reply takes up each point of his letter in turn, introduced by ומה שכתבת ("as for what you wrote") and answered after it.
- The rhetorical questions opened by וכי ("Can it be that ...", 2:28.56, 2:28.80, 2:28.96) and the sentences ending in a question mark (2:28.102, 2:28.106, 2:28.260, 2:28.279, 2:28.337) keep their question form; the text gives no answer to them within the paragraph.
- Quotations of the Kabbalists are in double quotation marks. They open after the formula וז"ל (2:28.501, 2:28.601) or after כ' with a folio (2:28.539, 2:28.580), and close at the end of each passage, since the text gives no closing formula. The quoted words are Hebrew, except כיילי כללא דא (2:28.598-600), which is Aramaic and is rendered by its sense.
- The verb ייחדו (2:28.589) is rendered "dedicate": to set the prayer apart for one addressee, the sense that fits אלא ("only"). "Unify" in the Kabbalistic sense is the alternative (see the review question); לז"א (2:28.592) is the entity the prayer is dedicated to.
- Two Biblical allusions carry the opening and the close of the argument: Prov 16:1 at the start (2:28.1-7), and the word לה' from Ps 119:126 (2:28.172), which the author reads as "for the LORD".
- אין הנדון דומה לראיה (2:28.249-252) is a fixed idiom of argument: the case under discussion is not like the case cited as proof, so the proof does not apply. לפני ולפנים (2:28.158-159) is the idiom for the innermost part (of the Temple), literally "before and within".

Note: Prose paragraph: the respondent's reply in chapter 2. Each word is glossed. Letter numerals are given as Arabic numerals (רמ"ח 248, רי"ו 216, ע"ב 72, ל"ב 32, כ"ה 25, י"ז ע"ב 17b). Kisse Eliyahu and Lechem Shelomo are book titles; Ein Sof and Ze'ir Anpin are kept as names.

Apparatus:

- Base text: Wikisource, as printed; the 1931 scan is not yet collated (Q2), so no reading is added or corrected here.
- Prov 16:1 (allusion at the opening, 2:28.1-7): the verse reads "The arrangements of the heart belong to man, and the answer of the tongue is from the LORD." The author's Hebrew is the verse's words with תשובה prefixed.
- Job 1:1 (allusion, 2:28.66-70): "וִירֵא אֱלֹהִים וְסָר מֵרָע", rendered "fear God and turn from evil", with the author's plural form.
- Isa 6:13 (allusion, 2:28.46-47): "זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ", "the holy seed".
- Isa 65:2 (allusion, 2:28.97-100): "בְּדֶרֶךְ לֹא־טוֹב", "in a way that is not good".
- Ps 92:15 (allusion, 2:28.129-130): "דְּשֵׁנִים וְרַעֲנַנִּים", "fat and luxuriant".
- Avot 2:10 (allusion, 2:28.224-225): the author's "פן יכוה בגחלתן" recalls the saying to beware of the coals of the sages; the words are his, not a quotation.
- Ps 119:126 (allusion, 2:28.171-172): "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה'", "It is a time to act for the LORD".
- Folio references as the author gives them: folio 17b (2:28.498-500), folio 25 (2:28.458-459, 2:28.541-543), folio 26 (2:28.582-583). No reference is added.
- The doubled "כל כל" (2:28.567-568) is as printed; both words are translated.
- ומונים (2:28.75): the word is uncertain. Read as והמונים with the ה dropped ("multitudes", rhyming with the -ים series); the alternative is a misprint for ומינים ("and heretics"). Rendered "and multitudes".
- המשרף (2:28.402, 2:28.427): not a person here. In 3:10 and 3:12 the questioner is charged with calling the book Metzaref ha-Emunah ("Refiner of Faith") "the book Mesharef" and "Mesharef ha-Emunah" ("Burner of Faith"), from שרף "burn": a play on מצרף. The transliteration "Mesharef" is kept.
- ותשבורת and ותוכנים (2:28.118-119): names of sciences in a list with medicine. תשבורת (cf. "חכמת התשבורת בשמים ובארץ", 4:27, with חשבון, 8:11) is mensuration, mathematics; תוכנים is the plural of תכונה, astronomy. Rendered "mathematics and astronomy".
- The Talmudic sayings (2:28.233-234, 2:28.241-260, 2:28.258-260) are given without a reference, since the author gives none.
- Esth 7:5 (allusion, 2:28.15-17): "אֲשֶׁר מְלָאוֹ לִבּוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן", "whose heart has emboldened him to do so"; again at 2:28.268-273, "מִי הוּא זֶה וְאֵי זֶה הוּא", "who is this one, and where is he".
- Ezra 9:3 (allusion, 2:28.12-13): "וָאֵשְׁבָה מְשׁוֹמֵם", "and I sat appalled".
- 1 Sam 10:5 (allusion, 2:28.21): "חֶבֶל נְבִיאִים", "a band of prophets".
- Prov 22:29 (allusion, 2:28.92-94): "לִפְנֵי מְלָכִים יִתְיַצָּב", "he shall stand before kings".
- Ps 19:11 and Prov 3:15 (allusion, 2:28.52-55): "הַנֶּחֱמָדִים מִזָּהָב וּמִפַּז רָב", "more desirable than gold, than much fine gold"; "יְקָרָה הִיא מִפְּנִינִים", "more precious than pearls".
- Ps 1:2 and Josh 1:8 (allusion, 2:28.120-122): "יֶהְגֶּה יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה", "he meditates day and night".
- Jer 46:27 and 30:10 (allusion, 2:28.123-124): "וְשָׁקֵט וְשַׁאֲנָן", "quiet and at ease".
- Isa 3:10 (allusion, 2:28.125-127): "פְּרִי מַעַלְלֵיהֶם יֹאכֵלוּ", "they shall eat the fruit of their deeds".
- Prov 14:15 (allusion, 2:28.141-144): "פֶּתִי יַאֲמִין לְכָל דָּבָר", "the simple believes every word".
- Neh 9:6 (allusion, 2:28.330-333): "וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם", "and You give life to all of them".
- שם (2:28.565): read "there" (in the sefirot, where the epithets apply); the alternative is "the name".

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:29

> והארכתי כל זה לישב לך דברי כס"א, אבל קבלתי כבר זכרתיה למעלה. ויש הוכחה מכאן, שמה שאתה שואלני אינו מטעם בקשתך האמת כמו שאמרת, כי אם לבקש איזה עלילה. ומה אני שאתה מחזיק אותי למקובל, כי אני בער ולא אדע. וכל תפלותי אפי' כצפצוף העופות אינם, כי העופות ניזונים שלא בצער ואין עליהם לא עול מלכות ולא עול דרך ארץ, ואפשר צפצוף בכוונה אבל אני כמה עול הזמן וטרדת המזונות מבלבלים דעתי ומחשבותי. ועוד שלא קבלתי מחכם מקובל מפה אל פה. ומי יתן ויניח לי ה' מטרדות הזמן והמזונות ויזמין לי רב מקובל יניחני במעגלי יושר, ואזכה להיות מבני עליה. ומה שהשבתי לך פעם שניה הוא דברי כס"א שהעלמת עין מהם, ומה שכתבת שאינך מגשים בספירות, והלא כתבת א"כ יהיה כח בגוף. ובפעם הזאת אתה אומר כי האור גוף דק. וכבר כתבתי לך כי מה שכינו אותן בשם אור אינו אלא כדי לשבר את האזן פעם תגשים ופעם תתנצל ולמה עולים בדעתך כל אלו הספקות אלא מפני שאתה מגשים. ומה שכתבת מי הוא המנהיג כל אלו העולמות הנעלמים, הממציאם הוא מחיה אותם. ומה שכתבת שנמצא הז"א אלהי התחתונים. הלא כתבתי לך שאינו אלא כלי לפעולות הבורא. ומה שכתבת שמקצתם אמרו את כל מעשה ה' הגדול מכלל דאיכא קטן? האומרים כן כבר ביארו הם שכוונתם על מטטרון ששמו כשם רבו, כמו שאמרו בתלמוד ואל משה אמר עלה אל ה', אלי מבעי ליה אלא זה מטטרון ששמו כשם רבו וכ"ה בילקוט. ומה שכתבת שרבותינו האמתיים אמרו, הובא במנורת המאור, שבשעת מתן תורה קרע הקב"ה ז' רקיעים וכו'. ובמדרש רבה אמרו אנכי ה' אלהיך, אני ראשון ואני אחרון. אני ראשון שאין לי אב ואני אחרון שאין לי בן ומבלעדי אין אלהים שאין לי אח. מי הוא האומר שיש לו אב או בם או אח? אלא אתה מוציא דבה על החכמים שהם אומרים כן, והם כבר ביארו דבריהם ז"ל, שכל הכנויים והתארים הם בספירות לשבר את האזן. לך נא וראה מה שכתב מהר"י גיקטליא בהקדמת שערי אורה, והאלהי ר"מ ריקנטי, ור"י חיים וז"ל, סוף דבר כל מקום שתראה דברים שאין ראוי לאמרם בבורא ית' כגון שיעור קומה והדומים להם הכל נאמר על הספירות וכשתראה שידברו דרך שבח והודיה, הכל נאמר על הבורא ית' שבתוכן ובחוצה להן כי אין דבר שיגבילהו ועל כן אין לומר בבורא ית' לא ימין ולא שמאל לא פנים ולא אחור וכו' עי"ש. ומה שכתבת שדעת המקובלים שהספירות משתלשלים בטבע כבן מן האב, חלילה שהם אמרו כן, אדרבה אמרו חלילה להאמין ולהעלות על לב שהספירות הם חלק מהאין סוף שיצאו ממנו ונשתלשל מעילה לעלול כי הוא עון פלילי. שהאין סוף אינו מתחלק לחלקים ח"ו, ואינו מקבל תוספת ולא מגרעת אלא מציאותו קיים תמיד בלי שום שינוי כלל, והוא חידשם חידוש גמור.

**I have gone on at length about all this, to reconcile for you the words of Kisse Eliyahu, but my tradition I have already mentioned above. And there is proof from this that what you ask me is not from the motive of your request for the truth, as you said, but rather to seek some pretext. And who am I that you should hold me to be a Kabbalist, for I am brutish and do not know. And all my prayers are not even like the chirping of birds, for the birds are fed without distress, and on them there lies neither the yoke of kingship nor the yoke of worldly occupation, and chirping can be done with intent, but I, under so much burden of the times and the cares of livelihood, have my mind and my thoughts confused. And furthermore, I have not received from a wise Kabbalist mouth to mouth. Would that the LORD relieve me of the troubles of time and of livelihood, and provide me a Kabbalist master who would set me on the paths of uprightness, and that I might merit to be among the sons of ascent. As for what I answered you the second time, it is the words of Kisse Eliyahu that you turned a blind eye to. And as for what you wrote, that you do not ascribe corporeality to the sefirot, but did you not write: "If so, there would be a force in a body"? And this time you say that light is a subtle body. And I already wrote to you that what they called them by the name light is only in order to accommodate the ear; one time you ascribe corporeality and another time you make excuses. And why do all these doubts come into your mind, except because you ascribe corporeality? As for what you wrote: "Who is it that governs all these hidden worlds?" The one who brings them into being is the one who keeps them alive. And as for what you wrote, that Ze'ir Anpin is found to be the god of the lower ones. Have I not written to you that he is nothing but a tool for the acts of the Creator? And as for what you wrote, that some of them said "all the great work of the LORD," from which it follows that there is a small one? Those who say so have themselves already explained that they meant Metatron, whose name is like his master's, as they said in the Talmud: "And to Moses He said, 'Come up to the LORD'; it should have said 'to Me'. But this is Metatron, whose name is like his master's"; and so it is in the Yalkut. And as for what you wrote, that our true rabbis said, it is cited in Menorat ha-Ma'or that at the time of the giving of the Torah the Holy One, blessed be He, tore 7 heavens, etc. And in Midrash Rabbah they said: "I am the LORD your God; I am the first and I am the last. I am the first, for I have no father, and I am the last, for I have no son; and besides Me there is no God, for I have no brother." Who is it that says he has a father, or a son, or a brother? Rather, you spread slander against the sages who say so, and they have already explained their words, of blessed memory, that all the epithets and the attributes are in the sefirot, to accommodate the ear. Go now and see what Mahari Gikatilia wrote in the introduction to Sha'arei Orah, and the divine Rabbi Menachem Rikanti, and Rabbi Y. Chayyim, and these are his words: "In sum, wherever you see things that are not fitting to say of the Creator, may He be blessed, such as measure of stature and the like, it is all said of the sefirot; and when you see them speak in the manner of praise and thanksgiving, it is all said of the Creator, may He be blessed, who is within them and outside them, for nothing limits Him; therefore one may not say of the Creator, may He be blessed, not right and not left, not face and not back, etc." See there. And as for what you wrote, that the opinion of the Kabbalists is that the sefirot descend in a chain, by nature like a son from the father, far be it that they said so. On the contrary, they said: "Far be it to believe or to bring to mind that the sefirot are part of Ein Sof that came out of it and descended from cause to effect, for it is a criminal sin. For Ein Sof is not divided into parts, God forbid, and it receives no addition and no diminution, but its existence is constant always, without any change whatever, and He originated them, an absolute origination."**

Literal: I have gone on at length about all this to reconcile for you the words of Kisse Eliyahu but my tradition already I mentioned it above and there is proof from this that what you ask me is not from the motive of your request for the truth as you said but rather to seek some pretext and what am I that you hold me as a Kabbalist for I am brutish and do not know and all my prayers even like the chirping of birds is not for the birds are fed without distress and there is not on them neither the yoke of kingship nor the yoke of the way of the land and it is possible chirping with intent but I so much burden of the times and the worry of livelihood confuse my mind and my thoughts and furthermore that not I have received from a wise man Kabbalist from mouth to mouth and would that will give and relieve me the LORD of the troubles of time and of livelihood and provide me a master Kabbalist who would set me on the paths of uprightness and I will merit to be from the sons of ascent as for what I answered to you time second is the words of Kisse Eliyahu that you turned a blind eye to them and as for what you wrote that you are not ascribing corporeality to the sefirot but did not you write if so there would be a force in a body and at this time this you say that light a body subtle and already I wrote to you that what they called them by the name light is not but in order to break (object marker) the ear at one time you ascribe corporeality and another time you make excuses and why come up in your mind all these doubts except because you ascribe corporeality as for what you wrote who is it that governs all these worlds hidden the one who brings into being is keeps alive them and as for what you wrote that is found Ze'ir Anpin god of the lower ones have I not written to you that he is not but a vessel for the acts of the Creator and as for what you wrote that some of them said (object marker) all the work of the LORD great from which it follows that there is a small one those who say so already have explained they their intent was on Metatron whose name is like the name of his master as they said in the Talmud and to Moses he said come up to the LORD to Me it should have said it but this is Metatron whose name is like his master's name and so it is in the Yalkut and as for what you wrote that our rabbis the true ones said it is cited in Menorat ha-Ma'or that at the time of the giving of the Torah tore the Holy One, blessed be He 7 heavens etc. and in Midrash Rabbah they said I am the LORD your God I the first and I last I am first for I have no father and I am last for I have no son and besides Me there is no God for I have no brother who is it that says he has to him a father or a son or a brother rather you spread slander against the sages who say so and they already have explained their words of blessed memory that all the epithets and the attributes are in the sefirot to break (object marker) the ear go now and see what wrote Mahari Gikatilia in the introduction to Sha'arei Orah and the divine Rabbi Menachem Rikanti and Rabbi Y. Chayyim and these are his words in sum the end of the matter all wherever you see things that are not fitting to say of the Creator may He be blessed such as measure of stature and the like of them all is said of the sefirot and when you see them speak in the manner of praise and thanksgiving all is said of the Creator may He be blessed who is within and outside them for there is not anything that limits Him therefore so one may not say of the Creator may He be blessed not right and not left not face and not back etc. see there and as for what you wrote that the opinion of the Kabbalists that the sefirot descend in a chain by nature like a son from the father far be it that they said so on the contrary they said far be it to believe or to bring to mind the heart that the sefirot are part of Ein Sof that came out from it and descended from cause to effect for it is a sin criminal that Ein Sof is not divided into parts God forbid and it does not receive addition and not diminution but its existence is constant always without any change whatever and He originated them origination absolute

Grammar:

- The paragraph is the respondent's reply to his questioner, in the respondent's own voice. 'You' is the questioner, and the English keeps the second person.
- Each point of the questioner's letter is answered in turn, opening with 'as for what you wrote' (2:29.101, 112, 160, 173, 187, 230, 373). The questions with 'but did you not' and 'and why' keep their force as questions.
- Clauses with 'that' after 'you wrote' are reported speech and take no quotation marks. 'You wrote: if so ...' and 'you wrote: who is it ...' quote the questioner's own words, so they are in quotation marks.
- The Talmud passage turns on the word 'to Me' (אלי): the verse should have said 'to Me', and the Talmud draws its conclusion from the difference. The English gives the Hebrew point in single quotation marks inside the double ones. 'אלי מבעי ליה' is Aramaic in the Talmud's wording; מכלל דאיכא קטן is Aramaic too.
- The verb 'to ascribe corporeality' (להגשים) and its forms run through the paragraph. It is the error the writer charges against the questioner, and it is rendered the same way each time.
- The idiom לשבר את האזן (2:29.143-145, 301-303), 'to break the ear', means to accommodate the ear, that is, to bring a matter within what the hearer can take in. The respondent uses it twice for the Kabbalists' physical epithets.

Note: The respondent's reply (2:29) in the respondent's voice. Honorifics, book titles and abbreviations are rendered by the decisions for this work; see the notes at the first occurrence of each.

Other readings:

- קבלתי: I received (verb reading). קבלתי as a verb: 'but I received, I already mentioned it above'; the English takes the noun 'my tradition'.
- תפלותי: my foolish talk (alternative spelling). תפלות 'foolishness' has the same consonants; the English takes 'prayers' from the context.
- בם: in them (printed text). The printed בם is 'in them'; the English reads the likelier בן, 'son'.

Apparatus:

- Witness: Wikisource base text. The 1931 scan is not yet collated, so the text is translated as read and this is flagged here (decisions, Q2).
- Bible verses: Exod 20:2 ('I am the LORD your God', 2:29.249-251, in the Midrash quotation); Isa 44:6 ('I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God', 2:29.252-271); Exod 24:1 ('And to Moses He said: Come up to the LORD', 2:29.213-218, in the Talmud quotation); Deut 11:7 ('all the great work of the LORD', 2:29.191-194); Ps 73:22 ('I am brutish and do not know', 2:29.38-40); Prov 4:11 ('the paths of uprightness', 2:29.95-96).
- Variant: the printed 'בם' (2:29.279), 'in them'. Read as 'בן' (son), the likelier word in 'a father or a son or a brother'. The printed word is kept in the Hebrew; the English follows the sense.
- The Talmud and Midrash passages carry no reference in the text, and none is added.
- The quotation 'In sum ...' ends at 2:29.371 and is followed by 'See there' (2:29.372). The quotation 'Far be it ...' closes at 2:29.430.
- Bible allusions: 'a criminal sin' (2:29.406-407) is Job 31:28 ('this too is a criminal sin'; cf. 31:11); 'spread slander' (2:29.284-285) is Num 14:36 ('and they spread slander') and Prov 10:18.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 2:30

> ומה שכתבת שז"א בן לאבא לאמא והוא אב לעלולים שאחריו, ויש לו אחות נוקבא דיליה, הכל משל וכינוי בספירות. ומה שכתבת שאין לעבוד שום פרצוף, זה ידוע בפי כל המקובלים, ואין צריכים לאזהרתך. ומה שכתבת בשם הרמב"ם חמשה הן הנקראים מינים וכו' מי הוא האומר שאין שם אלוה, או שהם שנים, או שהוא בעל גוף, או שאינו לבדו האחד או שעובד זולתו כדי להיות מליץ, או האומר שמצא סמנים או האומר שנברא העולם יש מיש ח"ו. אלא שכבר עלתה טינא בלבך, ואתה מעיין הספרים הקדושים ולוקח לך הדברים כפשטן וסומך על הבנתך. ושכחת מה שאמר חכם החכמים, ואל בינתך אל תשען. ומפני שכבר הודעת לי שאתה מבין תתיר לי ספקותי אשר שלחתי אליך ואשר אני עתיד לשלוח. ומה שכתבת והבנת רבים וגדולים חכמי לב הפורשים ממנה ראשונים ואחרונים, ח"ו שיש שום חכם פורש ממנה. ואם יש פורש ממנה הוא עצמו מודה בפה מלא שהוא מחסרון ידיעה בה. ומה שכתבת כמו שכ' הריב"ש וחו"י, שקר אתה דובר עליהם. והם שני עדים כשרים להעיד עליך שאתה דובר שקרים. וז"ל הריב"ש בקיצור כי ר' פרץ הכהן לא היה מדבר ולא מחשיב באותן הספירות. גם שמע מפיו שר' שמשון מקינון היה אומר אני מתפלל לדעת זה התינוק כלומר להוציא מלב המקובלים שהם מתפללים פעם לספירה אחת ופעם לספירה אחרת. גם בתפלת י"ח יש להם בכל אחת ואחת כוונה לספירה ידועה. וכל זה הוא דבר זר מאוד בעיני מי שאינו מקובל כמותם. וחושבים שזה אמונת שניות. וששמע אחד מן המתפלספים מספר בגנות המקובלים והיה אומר הנצרים מאמיני השלוש והמקובלים מאמיני העשיריות. ושאל להחכם הישיש דון יוסף ן' שושן והוא היה חכם בתלמוד. וראה פילוסופיא והיה מקובל וחסיד וגדול ומדקדק במצות. ואמר לו איך אתם המקובלים מכוונים בברכה אחת לספירה ידועה ובברכה אחת לספירה אחרת. ועוד הכי יש אלוהות לספירות? שיתפלל אדם להם? וענו לו חלילה שתהיה התפלה כי אם לשי"ת עילת העילות אלא שמכוין המחשבה להמשיך השפע לאותה ספירה המתיחסת לאותו דבר שהוא מבקש עליו כמו שתאמר שבברכת על הצדיקים יכוין לספירה הנקראת חסד שהיא מדת רחמים וכו'. והביא לו משל על זה. ענה ואמר והנה טוב מאד. ואמר איני תוקע עצמי באותה חכמה אחר שלא קיבלתיה מפי חכם מקובל. ואם ראיתי באורים על סודות הרמב"ן. הם מגלים טפח ומכסים טפחים. ואמר שחכם אחד פירש הקבלה שלא כד' הרמב"ן. ולכן אמר שדברי החכם ההוא יהיו לו לבדו. וחתם דבריו ולזה אני אומר שאין לסמוך בדברים כאלו אלא מפי חכם מקובל.

**As for what you wrote, that Ze'ir Anpin is the son of Abba and Imma, and that he is the father of the effects that come after him, and he has a sister, his Nukva; all of it is a parable and an allusion concerning the sefirot. As for what you wrote, that no partzuf is to be worshipped, this is known on the lips of all the Kabbalists, and they have no need of your warning. As for what you wrote in the name of the Rambam: "Five are those called heretics, etc." Who is the one who says there is no God, or that there are two, or that He has a body, or that He is not the One alone, or that he worships another besides Him in order to be an intercessor, or the one who says he found ingredients, or the one who says the world was created something from something, God forbid. But a grudge has already risen in your heart, and you study the holy books, take the words in their plain sense, and rely on your understanding. And you forgot what the wisest of the wise said: "and do not lean on your understanding." Since you have already informed me that you understand, resolve my doubts, which I sent you and which I am about to send. As for what you wrote, that you understood that many and great men of wise heart, early and late, withdraw from it: God forbid that there be any sage who withdraws from it. And if there is one who withdraws from it, he himself admits openly that it is from his lack of knowledge of it. As for what you wrote, as the Ribash and the Chavot Yair wrote, you speak falsehood about them. And they are two valid witnesses to testify against you that you speak lies. And these are the words of the Ribash, in brief: "that Rabbi Peretz ha-Kohen did not speak of those sefirot and did not attach importance to them. Also he heard from his mouth that Rabbi Shimshon of Kinon used to say: 'I pray according to the understanding of this child,' that is, to remove from the hearts of the Kabbalists the idea that they pray at one time to one sefirah and at another time to another sefirah. Also in the Eighteen Benedictions they have, in each and every one, an intention toward a known sefirah. And all this is a very strange thing in the eyes of anyone who is not a Kabbalist like them, and they think it is the belief in duality. And he heard one of the would-be philosophers speaking in disparagement of the Kabbalists, and he would say: 'The Christians are believers in the Trinity, and the Kabbalists are believers in the tens.' And he asked the elderly sage Don Yosef ibn Shushan, who was a sage in the Talmud, who had looked into philosophy and was a Kabbalist, pious, great, and scrupulous in the commandments. And he said to him: 'How is it that you Kabbalists direct one blessing to one known sefirah and another blessing to another sefirah. Furthermore, is it so that there are divinities for the sefirot? That a man should pray to them?' And they answered him: 'God forbid that the prayer be anything but to the Name, may He be blessed, the Cause of causes; but one directs the thought to draw the flow to that sefirah which relates to the thing he asks for, just as you would say that in the blessing for the righteous one should direct to the sefirah called Chesed, which is the attribute of mercy, etc.' And he brought him a parable on this. He answered and said: 'And behold, very good.' And he said: 'I do not thrust myself into that wisdom, since I did not receive it from the mouth of a Kabbalist sage. And if I have seen commentaries on the secrets of the Ramban, they reveal a handbreadth and cover handbreadths.' And he said that a certain sage explained the Kabbalah not as the Ramban holds, and therefore he said that the words of that sage shall be his alone." And he ended his words. Therefore I say that one must not rely on such words, except from the mouth of a Kabbalist sage.**
