- Base text from Wikisource; the 1931 scan is not yet collated (Wikisource additions, Q2).
- Ps 120:2 (embedded): משפת שקר, מלשון רמיה. The psalm has 'my soul' where the author writes ויצילנו (us).
- Ps 23:3 (embedded allusion): ינחני במעגלי צדק; the author writes יושר.
- Ps 86:11 (embedded): הוריני ה' דרכיך אהלך באמתך; יחד לבבי ליראה שמך.
- Ps 43:3 (embedded): ושלח אורך ואמתך המה ינחוני.
- Prov 25:11 (embedded): דבר דבור על אופניו. The author prints אפניו; the verse has אופניו.
- Ps 119:22: גל מעלי חרפה ובוז כי עדותיך נצרתי.
- Ps 119:23: גם כי ישבו שרים בי נדברו, עבדך ישיח בחוקיך.
- Ps 119:6 (embedded): אז לא אבוש.
- Deut 11:13: והיה אם שמוע תשמעו, the opening of the second paragraph of the Shema; the author writes לוהיה.
- Deut 13:2-5 (embedded allusion): אות ומופת; לא תשמע אל דברי הנביא ההוא; אחרי ה' אלהיכם תלכו.
- Deut 10:10 (embedded allusion; cf. Deut 9:9): עמדתי בהר ... ארבעים יום וארבעים לילה.
- Deut 30:12: לא בשמים היא, the verse on which Rabbi Yehoshua's saying rests.
- 2:34.199 לבור (printed): probably לעבור, 'to pass from', with the ע dropped (cf. 'to depart from their tradition'); translated by the sense of the context. The Hebrew לבור does not mean 'depart'.

## Chapter 3 — פרק 3 (Milchamot ha-Shem 3:1–3:19)

### Reading text

<sup>3:1</sup> §2. And all the more so we should not believe him when he says that Elijah was revealed to him, or the Elder of Elders, who is Atika Kadisha, which is called Keter Elyon (the Supreme Crown), for surely he is a false prophet, and his death is by strangulation. As is explained in the words of the Rambam in his commentary on the Mishnah, in his introduction to the Order of Zera'im. And in the Gemara, Pesachim 34, we read: "It was stated: the distraction of the mind. Rabbi Yochanan said: a disqualification by impurity, for if Elijah should come and declare it clean and say that impurity had not touched them, we listen to him; and Resh Lakish said: it is a disqualification of the body, for if Elijah should come and declare it clean, we do not listen to him." Thus far his words. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explains: "A disqualification of the body is a special feature in sacred offerings, in that they are disqualified by it; and there the disqualification is in itself; and even if Elijah should come and say that they were not defiled during all those days that he distracted his mind from them, we do not listen to him." Thus far. Hence, anyone who comes to change and to permit what is forbidden, even a rabbinic prohibition, we do not listen to him.

<sup>3:2</sup> §3. And in truth, you began the words of your mouth with folly and wicked madness, in that you said: "How my heart emboldened me to inquire and to investigate, etc." And why not? On the contrary, the reverse is more reasonable (since they say to worship Ze'ir Anpin, who is created, Yosher Levav, folio 3b, and strength to God). It is a complete obligation upon us and upon each and every one of Israel to know the LORD, that He is Creator and not created, and to worship Him, as it is written: "And you shall know this day and take it to your heart." "And you shall know that the LORD your God is God, etc." And it says: "Know the God of your father and worship Him." And the Sages permitted restraining from the forbidden, even in the privy and in the bathhouse, for it is forbidden to meditate in them on words of Torah. And to restrain from the forbidden is permitted. And as to your astonishment, how could they err? There is no wonder in this. Nor is the sect of the later Kabbalists any better, those who went in their simplicity after the command of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar who attributed it to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, and Rabbi Eleazar his son, and his companions of the Great Sanhedrin who sat in the chamber of the Hewn Stone about whom Scripture said: "If a matter is too hard for you in judgment, etc." "And you shall rise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose, etc." "And you shall act according to the word that they tell you, etc." And yet, for all this, the Torah said that if the Great Court erred in a ruling and the people acted on their word, they bring an offering for their error. If they erred in idolatry and ruled, they bring a bull as a burnt offering and a goat as a sin offering, from each tribe. This is what is stated in the parashah of Shelach: "And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done in error." And if in the other offences punishable by karet they erred and ruled, each tribe brings a bull for a sin offering. This is what is stated in the parashah of Vayikra. "And if all the congregation of Israel errs and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly."

<sup>3:3</sup> 4) The authority of our rabbis, the masters of the new Kabbalah, shall not be greater than the authority of the Great Beit Din who sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, and their grasp is no greater than the grasp of the Great Sanhedrin! And yet the Torah said that if they erred and ruled to permit the forbidden, or sinned inadvertently in idolatry, etc. We have learned from the Torah and from our rabbis, in the tractate Horayot, that the Great Beit Din can err and rule a permission in some particular case of idolatry. For man is formed of clay, whether great or small, and is prone to err; therefore the Torah commanded: "If a matter is too hard for you in judgment, etc. and you shall arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose," in order to lessen the error. How is it not impossible that even the Great Beit Din should not err. For it is said in the Torah, "and a matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly. And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done in error." And according to the shortness of our understanding, when we see the great difference between our early rabbis, and how was their faith in the matter of divinity and the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, according to the holy Torah, as explained by Rabbi Bachya, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and Rabbi Yehuda Halevi in the Kuzari and in his prayers, and Rabbi Saadia Gaon in the Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Rambam in his work, and in his commentary on the Mishnah, and in the Moreh Nevukhim. And the Roke'ach in the Gate of Unity, and the Sefer Mitzvot Gadol, and Rabbi Yosef Albo in the Sefer ha-Ikkarim, and Rabbi Meir Aldabi in the Shevilei Emunah. And many others, and likewise the complete ones. And how is it now in the books of our later rabbis, according to the new Kabbalah, which is drawn on from the start of the sixth millennium with cords of falsehood until it became in our time as with cart-ropes, and they believed in many gods. And that the principal point in them, to which all our worship and blessings are directed, is the last partzuf in Emanation, called (quick to anger) Ze'ir Anpin.

<sup>3:4</sup> 5) And this new faith is very far from the way of our holy Torah, written and oral. Therefore we separated ourselves from it, and we clung to the words of our rabbis of blessed memory, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud, Bavli and Yerushalmi, and the decisors, and the midrashim of our famous rabbis, Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma and Yalkut Shimoni, and Midrash ha-Gadol found in Yemen in manuscript, and Nur al-Tzalam, and the like. Also, the remnant of the books of our forebears, the sages of Yemen, we find and see that they adhere to the words of the great ones mentioned above and to their opinions. And when you saw that we separated from the new Kabbalah, your anger burned against us, and in haughtiness of spirit you, the arrogant, smeared falsehood on us. And we asked you to teach us the way: how would the words of our rabbis, the new Kabbalists, agree with the words of our early rabbis mentioned above, and with the words of the Tannaim and the Amoraim. And your answer to us was in the manner of deception and taunts.

<sup>3:5</sup> And for the third time your answer was like the question of one of the four sons: "What is this worship to you? To you and not to him." As if we had not been commanded in the Torah, "And know this day and take it to your heart, that the LORD, He is God, etc." And many verses came in the Torah, in the Prophets and in the Writings on this, and all the more so in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory. You have also returned to be of the company of tellers of evil talk and of those who receive it, when you say that already there are several witnesses against us, that we despise the Sages and can no longer deny it, etc. And it is known and notorious that testimony is accepted only in the presence of the party to the suit. From the Torah, civil cases and capital cases alike require inquiry and examination, as the Rambam of blessed memory wrote in chapter 3 of the Laws of Testimony. But the Sages said, "So that you do not lock the door before borrowers, monetary witnesses do not require inquiry and examination, etc." In what matters is this said? In admissions and loans, gifts and sales. But in fines, inquiry and examination are required, and needless to say in lashes and exile, and in a case of deception, even in civil cases, inquiry and examination are required.

<sup>3:6</sup> §6. And in our case all of them are in it, and how did your heart dare to accept evil talk from foolish men who walk barefoot, like men banned by heaven, and to consider it complete testimony, to hold your fellow in the Torah and in the commandments of Scriptural and rabbinic law as apikorsim and heretics, who are among those whom one lowers and does not raise? And it is known and notorious that this generation, a generation of vanity and falsehood, and it is among the princes of Israel, and each one takes pride in the disgrace of his fellow and of his teacher, whom they set up in their examination; 'orah' means Torah. And on those who make nights as days, and those who toil for the Torah, so that it not be forgotten from Israel according to their ability, you poured out contempt, and you made the students of the Torah and those who hold to it despised and lowly, like a vessel in which there is no delight. And all who do evil are good in your eyes, and more honored than them, and by means of false rumors you made the students of Torah a disgrace in the eyes of all who see them, until they came to a very low rank, that the ignorant boast of themselves, saying, "Happy are we, how good is our portion and pleasant our sleep until the rising of the sun, and we shall inherit honor more than those who stand in the house of the LORD at night"; to fulfill what was said, "And if you despise My statutes, if you despise those who teach My statutes," as the Rambam of blessed memory wrote in the Laws of the Study of Torah.

<sup>3:7</sup> §7. And these are the words of the Kabbalist, the author of Heikhal ha-Berakhah: "A positive commandment on the court to inquire into and to examine the witnesses with seven inquiries, etc. There are also examinations, which are questions: what clothing he wore; the dust of the ground on which he stood, whether black, or sand, or clay; and if they contradict one another, the testimony is void. From the roots of this commandment: the included bride, the beautiful young maiden who has no eyes, the governance of this world, that there be free choice, whose eyes are like doves, a deception to the sons of man. Her eyes in the Palace of Merit: the eyes of the congregation, who judge with knowledge on the testimony of two witnesses, two crowns; and the Da'at is the secret of the eyes, as is known; and this light spreads in seven aspects, etc." See there. And concerning the commandment "You shall not go about as a talebearer," he wrote, and these are his words: " that one should not tell his fellow that his adversary has spoken evil about him, as it is said, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer.' And among the laws of the commandment: even though he speaks the truth, there is a great sin in this. And also within the scope of this prohibition: that one should not speak in disparagement of his fellow, even if true, and this is as if he denied the fundamental principle, etc." And he expanded further on the punishment of the one who tells slander and on the reward of the one who guards from it; see there.

<sup>3:8</sup> §8. And in the warning, "You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow," he wrote: "even standing by, to any degree. You shall not see your fellow's distress when one puts him to shame, and you are silent; they stood and answered no more. But you shall protest with all your power against him who disgraces your fellow, or speaks about him with talebearing and slander; you shall not be one who hears and is silent, but you shall say to him: 'Wicked one, troubler of Israel, why do you speak defiance against the likeness of our Maker, and against the Shekhinah of our strength, which is the yod in "among your people," and departs through this sin.' Therefore this was juxtaposed to that, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer,' and you might say: since I do not speak, I will listen and be silent, and take pleasure in what his fellow, a wicked man, speaks. This listener too is an utterly wicked person. And he transgresses 'You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow.' And he has no portion in the God of Israel when he hears a wicked one speak defiance against a righteous person, or whisper a whisper of lies about his fellow; rather, you shall immediately push him away and say to him: 'Wicked one, go away from me, I do not listen to you.' But if he hears and is silent, and all the more so if he takes pleasure, his end is to be judged in unblown fire, and he will not merit to stand in the company of the righteous, as listener, as answerer, as speaker. All of them shall perish from the world in this one, and in the world to come." Thus far his words.

<sup>3:9</sup> 9) And you, our friend, it was not enough for you that you did not do any one of all these but you believed their words and accepted their lies on the testimony of one witness and one judge and not in the presence of the litigant without inquiry, without investigation, without examination and you enjoyed their words and you also helped to strengthen their lies and it was fixed in your mind as the truth itself until you wrote that I am no longer able to deny it, etc. And you did not take to heart that testimony is accepted only in the presence of the litigant and that you are obliged to investigate and inquire into them with seven inquiries, investigations and examinations, as you are commanded. All the more so, since they did their deeds in the dark and smoothed their tongues to you in secret with their words to find a fault to hate and you were obliged to silence them with a rebuke. This is nothing but wickedness of heart: that you enjoy and long for their gossip and their informing. The Merciful One save us from this opinion! And it is possible that you too add of your own false informing, in order to honor yourself at the disgrace of your friends. And in the chapter Arvei Pesachim (115) we read: "Rav Sheshet said in the name of R. A.: whoever tells evil talk and whoever bears false witness against his fellow deserves to be thrown to the dogs, as it is said: 'to the dog you shall throw it' and it is written explicitly: 'you shall not carry a false report'; and it is read in it: 'you shall not cause to bear'". And we find several more homilies of our Rabbis of blessed memory on the punishment of one who tells evil talk. And in Machzor Vitry, tractate Avot, on what we learned, "do not judge your fellow until you reach his place", he writes, see there: "that the same transgression may come into your hand and you may be saved and escape from it, as we find with Jeroboam son of Nebat, that when Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh, she brought in to him every kind of song in the world and said to him: 'So they do for such-and-such idolatry'. One time, he went to sleep, and the day grew late. She went and called the wood-carvers and the builders, who do the work of the craftsman and the designer, and they made over his bed the likeness of a firmament, and in it the sun, the moon, the stars and the constellations. In the morning he woke from his sleep to open the doors of the Temple, for the keys of the Temple were under his pillow. He saw that the firmament was bright with stars and the host, thinking that the night had not yet passed, he went back to sleep. And he slept four more hours, until he understood and recognised for himself that the night was not so long. And concerning that hour we learned a testimony about the morning daily offering, that was offered at four hours, in the Bechirta. Before he woke from his sleep, Jeroboam son of Nebat went to the door of his house, and a voice passed: 'Wicked one, how long will you sleep and neglect the morning daily offering? What is the matter with you, sleeper? Arise, call upon your God!' A bat kol came out and said to him: 'Wicked one, son of a wicked one, you are destined to abolish from Israel many, many offerings wilfully. And you hold him liable for the inadvertent as for the wilful. And for the coerced as for the voluntary!' And this is what is written: 'When Ephraim spoke there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel, but he incurred guilt through Baal and died'. This is said of Jeroboam, who was of the tribe of Ephraim, the trembling was the accuser against Solomon, he, Jeroboam, was prince in Israel and king, and the bat kol answered him that he would become guilty through Baal and die." Thus far his words. And you have done greatly and added to doing evil more than Jeroboam son of Nebat. For after you brought us to the prison by false informing before our exalted government! You called out all the people to go out to the cemetery, and commanded them to throw dust upon their heads for no reason. Not for a light commandment that we neglected, and not for a weighty commandment, God forbid, but because we walked according to the customs of our forefathers and set our learning in the Mishnah and in the Talmud and the Rambam and Shulchan Aruch to learn and to teach, to keep and to do. And we did not study further in a forged book, the book the Zohar, as is your custom.

<sup>3:10</sup> §10. And now, with the help of the Name, may He be blessed, let us return to the main point of our question, which we asked you to inform us according to the system of the Kabbalists, whom do we call upon in our prayers, and bless all our blessings and our worship, and from whom do we seek forgiveness and atonement. And your answer was in the words of a grumbler, like ravers: he claimed wheat from him, and he admitted barley to him, and you deny what is known and famous in their books to all, like one who swears about the man that he is a woman, and about the woman that she is a man, and about a pillar of marble that it is gold. And your anger burned against the book Metzaref ha-Emunah, and you mocked it and scorned it, and you called it the book the Mesharef etc., and thereby you revealed to all that you are the one who scorns the sages; and as to our questions: since Ze'ir Anpin, according to their words, is our God, and he feeds us and sustains us, and Him we worship; if so, all the worlds above the World of Emanation, who feeds and sustains them? If he casts their flow and their sustenance from below upward, and they worship and bow down to him, or perhaps their God fed and sustained them, he being the First Cause, and Him they worship, and we worship Ze'ir Anpin, who feeds us and sustains us? And if so, is the God of the upper ones not the God of the lower ones, God forbid? And this is the point of contradiction which we asked you to inform us and to instruct us, and to this your answer came: that the case is not like the proof, and does one bring proof to overturn a halakha given to Moses at Sinai? And that the sages of Kabbalah say thus: they received it from Moses.

<sup>3:11</sup> §11. We are very astonished and amazed at your words and at this reply of yours, and is it a halakha given to Moses at Sinai to believe in many divinities? And to worship other gods apart from the LORD our God, the First, and Rock of all? And He is the cause of all causes, all of them, and with deceit you came in these replies of yours to stubborn-hearted people, whom you boasted over, and showed them these words of yours, saying: "See, I have overturned their words, and rejected their proofs in haste," and your pamphlet goes round to all the diners, and after they praised and lauded you, that you are sharp and keen, you brought it to us. And behold, all of it is deceptions, as if you did not know what our question turns on, and to this false error of yours we shall return again, since it is known and famous in the rules of the decisors (Kenesset ha-Gedolah, the Radbaz, and Sh"Z), that wherever the Kabbalah disagrees with the ruling, one goes after the ruling, and this rule is famous in Israel. And if your words are that this Kabbalah is a halakha given to Moses at Sinai, and do you reject a halakha given to Moses on account of the reasoning of some tanna or amora, and all the more so a later decisor (see below, §15), and you must bring a proof and inform us where we have found this, that any tanna or amora would be so bold to dispute and to rule against the halakha received from Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. Would he not be called a fool, or a wicked and arrogant man? And in many places in the Talmud it is a saying in the mouths of the Rabbis to say: "If it is a halakha, we accept it, and if it is reasoning, there is an answer."

<sup>3:12</sup> §12. Behold, then, surely all your words are exaggerations and hyperboles, to alarm the fools and the madmen who love wonders and impossibilities, and you speak without knowledge. And all your words are without reason. And in deceit you refuse to know the LORD, as the prophet Jeremiah, peace be upon him, said in the name of the LORD: "Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they have refused to know Me, declares the LORD." And already one of the deceivers among you has said: "We know that the truth is with you." But what business is it of yours to reveal this matter and to publicize it to some of the students. It would be better for you to leave them in their error entirely, as the words of the wicked one among the four sons, who says: "What is this service to you? etc." And the proof that you daub whitewash: for in this letter of yours you published that the Rabbi, the author of Matzref ha-Emunah, is, God forbid, a heretic and a denier. And you called his book Mesharef ha-Emunah. And he, in his integrity, walks without turning aside from the words of the Zohar, and Mikdash Melekh, and Kisse Eliyahu, and the RaShB, and Yosher Levav, and Sefer ha-Berit, and Rabbi the Ari, and Rabbi Chayyim Vital in the book Etz Chayyim, and Nachalat Yosef, and their finest flour, to the right or to the left. As will be explained below, and first I will bring you several proofs. This Kabbalah is not a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai, for our Rabbis of blessed memory said in Eruvin: "Any baraita that is not taught in the house of Rabbi Oshaya, it is not a baraita, and you may not object from it, for it is corrupted." Thus, any baraita that did not enter the study-house of Rabbi Chiyya or of Rabbi Oshaya, not only is it not a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai. But one may not even raise an objection from it against an Amora. And in the Yerushalmi, Eruvin, chapter one, in the passage de-Lechayyim, it is written. And these are his words: "Acha said to him: So said Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: any mishnah that did not enter the fellowship, one does not rely on it." Thus far. And see below, §42. And in an old notebook of the compositions of our forefathers I found written in the name of Rabbi Saadia Gaon, and these are his words: "The book Shiur Komah: no trustworthy transmission has come down concerning it, for it is not in the Mishnah and not in the Talmud. And there is no proof by which we can infer whether Rabbi Ishmael truly said it, or another said it and ascribed it to him, as many of the forged books are ascribed to some of the famous scholars." Thus far his words. (Translation by the Rabbi, the author: "The book Shiur Komah: we have no tradition concerning it from the sages of our faith, since it is neither in the Mishnah nor in the Talmud, and also there is no proof to be drawn from it whether Rabbi Ishmael truly said it, or others besides him said it and ascribed it to Rabbi Ishmael, as they ascribe many of the books that were made to some of the famous sages.")

<sup>3:13</sup> 13) We learned from the words of the Gaon that there are many books that are ascribed to the names of the great sages of Israel (falsely), for the sake of some benefit that accrues to them, and we learned also that whatever is not stated explicitly in the Mishnah and in the Gemara, and that we see is the opposite of the plain sense of the Talmud, is not a tradition, and we do not rely on it. And for this reason no decisors rule from the midrashim where they disagree with the Talmud, and even the Jerusalem Talmud we do not heed where it disagrees with the Babylonian, on which all the house of Israel rely, both for leniency and for stringency, as all this is made clear in the words of our rabbis the decisors in several places. And see below, §42, what I wrote there in the name of the Rosh, and go and learn from what Rabbeinu Tam ben Yichya wrote, cited in the book Rivid ha-Zahav in the laws of Passover, and these are his words: "In our time knowledge has ceased, and the hidden matters of the Torah have been hidden from the eyes of every living thing; no man knows the order of this wisdom; and whoever holds to this, there befalls him a great share of the harm and the danger (that is to say, the harm and the danger of heresy, in that there is no share for him in the God of Israel). And concerning such things our Rabbis of blessed memory warned us, 'Do not seek what is too wondrous for you, and do not inquire into what is hidden from you.' And it is enough for us what the sages of the true tradition, agreed upon from every side, have taught us in the explanation of the Torah and its commandments. According to the tradition, from man to man, until the days of Moses; and it is called the Oral Torah, on account of which Moses went up on high and stood there forty days to learn its general principles and its particulars by the rules transmitted to him from the mouth of the Power. And with these matters we are bound to occupy ourselves, for they are our life and the length of our days, and in not one of them shall we err. His one law is to put to death whoever defies their word, and whoever transgresses the words of the Sages is liable to death. But the remaining allusions in them, which the sages of Kabbalah did not exhaust in their lifetimes, although they are hidden matters of the Torah and matters of the intellect; we were not commanded concerning them. For these remained for the select few to be occupied with them, in the times that were before us, etc. And not everyone who wishes to take the Name takes it. For these are matters that are like its furnace; they are so forever. And in our time the merit of the fathers has ended, and no one holds this wisdom justly: on the contrary, they destroy the corners of the Torah, and its pillars shudder at the sound of the trumpeters; the blind, who pass over, do not know the way where light dwells; they grope like the blind, and weary themselves seeking the door. And where they thought to gain, suddenly they shall be broken, and there is no healing. And many of the unlearned boast, saying: 'The secret of the LORD is ours; the upper waters are our heritage, not yours, you masters of the Talmud who walk in darkness.' Their heart is not with their people; their eyes are plastered over, so that they cannot see, and the word is not in them; they are wise to do harm to themselves. For they hold fast to what the hand of their intellect is too short to reach. And they want to climb the rungs; it is not in their power to reach the goal. And they bring up a potsherd in their hands to scrape with it. And they become a snare to them, etc. For there comes out from them a stumbling-block, to breach the fence of the Torah and to tear down its walls. One boasts of what he does not understand, and errs in the beginnings of the Torah and its roots, and comes to heresy. And he is distanced from the haven of his desire, which is the nearness of God; it would have been better for him had he not been created, all the more so to change a midrash and to annul a halakhah." Thus far his words.

<sup>3:14</sup> §14. See and understand, our friend the pleasant reader, how our honored Rabbi Tam, the aforementioned, cried out like a herald against those who engage in the new Kabbalah, for they breached the fences of the Torah, and laid bare, laid bare, its foundations and its roots in the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, as will be explained below. Instead of thinking to draw near to the Name, may He be blessed, they strayed from the way and came to believe in many other gods, and to worship them! And like the words of Rabbi Tam ben Yachya, Mahari Albo also wrote in the Ikkarim, chapter 28, of the second. And further he expounded at length in the book Ravid ha-Zahav, and also brought the words of the great Rabbi Maharshal, in his responsa and in the work Yam shel Shlomo, against those who boast of the novelties they study in Kabbalah. And he wrote that since the Talmud was sealed, we may not be stringent against the Gemara, and it is like heresy, as explained at length in Chok Ya'akov, section 489, subsection 11. All this is according to the assumption and the ascription whereby they ascribed the Zohar to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the Tanna, but after the criticism which the wise of heart examined and investigated after him, from whose womb the things mentioned in it came out, and when the work mentioned came out, and from whose hand it came out, it was explained very plainly that it is a work of one of the latter ones, and those ideas did not come out of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the Tanna, peace be upon him, at all, for in it are found many things in the fundamentals of the faith of our holy Torah contrary to the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in the Talmud and in the Midrashim of our Rabbis of blessed memory, famous in Israel, certainly one must not rely on it in any matter touching the customs of Israel that our forebears practised. And the sages of the Middle Ages did not do well, who changed upon us several things in the prayer books, according to the Zohar and the Kabbalists, for some of those changes lead to heresy, to believe in many powers and to worship other gods, as will be explained below.

<sup>3:15</sup> §15. Also the Rav Ravid ha-Zahav brought further the words of Maran in Beit Yosef, who was concerned about the words of the Zohar in a place where the Gemara does not mention anything contrary to its words. And the Rema, of blessed memory, wrote about him that although the Gemara does not mention anything contrary to its words, there is no basis for this in the words of the decisors, and one need not be concerned with the words of the Zohar, see there. Further he brought the words of the Radbaz, of blessed memory, that he wrote that every matter mentioned in the Gemara or in one of the decisors or the masters of the halakhot, even if it be contrary to what is written in the books of Kabbalah, I rule on it, both to be lenient and to be strict, and I will not be concerned with what is written in those books. As for myself, if it is a stringency, I follow it and if a leniency, I will not be concerned with it. Further he wrote in the name of the Ra'em and other decisors that one need not be concerned about the words of the Kabbalists against any decisor, see there. Say now, that from the words of the decisors mentioned in the responsum of the Rav Ravid ha-Zahav, and they are Maran, of blessed memory, and Moreinu ha-Rav Moshe, and the Radbaz, and the Kenesset ha-Gedolah, and Mahari ha-Levi, K., Maharash ha-Levi and Rabbi Eliyahu ha-Levi, and Rabbi Moshe Alkaboli, and Rabbi Tam ben Yachya, and the Rav Chok Ya'akov, and Maharshal, and Maharam al-Shakar, who say that one need not be concerned with the words of the Zohar and the Kabbalists, when they are against the Mishnah and the Talmud, and even against a single decisor. Behold, from this prove to yourself that you wrote that they are a law of Moses from Sinai, that your words are a fabrication and utter folly.

### Chapter 3 by paragraph

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:1

> ב) וכ"ש שלא נאמין לו באמרו שנגלה אליו אליהו או סבא דסבין, שהוא עתיקא קדישא הנקרא כתר עליון, דודאי נביא שקר הוא ובמיתתו בחנק. כמבואה בדברי הרמב"ם בפי' המשנה בהקדמתו לסדר זרעים. ובגמ' פסחים (לד) גרס' אמתר הסח הדעת ר' יוחנן אמר פסול טומאה, שאם יבוא אליהו ויטהרנה ויאמר שלא נגעה טומאה בהן שומעין לו, ור"ל אמר פסול הגוף הוי, שאם יבוא אליהו ויטהרנה אין שומעין לו עכ"ל, ופי' רשי ז"ל פיסול הגוף מעלה היא בקדשים היא שנפסלין בכך, ושם פיסול הוא לעצמו, ואפי' אם יבוא אליהו ויאמר שלא נטמאו כל רותן הימים שהסיח דעתו מהן אין שומעין לו ע"כ, אלמלא כל הבא לשנות ולהתיר את האסור, אפי' איסור דרבנן אין שומעין לו.

**§2. And all the more so we should not believe him when he says that Elijah was revealed to him, or the Elder of Elders, who is Atika Kadisha, which is called Keter Elyon (the Supreme Crown), for surely he is a false prophet, and his death is by strangulation. As is explained in the words of the Rambam in his commentary on the Mishnah, in his introduction to the Order of Zera'im. And in the Gemara, Pesachim 34, we read: "It was stated: the distraction of the mind. Rabbi Yochanan said: a disqualification by impurity, for if Elijah should come and declare it clean and say that impurity had not touched them, we listen to him; and Resh Lakish said: it is a disqualification of the body, for if Elijah should come and declare it clean, we do not listen to him." Thus far his words. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explains: "A disqualification of the body is a special feature in sacred offerings, in that they are disqualified by it; and there the disqualification is in itself; and even if Elijah should come and say that they were not defiled during all those days that he distracted his mind from them, we do not listen to him." Thus far. Hence, anyone who comes to change and to permit what is forbidden, even a rabbinic prohibition, we do not listen to him.**

Grammar:

- שלא נאמין לו: 'that we should not believe him', a clause with שלא and the imperfect after כ"ש, 'all the more so'.
- סבא דסבין is Aramaic: 'the Elder of Elders', with the Aramaic relative ד and the title given as a name-like epithet.
- The Talmud passage is quoted with 'גרס' (גרסינן, 'we read'); the closing 'עכ"ל' ends it, and 'ע"כ' ends Rashi's words after it.
- שאם in the two rulings is explanatory, 'for if': Elijah's testimony is offered as the test of whether the disqualification is one of impurity or of the body. הסח הדעת is a noun phrase, 'the distraction of the mind'.
- ויטהרנה: the verb with the object suffix -נה; the English 'declare it clean' takes the suffix as 'it'.

Note: The paragraph has three parts: the refusal to believe the claimed revelation, a Talmud passage with Resh Lakish's view, and Rashi's explanation with the conclusion. The Hebrew is the Wikisource base text.

Apparatus:

- Base text: Wikisource edition, translated as base text and flagged until the 1931 scan is collated (decisions, Q2).
- Rambam: his commentary on the Mishnah, introduction to Zera'im, as the author gives it (no chapter or page).
- Pesachim (לד): the author's '34' as written; the quotation as he gives it, not checked against the Talmud text.
- אמתר (3:1.37): printed word, not a word of the Gemara; translated 'It was stated' on the likelier אתמר (letters transposed); the alternative is the bare transliteration 'Amtar'.
- רותן (3:1.92): printed word; translated 'those' on the likelier אותן, which the context requires ('all those days that he distracted his mind from them'); the alternative is 'their [unclear]'.
- אלמלא (3:1.101): printed word ('if not for'); translated 'Hence' on the likelier אלמא ('so it follows'); with אלמלא the sentence has no main clause.
- ושם (3:1.80) in Rashi: 'and there' (chosen) or 'and the name' ('and the name of disqualification is in itself').

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:2

> ג) ובאמת שהחלת דברי פיך סכלות והוללות רעה שאמרת איך מלאני לבי לדרוש ולחקור וכו' ולמה לא? אדרבא איפכא מסתברא (כיון שאומרים לעבוד לז"א שהוא נברא יושר לבב דף ג' ע"ב ועוז לאלוהים). חוב גמור עלינו ועל כל אחד ואחד בישראל לדעת את ה' שהוא בורא ולא נברא ולעבדו ככתוב וידעת היום והשבות אל לבבך. וידעת כי ה' אלהיך הוא האלהים וכו' ואומר דע את אלהי אביך ועבדהו. והתירו חכמים לאפרושי מאיסורא אפי' בבית הכסא ובבית המרחץ שאסור להרהר בהם בדברי תורה. ולאפרושי מאיסורא שרי. ועל תמיהתך איך יטעו? אין זה פלא. ולא עדיפי כת המקובלים האחרונים אשר הלכו לתומם אחרי צו של הפילוסוף מחבר הזהר שתלאו ברשב"י ור' אלעזר בנו וחביריו מסנהדרי גדולה היושבים בלשכת הגזית שעליהם אמר הכתוב כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט וכו' וקמת ועלית אל המקום אשר יבחר ה' אלוהיך וכו' ועשית על פי הדבר אשר יגידו לך וכו'. ועם כל זה אמרה תורה שאם שגגו ב"ד הגדול בהוראה ועשו העם על פיהם מביאים קרבן על שגגם. אם בע"ז שגגו והורו מביאים פר לעולה ושעיר לחטאת מכל שבט ושבט. והוא האמור בפרשת שלח והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה, ואם בשאר כריתות שגגו והורו מביא כל שבט ושבט פר לחטאת והוא האמור בפרשת ויקרא. ואם כל עדת ישראל ישגו ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל.

**§3. And in truth, you began the words of your mouth with folly and wicked madness, in that you said: "How my heart emboldened me to inquire and to investigate, etc." And why not? On the contrary, the reverse is more reasonable (since they say to worship Ze'ir Anpin, who is created, Yosher Levav, folio 3b, and strength to God). It is a complete obligation upon us and upon each and every one of Israel to know the LORD, that He is Creator and not created, and to worship Him, as it is written: "And you shall know this day and take it to your heart." "And you shall know that the LORD your God is God, etc." And it says: "Know the God of your father and worship Him." And the Sages permitted restraining from the forbidden, even in the privy and in the bathhouse, for it is forbidden to meditate in them on words of Torah. And to restrain from the forbidden is permitted. And as to your astonishment, how could they err? There is no wonder in this. Nor is the sect of the later Kabbalists any better, those who went in their simplicity after the command of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar who attributed it to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, and Rabbi Eleazar his son, and his companions of the Great Sanhedrin who sat in the chamber of the Hewn Stone about whom Scripture said: "If a matter is too hard for you in judgment, etc." "And you shall rise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose, etc." "And you shall act according to the word that they tell you, etc." And yet, for all this, the Torah said that if the Great Court erred in a ruling and the people acted on their word, they bring an offering for their error. If they erred in idolatry and ruled, they bring a bull as a burnt offering and a goat as a sin offering, from each tribe. This is what is stated in the parashah of Shelach: "And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done in error." And if in the other offences punishable by karet they erred and ruled, each tribe brings a bull for a sin offering. This is what is stated in the parashah of Vayikra. "And if all the congregation of Israel errs and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly."**

Grammar:

- שהחלת דברי פיך סכלות והוללות רעה: echoes Eccl 10:13; 'folly and wicked madness' is what they began with, and 'שאמרת' ('in that you said') introduces the reader's own words.
- איך מלאני לבי לדרוש ולחקור: the infinitives לדרוש and לחקור follow 'emboldened me'; the reader's question is closed by 'וכו'' and the author's reply begins with 'ולמה לא'.
- ועוז לאלוהים sits in the author's parenthesis and no formula introduces it, so it takes no quotation marks; the parenthesis is kept as written.
- לאפרושי מאיסורא: Aramaic causative infinitive, 'to restrain (someone) from a prohibition'; the author's point is that the Sages allowed even speech of Torah in the forbidden places to restrain from a transgression.
- ואומר: 'and it says' introduces a verse; 'ועבדהו' is the verb 'worship' with the object suffix -הו, 'worship him'.
- The conditional clauses (אם שגגו ... מביאים; ואם שגגו ... מביא) are built on perfects of 'to err' with present-tense apodosis, as the verses have them.

Ancient Near East:

- The Hall of Hewn Stone (lishkat ha-gazit) is the chamber where the Great Sanhedrin sat, in the rabbinic account of the Temple; the author uses it to set the Sanhedrin against the circle he attacks.

Apparatus:

- Deut 4:39: 'וידעת היום והשבות אל לבבך', quoted with 'ככתוב'.
- Deut 7:9: 'וידעת כי ה' אלהיך הוא האלהים', quoted with 'וכו''.
- 1 Chr 28:9: 'דע את אלהי אביך ועבדהו', quoted with 'ואומר'.
- Eccl 10:13: 'תחלת דברי פיהו סכלות ואחרית פיהו הוללות רעה', echoed in 'שהחלת דברי פיך סכלות והוללות רעה' (an allusion, no quotation marks).
- Esth 7:5: 'אשר מלאו לבו לעשות כן', echoed in 'מלאני לבי' (cf.).
- ועוז לאלוהים in the parenthesis: no formula marks it, so no quotation marks; possibly Ps 68:35 ('תנו עוז לאלהים') or Ps 62:12 ('כי עז לאלהים'); not verified.
- יושר לבב דף ג' ע"ב: a book title with the author's folio, as written; no text of the book is quoted here.
- Deut 17:8: 'כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט' and 'וקמת ועלית אל המקום אשר יבחר ה' אלהיך'. Deut 17:10: 'ועשית על פי הדבר אשר יגידו לך'. The author writes 'אלוהיך' for 'אלהיך'; the English follows the verse.
- Num 15:24: 'והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה'.
- Lev 4:13: 'ואם כל עדת ישראל ישגו ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל'.
- לאפרושי (3:2.71, 83): read as causative, 'to restrain'; the alternative is the reflexive 'to abstain'.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:3

> ד) ולא יהא כח רבותינו בעלי הקבלה החדשה גדול מכח ב"ד הגדול היושבים בלשכת הגזית ולא השגתם יתירה מהשגת סנהדרי גדולה! ועם כל זה אמרה תורה שאם טעו והורו להתיר את האסור, או שגגו בע"ז וכו'. למדנו מן התורה ומרבותינו במסכת הוריות, שאפשר לב"ד הגדול לטעות ולהורות התר באיזה פרט בע"ז. כי האדם קורץ מחומר בין גדול בין קטן, ועלול הוא לטעות, ולכן צותה תורה כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט וכו' וקמת ועלית אל המקום אשר יבחר ה' אלהיך כדי למעט הטעות. איך אינו נמנע שלא יטעו אפי' ב"ד הגדול. שהרי נאמר בתורה ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל. והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה. ולפי קוצר דעתינו בראותינו ההפרש הגדול שיש בין רבותינו הראשונים ואיך היתה אמונתם בענין האלוהות ויחוד השי"ת על פי תוה"ק כמבואר בר' בחיי בעל חובת הלבבות ור' יהודה הלוי בספר הכוזרי ובתפלותיו ור' סעדיה גאון בס' האמונות והדעות והרמב"ם בחיבורו ובפי' המשנה ובס' מורה הנבוכים. והרוקח בשער הייחוד, וס' מצות הגדול ורבי יוסף אלבו בספר העיקרים, ור' מאיר אלדבי בספר שבילי אמונה. וזולתם רבים וכן שלימים. ואיך הוא עתה בספרי רבותינו האחרונים ע"פ הקבלה החדשה הנמשכת מתחלת אלף השישי בחבלי השוא עד שנעשית בזמנינו כעבות העגלה והאמינו באלהים רבים. ושהעיקר בהם אשר אליו כל עבודתינו וברכותינו הוא הפרצוף האחרון שבאצילות הנקרא (קצר אפים) זעיר אנפין.

**4) The authority of our rabbis, the masters of the new Kabbalah, shall not be greater than the authority of the Great Beit Din who sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, and their grasp is no greater than the grasp of the Great Sanhedrin! And yet the Torah said that if they erred and ruled to permit the forbidden, or sinned inadvertently in idolatry, etc. We have learned from the Torah and from our rabbis, in the tractate Horayot, that the Great Beit Din can err and rule a permission in some particular case of idolatry. For man is formed of clay, whether great or small, and is prone to err; therefore the Torah commanded: "If a matter is too hard for you in judgment, etc. and you shall arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose," in order to lessen the error. How is it not impossible that even the Great Beit Din should not err. For it is said in the Torah, "and a matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly. And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done in error." And according to the shortness of our understanding, when we see the great difference between our early rabbis, and how was their faith in the matter of divinity and the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, according to the holy Torah, as explained by Rabbi Bachya, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and Rabbi Yehuda Halevi in the Kuzari and in his prayers, and Rabbi Saadia Gaon in the Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Rambam in his work, and in his commentary on the Mishnah, and in the Moreh Nevukhim. And the Roke'ach in the Gate of Unity, and the Sefer Mitzvot Gadol, and Rabbi Yosef Albo in the Sefer ha-Ikkarim, and Rabbi Meir Aldabi in the Shevilei Emunah. And many others, and likewise the complete ones. And how is it now in the books of our later rabbis, according to the new Kabbalah, which is drawn on from the start of the sixth millennium with cords of falsehood until it became in our time as with cart-ropes, and they believed in many gods. And that the principal point in them, to which all our worship and blessings are directed, is the last partzuf in Emanation, called (quick to anger) Ze'ir Anpin.**

Literal: 4) and-not will-be authority of-our-rabbis masters-of the-Kabbalah the-new greater than-the-authority-of Beit-Din the-great who-sit in-the-chamber-of the-hewn-stone and-not their-grasp greater than-the-grasp-of Sanhedrin the-great! and-yet all this said the-Torah that-if erred and-ruled to-permit the forbidden or sinned-inadvertently in-idolatry etc. we-learned from the-Torah and-from our-rabbis in the-tractate Horayot that-possible for-the-Beit-Din the-great to-err and-to-rule permission in-which particular-case in-idolatry. for man is-formed of-clay whether great or small and-prone he to-err therefore commanded the-Torah that is-too-hard for-you a-matter for-judgment etc. and-you-shall-arise and-go-up to the-place which will-choose the-LORD your-God in-order to-lessen the-error how is-it-not impossible that-not they-would-err even Beit-Din the-great for-behold it-is-said in-the-Torah and-is-hidden a-matter from-the-eyes-of the-assembly and-it-shall-be if from-the-eyes-of the-congregation was-done in-error and-according-to the-shortness-of our-understanding when-we-see the-difference the-great that-there-is between our-rabbis the-early and-how was their-faith in-the-matter-of the-divinity and-the-unity the-Name-may-He-be-blessed according-to the-mouth-of the-holy-Torah as-explained by-Rabbi Bachya the-author-of Chovot ha-Levavot and-Rabbi Yehuda Halevi in-the-book the-Kuzari and-in-his-prayers and-Rabbi Saadia Gaon in-the-book the-Emunot and-the-De'ot and-the-Rambam in-his-work and-in-the-commentary of-the-Mishnah and-in-the-book Moreh Nevukhim and-the-Roke'ach in-the-gate of-unity and-the-book-of Mitzvot the-great and-Rabbi Yosef Albo in-the-book the-Ikkarim and-Rabbi Meir Aldabi in-the-book Shevilei Emunah and-others many and-so-too the-complete-ones and-how it now in-the-books-of our-rabbis the-later according-to the-Kabbalah the-new drawn-out from-the-start-of the-thousand the-sixth with-cords-of falsehood until it-became in-our-time as-with cart-ropes and-they-believed in-gods many and-that the-principal in-them to-which all our-worship and-our-blessings is the-partzuf the-last in-Emanation called quick to-anger Ze'ir Anpin

Grammar:

- ולא יהא כח ... גדול מכח: a negated future (יהא) with a comparison; the English keeps the repeated 'the authority of' so that the comparison is plain.
- איך אינו נמנע שלא יטעו: נמנע is 'impossible', so the clause says that it is impossible for even the Great Beit Din not to err, that is, error is unavoidable; the full stop of the Hebrew is kept and the English keeps 'How is it not ...'.
- Three Torah passages are cited: Deut 17:8 (quoted, with וכו' as the author's truncation sign), Lev 4:13 and Num 15:24 (introduced by שהרי נאמר בתורה and continued by והיה).
- The long period ולפי קוצר דעתינו ... is divided at 'when we see' and 'how was their faith'; no clause is dropped and the order of the list of authors is kept. It has no main clause of its own: the main clause is ואמונה זו החדשה רחוקה מאד in 3:4.

Note: Plain sentences follow the Hebrew full stops. The Torah quotations take double quotation marks; the author's וכו' is kept as 'etc.'. The list of authors is elliptical in the Hebrew after the full stop at הנבוכים, and the English keeps that ellipsis. The period that begins ולפי קוצר דעתינו has no main clause here; 3:4 supplies it.

Ancient Near East:

- The Chamber of Hewn Stone (lishkat ha-gazit): the chamber in the Temple where the Great Court sat, as the author's words place it. The Hebrew gives no further detail.

Apparatus:

- Base text: Wikisource; not yet collated with the 1931 scan (open question 2), so the English is the base text as it stands.
- Printed list marker ד) (the fourth item) opens the paragraph; the next paragraph opens ה) (the fifth item).
- Deut 17:8, quoted with 'etc.' marking the author's omission (וכו').
- Lev 4:13, quoted: ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל.
- Num 15:24, quoted: והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה.
- Isa 5:18, embedded allusion (no quotation marks): בחבלי השוא and כעבות העגלה; הנמשכת echoes משכי in the same verse.
- Prov 14:17, for the author's קצר אפים, set against ארך אפים in Exod 34:6.
- Job 33:6, embedded allusion (no quotation marks): קורץ מחומר echoes מחמר קרצתי, 'formed from clay'.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:4

> ה) ואמונה זו החדשה רחוקה מאד מדרך תורתינו הק' שבכתב ושבעל פה. ולכן פירשנו עצמינו ממנה ודבקנו בדברי רבותינו ז"ל בעלי המשנה והתלמוד בבלי וירושלמי והפוסקים ומדרשי רבותינו המפורסמים, מדרש רבה ותנחומא וילקוט שמעוני ומדרש הגדול המצוי בתימן בכת"י, ונור אלצלאם וכיוצא בהם. גם שארית חבורי קדמונינו חכמי תימן מצינו וראינו שהם אדוקים בדברי הגדולים הנזכרים לעיל ובדעותיהם. וכראותכם שפירשנו מן הקבלה החדשה חרה אפכם בנו, וברמות רוחא טפלתם עלינו שקר זדים. ושאלנו אתכם להורותינו הדרך איך יסכימו דברי רבותינו המקובלים החדשים עם דברי רבותינו הראשונים הנזכרים לעיל, ועם דברי התנאים והאמוראים. והיתה תשובתכם אלינו בדרך הטעאה וקינטורים.

**5) And this new faith is very far from the way of our holy Torah, written and oral. Therefore we separated ourselves from it, and we clung to the words of our rabbis of blessed memory, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud, Bavli and Yerushalmi, and the decisors, and the midrashim of our famous rabbis, Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma and Yalkut Shimoni, and Midrash ha-Gadol found in Yemen in manuscript, and Nur al-Tzalam, and the like. Also, the remnant of the books of our forebears, the sages of Yemen, we find and see that they adhere to the words of the great ones mentioned above and to their opinions. And when you saw that we separated from the new Kabbalah, your anger burned against us, and in haughtiness of spirit you, the arrogant, smeared falsehood on us. And we asked you to teach us the way: how would the words of our rabbis, the new Kabbalists, agree with the words of our early rabbis mentioned above, and with the words of the Tannaim and the Amoraim. And your answer to us was in the manner of deception and taunts.**

Grammar:

- The paragraph is a chain of first-person plural past acts (פירשנו, ודבקנו, שאלנו); the reply of the other side is in the perfect (והיתה).
- ושאלנו אתכם ... איך יסכימו: the question is indirect (איך with the imperfect); the English keeps it as a report, 'how would ... agree'.
- וכראותכם ... חרה אפכם: כראותכם is the infinitive with כ, 'upon your seeing'; the tense comes from the main verb חרה, hence 'when you saw'.
- וברמות רוחא טפלתם עלינו שקר זדים: the Aramaic idiom ברמות רוחא is translated by its sense; the rest adapts Ps 119:69 (טפלו עלי שקר זדים), in which זדים, 'the arrogant', is the subject; here it names those addressed.

Note: The list of sources is kept in the order the author gives it. Midrash ha-Gadol is a title; Nur al-Tzalam is transliterated as printed (see apparatus).

Ancient Near East:

- Midrash ha-Gadol: a midrashic compilation on the Torah, preserved above all in Yemenite manuscripts; the author names it as 'found in Yemen in manuscript'.

Apparatus:

- Ps 119:69, embedded allusion (no quotation marks): טפלו עלי שקר זדים, adapted to טפלתם עלינו שקר זדים.
- Printed אלצלאם (3:4.41), transliterated as written 'al-Tzalam'; the likelier title is Nur al-Zulam, 'Light of the Darkness' (Hebrew Me'or ha-Afelah); 'al-Salam' would be spelled with ס.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:5

> ובפעם השלישית היתה תשובתכם כשאלת אחד מארבעה בנים מה העבודה הזאת לכם, לכם ולא לו, כאילו לא נצטוינו בתורה וידעת היום והשבות אל לבבך כי ה' הוא האלהים וכו' וכמה מקראות באו בתורה ובנביאים ובכתובים על זה וכל שכן בדברי רז"ל. גם חזרת להיות מכת מספרי לשון הרע וממקבליו באמרך שכבר יש עלינו כמה עדים שאנחנו מבזים את החכמים ולא נוכל להכחיש עוד וכו'. והן ידוע ומפורסם שאין מקבלין עדות אלא בפני בעל דין. ומן התורה אחד דיני ממונות ואחד דיני נפשות בדרישה וחקירה כמו שכ' הרמב"ם ז"ל בפרק ג' מהלכות עדות אבל אמרו חכמים כדי שלא תנעול דלת בפני לוין אין עדי ממון צריכים דרישה וחקירה וכו'. במה דברים אמורים בהודאות והלואות, מתנות ומכירות, אבל בדיני קנסות צריכים דרישה וחקירה, ואין צריך לומר במלקיות ובגלות, ובדין מרומה אף בדיני ממונות צריך דרישה וחקירה.

**And for the third time your answer was like the question of one of the four sons: "What is this worship to you? To you and not to him." As if we had not been commanded in the Torah, "And know this day and take it to your heart, that the LORD, He is God, etc." And many verses came in the Torah, in the Prophets and in the Writings on this, and all the more so in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory. You have also returned to be of the company of tellers of evil talk and of those who receive it, when you say that already there are several witnesses against us, that we despise the Sages and can no longer deny it, etc. And it is known and notorious that testimony is accepted only in the presence of the party to the suit. From the Torah, civil cases and capital cases alike require inquiry and examination, as the Rambam of blessed memory wrote in chapter 3 of the Laws of Testimony. But the Sages said, "So that you do not lock the door before borrowers, monetary witnesses do not require inquiry and examination, etc." In what matters is this said? In admissions and loans, gifts and sales. But in fines, inquiry and examination are required, and needless to say in lashes and exile, and in a case of deception, even in civil cases, inquiry and examination are required.**

Literal: and for the third time was your reply like the question of one of the four sons what the worship this to you to you and not to him as if not we were commanded in the Torah and know this day and take to your heart that the LORD He is God etc. And many verses came in the Torah and in the Prophets and in the Writings on this and all the more so in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory also you have returned to be of the company of the tellers of evil talk and of those who receive it when you say that already there are against us several witnesses that we despise (object marker) the Sages and cannot deny any longer etc. And indeed it is known and notorious that there is no accept testimony except in the presence of the party to the suit And from the Torah one of the laws of civil matters and one of the laws of capital cases in inquiry and examination as wrote the Rambam of blessed memory in chapter 3 of the Laws of Testimony But said the Sages so that not you lock the door before borrowers there is no witnesses of money need inquiry and examination etc. In what matters are said in admissions and loans gifts and sales But in the cases of fines require inquiry and examination and there is no need to say in lashes and in exile and in a case of deception even in the cases of civil requires inquiry and examination

Grammar:

- The Haggadah's wicked son asks 'What is this worship to you?' (מה העבודה הזאת לכם, Exod 12:26) and the Haggadah adds 'לכם ולא לו'; the author quotes both, and the English sets them in quotation marks as a quoted question.
- In 'וידעת היום והשבות אל לבבך' the verbs are second-person forms of Deut 4:39; 'כי ה' הוא האלהים' has no copula in Hebrew, so 'is God' supplies it.
- 'ומן התורה אחד דיני ממונות ואחד דיני נפשות בדרישה וחקירה' has no finite verb; אחד ... ואחד means 'both ... and', so civil and capital cases alike are subject to inquiry and examination; 'require' is supplied from 'צריכים' in the next sentences.
- 'אמרו חכמים' is an explicit quotation formula, so the words it introduces take double quotation marks; the author gives no source, and none is added. The quotation is closed after 'וכו'', because what follows ('במה דברים אמורים') carries no formula.
- 'במה דברים אמורים' is a fixed Mishnaic question: 'in what case is this said?' 'ואין צריך לומר' is 'needless to say', and its object is understood from the preceding clause.

Ancient Near East:

- The four sons: the four children of the Passover Haggadah. The question 'What is this service to you?' (Exod 12:26) is the wicked son's, as the Haggadah gives it.

Apparatus:

- Exod 12:26: 'מה העבודה הזאת לכם' (the wicked son of the Passover Haggadah); 'לכם ולא לו' is the Haggadah's addition.
- Deut 4:39: 'וידעת היום והשבת אל לבבך כי ה' הוא האלהים'; the printed text has והשבות; the author stops at וכו', and the verse continues beyond the words quoted.
- Wikisource base text (Q2): translated as it stands; flagged until the 1931 scan is collated.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:6

> ו) ובנדון דידן כולהו איתינהו ביה, ואיך מלאך לבך לקבל לשון הרע מאנשים סכלים ההולכים יחפים כמנודים לשמים, ולחשוב אותה לעדות גמורה, להחזיק את עמיתך בתורה ובמצות דאוריתא ודרבנן לאפיקורסים ומינים שהם מכלל אותם שמורידין ולא מעלין? וידוע הוא ומפורסם, כי זה הדור, דור שוא ושקר, והיא בנשיאי ישראל, וכל אחד מתכבד בקלון חברו ורבו אשר העמידו בקרו אורה זו תורה. ובמשימי לילות כימים ועבדי לתורה שלא תשתכח מישראל כפי יכולתם שפכתם בוז, ותשימו את לומדי התורה ומחזיקים בה נבזים ושפלים ככלי אין חפץ בו. וכל עושי רע טוב בעיניכם, ומכובד יותר מהם, ועל ידי דבות שקר שמתם לומדי תורה לשמצה בעיני כל רואיהם עד שבאו למדרגה פחותה מאד, שעמי הארץ משתבחים בעצמם לומר אשרינו מה טוב חלקנו וערבה שנתינו עד עלות השמש וכבוד ננחל יותר מאלה העומדים בבית ה' בלילות, לקיים מה שנאמר ואם בחקותי תמאסו, אם במלמדי חקותי תמאסו, כמו שכ הרמב"ם ז"ל בהל' תלמוד תורה.

**§6. And in our case all of them are in it, and how did your heart dare to accept evil talk from foolish men who walk barefoot, like men banned by heaven, and to consider it complete testimony, to hold your fellow in the Torah and in the commandments of Scriptural and rabbinic law as apikorsim and heretics, who are among those whom one lowers and does not raise? And it is known and notorious that this generation, a generation of vanity and falsehood, and it is among the princes of Israel, and each one takes pride in the disgrace of his fellow and of his teacher, whom they set up in their examination; 'orah' means Torah. And on those who make nights as days, and those who toil for the Torah, so that it not be forgotten from Israel according to their ability, you poured out contempt, and you made the students of the Torah and those who hold to it despised and lowly, like a vessel in which there is no delight. And all who do evil are good in your eyes, and more honored than them, and by means of false rumors you made the students of Torah a disgrace in the eyes of all who see them, until they came to a very low rank, that the ignorant boast of themselves, saying, "Happy are we, how good is our portion and pleasant our sleep until the rising of the sun, and we shall inherit honor more than those who stand in the house of the LORD at night"; to fulfill what was said, "And if you despise My statutes, if you despise those who teach My statutes," as the Rambam of blessed memory wrote in the Laws of the Study of Torah.**

Literal: §6. and in the case of our all of them are in it and how has filled-you your heart to accept the talk of evil from men foolish who walk barefoot like banned by heaven and to consider it as complete testimony to hold (object marker) your fellow in the Torah and in the commandments of Scriptural law and rabbinic as apikorsim and heretics who are among those whom one lowers and not raise And it is known and notorious that this generation a generation of vanity and falsehood and it is among the princes of Israel and each one takes pride in the disgrace of his fellow and his teacher whom they set up in their examination light this Torah And on-those-who make nights as days and those who work for the Torah so that not be forgotten from Israel according to their ability you poured out contempt and you made (object marker) the students of the Torah and those who hold to it despised and lowly like a vessel there-is-not delight in-it And all those who do evil good in your eyes and honored more than them and by means of rumors of falsehood you made the students of Torah a disgrace in the eyes of all who see them until they came to a rank low very that the people-of-the-land boast of themselves saying Happy are we how good our portion and pleasant our sleep until the rising of the sun and honor we shall inherit more than those who stand in the house of the LORD at night to fulfill what was said And-if in My statutes you despise if in those who teach My statutes you despise as wrote the Rambam of blessed memory in the Laws of the study of Torah

Grammar:

- The paragraph opens with an Aramaic sentence (Bavli Aramaic): 'ובנדון דידן כולהו איתינהו ביה' is 'and in our case all of them are in it'. Its only question is marked '?' after 'ולא מעלין'.
- 'ואיך מלאך לבך לקבל' is rhetorical and perfect: 'how did your heart dare to accept'; מלאך is מלא with the suffix ך (Esth 7:5).
- 'לאפיקורסים ומינים' is the object of 'להחזיק' with a double predicate: 'to hold him as apikorsim and heretics'.
- 'כי זה הדור, דור שוא ושקר' repeats 'דור' as an apposition: 'this generation, a generation of vanity and falsehood'.
- 'ובמשימי ... שפכתם בוז' puts the object first with ב ('on'): 'you poured out contempt on those who make nights as days'.
- The quotations are 'Happy are we' (the speech of the unlearned) and 'And if you despise My statutes' (Lev 26:15, the second clause not in the verse), introduced by 'לומר' and 'שנאמר'.

Apparatus:

- Lev 26:15: 'ואם בחקתי תמאסו'; the author writes בחקותי, and the second clause 'אם במלמדי חקותי תמאסו' is not in the verse.
- Ps 134:1: 'העומדים בבית ה' בלילות'.
- Hos 8:8: 'ככלי אין חפץ בו'; cf. Jer 22:28 'כלי אין חפץ בו'.
- Esth 8:16: 'אורה' (the saying 'אורה זו תורה' is the sages' explanation of it).
- Job 17:12: 'לילה ליום ישימו' (echoed in 'משימי לילות כימים').
- Job 12:21 and Ps 107:40: 'שופך בוז על ...' (echoed in 'שפכתם בוז').
- Mal 2:17: 'כל עשה רע טוב בעיני ה'' (echoed in 'וכל עושי רע טוב בעיניכם').
- Esth 7:5: 'אשר מלאו לבו' (echoed in 'מלאך לבך').
- Prov 3:24: 'וערבה שנתך' (echoed in 'וערבה שנתינו').
- 'בקרו' (3:6.58) is uncertain; see the token note.
- Wikisource base text (Q2): translated as it stands; flagged until the 1931 scan is collated.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:7

> ז) וז"ל המקובל בעל היכל הברכה, מצות עשה על הב"ד לדרוש ולחקור את העדים בשבע חקירות וכו' עוד יש בדיקות שהוא שאלות מה היה לבוש, עפר הארץ שהיה עומד עליה שחור או חול, או חמר, ואם כחשו זה לזה בטל העדות. משרשי המצוה הזאת הכלה הכלולה עולימתא שפירתא דלית בה עינין, הנהגת העולם הזה שיהא בחירה חפשית עיניו כיונים אונאה לבני נשא. ועינין דילה בהיכל זכות, עיני העדה, שדנין בידיעה על פי שנים עדים, תרין עטרין, והדעת הוא סוד עינים כנודע, ואור זה מתפשט בשבע בחינות וכ' ע"ש. ובמצות לא תלך רכיל כתב וז"ל, שלא להגיד לחברו, שכנגדו דבר עליו רע, שנאמר, לא תלך רכיל. ומדיני המצוה אף שמדבר אמת, ויש עון גדול בזה. וגם בכלל לאו זה שלא ידבר כגנות חברו אף אמת והוא כאילו כפר בעיקר וכו'. והאריך עוד בעונש המספר לשון הרע ובשכר הנשמר ממנו, יעו"ש.

**§7. And these are the words of the Kabbalist, the author of Heikhal ha-Berakhah: "A positive commandment on the court to inquire into and to examine the witnesses with seven inquiries, etc. There are also examinations, which are questions: what clothing he wore; the dust of the ground on which he stood, whether black, or sand, or clay; and if they contradict one another, the testimony is void. From the roots of this commandment: the included bride, the beautiful young maiden who has no eyes, the governance of this world, that there be free choice, whose eyes are like doves, a deception to the sons of man. Her eyes in the Palace of Merit: the eyes of the congregation, who judge with knowledge on the testimony of two witnesses, two crowns; and the Da'at is the secret of the eyes, as is known; and this light spreads in seven aspects, etc." See there. And concerning the commandment "You shall not go about as a talebearer," he wrote, and these are his words: " that one should not tell his fellow that his adversary has spoken evil about him, as it is said, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer.' And among the laws of the commandment: even though he speaks the truth, there is a great sin in this. And also within the scope of this prohibition: that one should not speak in disparagement of his fellow, even if true, and this is as if he denied the fundamental principle, etc." And he expanded further on the punishment of the one who tells slander and on the reward of the one who guards from it; see there.**

Grammar:

- The paragraph is two quotations. The first is introduced by וז"ל המקובל בעל היכל הברכה (3:7.2-3:7.6), 'and these are the words of the Kabbalist, the author of Heikhal ha-Berakhah', and runs to וכו' (3:7.87); the author's own ע"ש (3:7.88) stands outside it. The words עולימתא שפירתא דלית בה עינין, ועינין דילה, תרין עטרין and בני נשא are Aramaic and are rendered by sense. The text does not name their source, and none is added.
- מצות עשה על הב"ד לדרוש ולחקור: 'a positive commandment on the court to inquire and examine'. על with a noun reads 'incumbent upon'; the infinitives give the content of the commandment.
- ואם כחשו זה לזה בטל העדות: a conditional with a perfect verb; the result clause is בטל, 'is void'. The two witnesses are the subject of the conflict (כחשו).
- וז"ל followed by a name means 'and these are the words of X:', so the Kabbalist (3:7.3-3:7.6) is the speaker named by the formula and not part of the quotation. בעל + a book title is 'the author of'.
- אף שמדבר אמת: אף ש is 'even though'; the clause is a concession to the main clause ויש עון גדול בזה, 'there is a great sin in this'.
- The second quotation begins at כתב וז"ל (3:7.93-3:7.94) and ends at וכו' (3:7.129); the closing words והאריך עוד are the author's own report and take no quotation marks.

Note: The first quotation opens after the formula and the name of the speaker, and closes after "etc."; the author's ע"ש stands outside it. The second quotation has a Bible verse inside it, in single marks.

Ancient Near East:

- Heikhal ha-Berakhah ("Palace of Blessing") is a Kabbalistic commentary on the Torah by R. Yitzchak Yehudah Yechiel Safrin of Komarno; the author of Milchamot ha-Shem cites it here for its remarks on the commandments.

Apparatus:

- Wikisource transcription. The 1931 scan is not yet collated; Wikisource additions are translated as base text (decisions, Q2).
- Lev 19:16: 'לא תלך רכיל' (3:7.90-3:7.92 and 3:7.102-3:7.105). The quotation stops before בעמיך, so only the words on the page are translated.
- Song 5:12: 'עיניו כיונים', 'his eyes are like doves' (3:7.58-3:7.59), embedded in the Kabbalist's text.
- Deut 17:6: 'על פי שנים עדים', 'on the testimony of two witnesses' (3:7.71-3:7.74); cf. Deut 19:15.
- 3:7.121: printed כגנות; the likelier word is בגנות ('in disparagement of'), translated by the sense.

#### Milchamot ha-Shem 3:8

> ח) ובאזהרת לא תעמוד על דם רעך, כ' אפי' עמידה כל דהו. לא תראה בצערו של חברך שאחד מלבין פניו ואתה שותק, עמדו ולא ענו עוד, אלא תהיה מוחה בכל יכלתך במי שמבזה חברך, או מדבר עליו רכילות ולשון הרע, אתה לא תהיה שומע ושותק, אלא תאמר לו רשע עוכר ישראל, למה תדבר סרה על דמות יוצרנו ועל שכינת עוזינו שהיא היו"ד שבעמיך, ומסתלקת בעון זה. ולכך נסמכה זה לזה, לא תלך רכיל ותאמר כיון שאיני מדבר אשמע ואשתוק ונהנה במה שחברו רשע מדבר, גם זה השומע רשע גמור. ועובר על לא תעמוד על דם רעך. ואין לו חלק באלהי ישראל כששומע רשע מדבר סרה על צדיק, או לוחש מלחש בשקרים על חברו רק תכף תדחה אותו ותאמר לו רשע לך מעלי, איני שומע לך, כי אם הוא שומע ושותק, וכל שכן אם נהנה, סופו נידון באש לא נופח, ולא יזכה לעמוד במחיצת הצדיקים, כשומע, כעונה, כמדבר, כולם יספו מן העולם בזה ובבא עכ"ל.

**§8. And in the warning, "You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow," he wrote: "even standing by, to any degree. You shall not see your fellow's distress when one puts him to shame, and you are silent; they stood and answered no more. But you shall protest with all your power against him who disgraces your fellow, or speaks about him with talebearing and slander; you shall not be one who hears and is silent, but you shall say to him: 'Wicked one, troubler of Israel, why do you speak defiance against the likeness of our Maker, and against the Shekhinah of our strength, which is the yod in "among your people," and departs through this sin.' Therefore this was juxtaposed to that, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer,' and you might say: since I do not speak, I will listen and be silent, and take pleasure in what his fellow, a wicked man, speaks. This listener too is an utterly wicked person. And he transgresses 'You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow.' And he has no portion in the God of Israel when he hears a wicked one speak defiance against a righteous person, or whisper a whisper of lies about his fellow; rather, you shall immediately push him away and say to him: 'Wicked one, go away from me, I do not listen to you.' But if he hears and is silent, and all the more so if he takes pleasure, his end is to be judged in unblown fire, and he will not merit to stand in the company of the righteous, as listener, as answerer, as speaker. All of them shall perish from the world in this one, and in the world to come." Thus far his words.**
